translation.quality: The source edition describes its English as machine-assisted and post-edited and cautions that errors may remain. These passages were extracted from the al-Tabari-labeled sections; they have not been independently checked against the Arabic.

x: God Almighty says:
h
The command of God has come

and is near to you, O people, so do not hasten its occurrence. Then the people of interpretation differed about the matter that God informed His servants of its coming and its closeness to them, what it is, and what it is?
Some of them said: It is His obligations and rulings.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
The command of God has come
, so do not hasten it, he said: The rulings, the limits, and the obligations.

x: Others said: Rather, this is a threat from God to the people who associate partners with Him. He informed them that the Hour has drawn near, and that their punishment has come to an end, so it has drawn near.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: When this verse was revealed, meaning,
h
The command of God has come
, so do not hasten it, some hypocrites said to one another: This man claims that
h
the command of God has come

, so refrain from some of what you were doing until you see what will happen. When they saw that nothing was coming down, they said: We do not see anything. Then the verse was revealed: The reckoning of the people has drawn near, while they are in heedlessness turning away. They said: This man also claims something similar. When they saw that nothing was coming down, they said: We do not see anything coming down. Then the verse was revealed: “And if We delay the punishment from them for a limited term, they will surely say, ‘What is holding it back?’ Unquestionably, the Day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them, and that which they used to ridicule will encompass them.”

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Hafs, who said:
m: When
h
The command of God has come
was revealed, they raised their heads, and So do not hasten it was revealed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wazeh told us: Abu Bakr bin Shuaib told us:
m: I heard Abu Sadiq reciting: O My servants,
h
the command of God has come

, so do not hasten it. The first of the two opinions on this, in my opinion, is the most correct opinion, which says: It is a threat from God to the disbelievers in Him and His Messenger, and an announcement from Him to them of the approaching punishment and destruction for them. This is because He followed that with His saying,
h
Glory be to Him and He is exalted above what they associate with Him

. This indicates His rebuke of the polytheists and His threat to them. Moreover, it has not reached us that any of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hastened the obligatory duties before they were imposed upon them, so it was said to them because of that: The obligatory duties of God have come to you, so do not hasten them. As for those polytheists who hastened the punishment, they were many. And His saying,
h
Glory be to Him

, and He is exalted above what they associate with Him. God Almighty says, glorifying God and exalting Him above the polytheism that the Quraysh and those of the Arabs who were like them and who believed in it. The reciters differed in their reading of the Almighty’s saying: About what they associate. The people of Medina, some of the Basrans and the Kufians read it as About what they associate with the letter ya to inform about the people of disbelief in God, and to direct the address with haste to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They also read the second with the letter ya. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the letter ta to direct the address with His saying Do not hasten it to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the polytheists. Reading with the letter ta in both letters as an address to the polytheists is more correct because of the interpretation that I have explained, that this is a threat from God to the polytheists. He began the beginning of the verse with threatening them, and concluded the end of it with the reprehensibility of their action, and the enormity of their disbelief as an address to them.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of the Almighty’s saying: About what they associate.

The people of Medina, some of the Basrans and the Kufians read it as About what they associate with the letter ya to inform about the people of disbelief in God, and to direct the address with haste to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with the letter ta to direct the address with His saying Do not hasten it to the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and with His saying, may God bless him and grant him peace, to the polytheists.

x: The reciters differed in reading the phrase yanzil al-malaikah He sends down the angels. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa read it as yanzil al-malaikah with a ya' and a shaddah on the zay and the accusative of the angels, meaning: God sends down the angels with the spirit.
Some of the Basrans and some of the Meccans read it as yanzil al-malaikah with a ya' and a light zay and the accusative of the angels.

c: It was narrated from some of the Kufians
m: that he used to read it tanzil al-malaikah with a ta' and a shaddah on the zay and the angels in the nominative. There was a difference of opinion about that from him.

c: It was narrated from him
m: that he agreed with the rest of the reciters of his country. The most correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read yanzil al-mala’ikah meaning: God sends down angels. I chose that because God is the one who sends down His angels with His revelation to His messengers, so adding the action of that to Him is more appropriate and more deserving. I chose yanzil with emphasis rather than alleviation, because He, the Most High, used to send down revelation to those He sent down, little by little. And the emphasis with it, since that was its meaning, is more appropriate than the alleviation. The interpretation of the statement is: God sends down His angels with that by which the truth is revived and falsehood is destroyed by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants meaning upon whomever He wills of His messengers that they warn. The first is in the accusative case, in response to the spirit, and the second is in the accusative case by warn. The meaning of the statement is: God sends down the angels with the spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants, that they warn My servants of My wrath over their disbelief in Me and their association of partners in taking gods and idols with Me, for there is no god but Me. He says: Divinity is not appropriate except for Me, and it is not appropriate for anything to be worshipped other than Me. So fear Me means: So beware of Me by performing My obligations, singling out worship and devoting Your Lordship to Me, for that is your salvation from destruction. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
The angels descend with the spirit
, meaning: with revelation.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants
, he says: He sends down the angels...

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement, with the spirit of His command, that no angel descends except with a spirit with him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, he said:
m: Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: His statement,
h
He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command
, he said: No angel descends except with a spirit.
h
He sends down the angels with the spirit by His command

upon whomever He wills of His servants, he said: By prophethood. Ibn Jurayj said: And I heard that the spirit was created from the angels and the spirit descended with it (And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord).

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas,
m: regarding His statement:
h
He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants

, [saying], ‘Warn that there is no god except Me, so fear Me.’ He said: Every word that our Lord speaks is a spirit from Him And thus We have revealed to you a spirit by Our command… to His statement Unquestionably, to God do all matters return.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
He sends down the angels with the Spirit by His command
means: He sends down mercy and revelation by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants and He chooses from among them messengers.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The angels send down the spirit by His command upon whomever He wills of His servants. He said: With revelation and mercy. As for his saying,
h
Warn that there is no god but Me
, so fear Me, we have explained its meaning. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Warn that there is no god but Me
, so fear Me, God only sent the messengers so that God alone would be worshipped, His command would be obeyed, and His wrath would be avoided.

It was narrated from him that he agreed with the rest of the reciters of his country.
The most correct reading in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who read yanzil al-mala’ikah meaning: God sends down angels.

x: God Almighty says, defining His creation as His proof against them in His Oneness, and that divinity is only suitable for Him: Your Lord, O people, created the heavens and the earth with justice, and He is the Truth, the One Who created them. No partner shared with Him in creating and bringing them into existence, nor did He assist Him in this. So how could He have a partner? Exalted is He above what they associate with Him. God Almighty says: Your Lord, O people, is exalted above your polytheism and your calling upon a god other than Him. He is exalted above having a likeness, partner, or supporter, because no god can be except He who creates and brings into existence with His power the likes of the heavens and the earth, and invents bodies and brings them into existence from nothing. This is not within the power of anyone except God, the One, the Subduer, to whom worship is only due, and divinity is only suitable for Him.

God the Almighty says: And among His proofs against you, O people, is that He created man from a sperm-drop, then He brought forth from despised water an amazing creation. He transformed him, creating him at times after creating him in three layers of darkness. Then He brought him out into the light of this world after his creation was complete and He breathed the spirit into him, then He nourished him and provided him with sustenance and made him grow, until when he stood on his feet, he disbelieved in the favor of his Lord, denied his Manager, and worshipped He who can neither harm nor benefit, and argued with his God, saying: (Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed?) and he forgot the One who created him, so He proportioned him as a perfect creation from despised water. What is meant by clear is that he clarifies his contention with speech, and argues with his tongue, and that is his clarification. And what is meant by man is all people. He brought him out with the wording of one, which is in the meaning of all.

God Almighty says: And among His proofs against you, O people, is what He created for you of the livestock, and made them subservient to you, and made for you from their wool and fur and hair clothing with which to keep you warm, and benefits from their milk, and their backs on which you ride. And from them you eat. He says: And from the livestock is that which you eat its meat, such as camels, cows, sheep, and all other things whose meat is eaten. And the word ma was omitted from the speech because of the indication of who on it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me.
m: Al-Muthanna said: He told us. Ibn Dawud said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us. He said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement,
h
And the grazing livestock He has created for you
; in them is warmth, meaning: clothing.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And the grazing livestock He has created for you
; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. He means by warmth: the clothes, and the benefits: what they benefit from of food and drink.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty For you therein is warmth, he said: Woven clothing, and from it is riding, milk, and meat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Therein is warmth for you, woven clothing, and benefits: riding, meat, and milk.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Therein is warmth for you and many benefits
, he said: the offspring of every animal.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Israel told us
m: with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And the grazing livestock He has created for you
; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, meaning: In them is clothing, benefit, and sustenance for you.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
And the grazing livestock He has created for you
; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. He said: They are benefits and food.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And the grazing livestock He has created for you
; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, he said: The warmth of the blankets that God made from them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: It reached me on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And the grazing livestock He has created for you
; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits. He said: Their offspring, riding, milk, and meat.

x: God Almighty says: And there is adornment for you in them when you bring them home at night and when you send them out to pasture.

God the Almighty says: And for you in these livestock and cattle which He created for you is beauty when you bring them back to pasture meaning: you bring them back in the evening from their pastures to their resting places and homes to which they return, and that is why the place is called: the pasture, because they return to it in the evening, so they return to it, and it is said from it: So-and-so rested his livestock, so he rests them.

i: And His saying and when you send them out to pasture means: and at the time of your taking them out in the morning from their resting places to their pastures, and it is said from it: So-and-so sent his livestock out, he sends them out to pasture in the morning, and the livestock is sent out to pasture: if it goes out to pasture to pasture, so pasturing is in the morning, and resting is in the evening, and from it the saying of the poet:
x: As if the remains of donkeys were on their backs, the bear was trotting over the desert while it was wandering And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And for you therein is beauty when you bring them back home and when you send them out to pasture. That is most amazing when they rest, with large udders and long humps, and when you send them out to pasture, when they are sent out to graze.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And there is beauty for you in them when you bring them back home and when you send them out to pasture. He said: When they go out to pasture, their humps are at their largest and their udders are at their best. His statement,
h
And they carry your burdens to a land you could not have reached except with great difficulty
, means: And these livestock carry your burdens to another land you could not have reached except with great effort from yourselves and great hardship.

c: As Ahmad bin Ishaq told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: h
And your burdens are carried to a land which you could not have reached except with great difficulty
. He said: If you had taken it upon yourself, you would not have reached it except with great effort.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: To a country you could not have reached except with great difficulty. He said: If you were tasked with it, you would not have reached it except with great difficulty.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hammani told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: To a land which you could not have reached except with great difficulty. He said: The land is Mecca.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, except with great difficulty, he said: Hardship for you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And your burdens are carried to a land which you could not have reached except with great difficulty
, he said: with great effort.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar. The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of the regions read it with a kasra on the sheen, except with difficulty, except for Abu Jaʿfar al-Qariʿ, for...

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Abu Saeed al-Razi told me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar,
m: the reciter of Medina, that he used to recite You were not able to attain it except with difficulty with an open shin, and he used to say: Verily, difficulty means difficulty of the soul. Ibn Abi Hammad said: Muʿadh al-Hara’ used to say: It is a dialect, the Arabs say Bishaq and Bishaq, and Barq and Barq. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is what the readers of the countries do, which is to break the shin, due to the consensus of the authoritative readers on it, and what contradicts it is an anomaly. This verse may be recited with the shin broken or open, and that is what the poet said: And a man with camels who runs and thinks they are his, my brother, is a pimp who splits them and is persistent. And from its splitting with the kasra and the fatha, and likewise the saying of Al-Ajjaj: He became dragged to the point of being torn And shaqā with the fathah and the kasr, and what he means by his saying yawāzī shaqān: he suffers hardship, and some of the Arabists would go with the fathah to the source of shaqāt alayhi ashqān, and with the kasr to the noun. It may be possible that those who read with the kasr meant except with a deficiency in strength, and the loss of some of it until he does not reach it except after its deficiency, so its meaning in that case would be: you would not have reached it except with the difficulty of your strength, and the loss of its other lip, and it is narrated from the Arabs: take this shaq: for the shaqah of the sheep with the kasr. As for shaqāt alayhi ashqān, nothing has been narrated in it except the accusative. And His saying, Indeed, your Lord is Most Kind and Most Merciful, the Most High says: Indeed, your Lord, O people, is Most Kind and Most Merciful to you. Out of His mercy to you, He created for you livestock for your benefit and interests, and He created the heavens and the earth as evidence for you of the oneness of your Lord and knowledge of your God, so that you may thank Him for His blessings upon you, and He may increase you from His grace.

This verse may be recited with the shin broken or open, and that is what the poet said: And a man with camels who runs and thinks they are his, my brother, is a pimp who splits them and is persistent.

It may be possible that those who read with the kasr meant except with a deficiency in strength, and the loss of some of it until he does not reach it except after its deficiency, so its meaning in that case would be: you would not have reached it except with the difficulty of your strength, and the loss of its other lip, and it is narrated from the Arabs: take this shaq: for the shaqah of the sheep with the kasr.

x: God Almighty says: And He created horses, mules, and donkeys for you also that you may ride them and as an adornment. He says: And He made them for you as an adornment with which you adorn yourselves, along with the hypocrites that are in them for you, for riding and other things. The horses and mules are placed in the accusative case in apposition to the ha’ and the alif in His statement
h
He created them

. The adornment is placed in the accusative case by an implied verb as I explained. If there was no waw with it, the statement would have been for you to ride them as an adornment. It would have been placed in the accusative case by the verb that preceded it, to which it is connected. However, the entry of the waw indicates that there is a pronoun for a verb with it, and that it is disconnected from the verb that preceded it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: That you may ride them and as an adornment. He said: He made them for you to ride, and He made them an adornment for you.

x: Some scholars believed that this verse indicates the prohibition of eating horse meat.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Damrah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride, he said: This is for riding. And the grazing livestock - He has created them for you; in them is warmth, he said: This is for eating.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Hisham al-Dastawai told us, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Katheer told us, on the authority of the client of Nafi’ ibn Alqamah,
m: that Ibn Abbas disliked the meat of horses, mules, and donkeys, and he used to say: God said, And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. So this is for eating. And horses, mules, and donkeys that you may ride. So this is for riding.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he was asked about horse meat, and he disliked it and recited this: And horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride... the verse.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Qais bin Al-Rabi’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he was asked about horse meat, so he said: Read the one before it: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. “And horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride and as an adornment.” So he made this for eating, and this for riding.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Ghania told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Hakam:
m: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits, and from them you eat. So he made eating from it, then he recited until he reached and horses, mules, and donkeys that you may ride. He said: He did not make eating in them for you. He said: Al-Hakam used to say that horses, mules, and donkeys are forbidden in the Book of God.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Ibn Abi Ghaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, he said:
m: Horse meat is forbidden in the Book of God, then he recited: And the grazing livestock He has created for you; in them is warmth and [numerous] benefits ... to His saying: that you may ride them.

x: A group other than them from the people of knowledge disagreed with them in this interpretation, and they saw that it does not indicate the prohibition of anything, and that God, may He be glorified and praised, only made His servants aware of this verse and the rest of what is in the beginning of this surah as a blessing upon them and alerted them to His arguments against them, and His evidence for His Oneness, and the error of the actions of those who associate partners with Him from the polytheists.
Some people mentioned that there is nothing wrong with eating horse meat.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad,
m: that he ate horse meat.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Al-Aswad,
m: something similar.

c: Ahmad told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: Our companions slaughtered a horse in the desert and ate from it, and they saw no harm in it. Surat al-Nahl 16:8 And horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride and as adornment. And He creates that which you do not know. The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is what the proponents of the second statement said, and that is because if there was an indication in the words of God Almighty, that you may ride them, that they are not suitable for eating, since they are for riding, then there would be an indication in His words, in them is warmth and [other] benefits, and from them you eat, that they are not suitable, since they are for eating and the warmth is for riding. And in the consensus of all that riding what God Almighty said, and from them you eat, is permissible and lawful, not forbidden, there is clear evidence that eating what He said, that you may ride them, is permissible and lawful, not forbidden, except in what is explicitly forbidden or is indicated as forbidden by a Book or revelation to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for this verse, eating nothing is forbidden. It was placed to indicate the prohibition of the meat of domesticated donkeys by revelation to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and of mules, as we have explained in our book, The Book of Foods, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, since this place was not among the places to explain the prohibition of that, but we mentioned what we mentioned to indicate that there is no basis for the statement of those who used this verse as evidence for the prohibition of horse meat.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abdul Karim, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Jabir, he said:
m: We used to eat horse meat during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: What about mules? He said: As for mules, no. And His statement:
h
And He creates what you do not know

. God Almighty says: And your Lord creates, along with His creation of these things that He mentioned to you, what you do not know, of what He has prepared in Paradise for its people, and in Hell for its people, of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived.

evidence.text: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he was asked about horse meat, and he disliked it and recited this: And horses, mules, and donkeys for you to ride... the verse.

x: God Almighty says: And upon God, O people, is the explanation of the path of truth to you. So whoever is guided, it is for the benefit of himself, and whoever goes astray only goes astray to his own detriment.

i: The path is the road, and the purpose of the path is the straight path that has no crookedness in it, as the rajaz poet said:
x: He turned away from the straight path.
And His statement:
h
And among them is some that are crooked

means, the Most High said: And among the paths is some that are crooked and deviate from the straight path. So the intended path is Islam, and the crooked path is Judaism, Christianity, and other disbelieving religions, all of which are crooked and deviate from the straight path and its intended path, except for the Muslim Hanafi school. And it was said:
h
And among them is some that are crooked

, because the path is both feminine and masculine, so it was made feminine in this place. And some of them used to say: And it was said: And among them, because even though the word path is one word, its meaning is plural. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And upon God is the direction of the way
, he said: the explanation.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told us: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And upon God is the direction of the way
, meaning: It is upon God to clarify guidance and misguidance.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And upon God is the determination of the way he said: The path of truth is upon God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And upon God is the direction of the way
, meaning: upon God is the explanation, the explanation of what is permissible and what is forbidden, and what is obedience to Him and what is disobedience to Him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement:
h
And upon God is the direction of the way
, he said: The way is the path of guidance.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And upon God is the direction of the path. He said: Its illumination.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And upon God is the direction of the way
, he said: Upon God is the explanation, He explains guidance from misguidance, and He explains the path that has diverged from His paths, and some of it is unjust.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them are some that are crooked: meaning among the paths, the paths of Satan. And in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: And among you are some that are crooked. And if God had willed, He would have guided you all.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And among them is one who is unjust. He said in the wording of Ibn Masoud: And among you is one who is unjust.

c: Muhammad bin Masoud told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And some of them are crooked, meaning: the scattered paths.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, And among them are those who are unjust, he said: the different desires.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And among them are those that deviate from His path, meaning: the paths that diverged from His path.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: And among them are the deviant ones are the paths that diverge from His path.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: And some of them are deviating, he said: Some of the paths deviate from the truth. He said: God said: And do not follow paths, for they will separate you from His path. And His statement,
h
And if He had willed

, He would have guided you all, means: And if God had willed, He would have been kind to all of you, O people, with His guidance, so that you would have been guided, and would have adhered to the straight path, and would not have deviated from it, so that you would have scattered along unjust paths away from the truth.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And if He had willed

, He could have guided you all, he said: If He had willed, He could have guided you all to the path, which is the truth, and he recited: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together... the verse, and he recited: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance... the verse.

evidence.text: And in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud: And among you are some that are crooked.

x: God the Almighty says: And He who has bestowed these blessings upon you, and created for you livestock, horses, and all other animals for your benefits and interests, is the Lord who sent down water from the sky, meaning: rain for you from that water, a drink that you drink, and from it the drink of your trees, and the life of your plants and their vegetation. In it you graze He says: In the trees that grow from the water that was sent down from the sky you graze, meaning you graze, it is said from it: Asama so-and-so made his camels yasimaha yasamaha, if he made them graze, and also sawmaha yasumaha, and samat hi: if they grazed, so they are sawma, and they are grazing camels. And from this it is said of the livestock released in the wilderness and elsewhere for grazing samamah.

Some of them have directed the meaning of sawma in the sale to it being from this, and that it is the going of each of the two parties to the sale in what is due to him of an increase in price and its decrease, just as the grazing livestock go wherever they want, from their pastures, and from this is the saying of al-A’sha: The people walked with the pillars to the pasture, and the guide became tired. Where is the path? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr Ibn Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: h
And from it are trees in which you graze
. He said: You graze.

c: Ahmad bin Suhayl Al-Wasiti told us: Qara bin Issa told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Arabi, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: In it you will graze, he said: You will pasture.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: They graze.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And from it are trees in which you graze their livestock and goats
, meaning: trees in which they graze their livestock and goats.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: In it you will pasture he said: you will graze.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: They will graze in it.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement, you will graze your livestock, he said: you will graze your livestock.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Talha bin Abi Talha Al-Qanad, who said:
m: I heard Abdullah bin Abdul Rahman bin Abza say: They are shepherds in it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
A tree in which you graze
means: you graze.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: They graze.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
A tree in which you graze
, he said: You graze.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement:
h
And from it are trees in which you graze
, he said: You graze. He said: The flock is the herd. And the poet said: Like Ibn Buza’ah or someone like him, it is better for you, Ibn Masima Al-Ajmal He said: O son of the camel herder.

x: God Almighty says: Your Lord causes to grow for you, by the water which He has sent down for you from the sky, your crops, your olives, your palm trees, your grapes, and of all the fruits: meaning, of all the fruits other than that, as provisions for you, sustenance, food, and fruits, as a blessing from Him to you and a favor, and an argument against whoever among you disbelieves in Him. Indeed in that is a sign. God Almighty says: Indeed in God’s bringing forth from the sky what He has described for you is a sign: meaning, a clear indication and a clear sign: for a people who reflect. He says: for a people who consider God’s admonitions and reflect on His arguments, so they remember and turn back.

God Almighty says: And among the blessings upon you, O people, in addition to the ones He mentioned before, is that He has subjected to you the night and the day, alternating between them. This is for your management of your livelihood, and this is for your dwelling in it, and the sun and the moon to know the times of your times, your months and your years, and the improvement of your livelihood. And the stars are subjected to you by God’s command, running in their orbits so that you may be guided by them in the darkness of the land and the sea. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reason. God Almighty says: Indeed in God’s subjecting of that to what He has subjected it to are clear indications for a people who understand God’s proofs, and understand His warning to them.
He, may His praise be glorified, means by His saying,
h
And what He has created for you
, and He has subjected to you what He has created: meaning what He created for you on the earth in its various colors, from animals and fruits.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And what He has created for you on the earth
, meaning:
h
And what He has created for you
of different colors of animals, trees, and fruits, are blessings from God that are manifest, so be grateful for them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Of the animals, trees, and fruits. And his statement mukhtalifan is in the accusative case because his statement and what is in the accusative case with the meaning that I described. And if that is the case, then mukhtalifan alwanuhu must be a state of what, and the predicate below it is complete. And if what was not in the accusative case, and the speech was initiated by his statement and what He created for you, then there would be nothing in mukhtalifan except the nominative case, because what would then become the subject of what.

x: God Almighty says: And He who did these actions to you, and bestowed upon you, O people, these blessings: He who subjected to you the sea, which is every river, whether its water is salty or fresh, that you may eat from it tender meat, which is the fish that is caught from it, and extract from it ornaments that you may wear, which are pearls and coral.

c: Al-Muthanna also told me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: Hisham told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And it is He who has subjected the sea that you may eat from it tender meat
, he said: from both of them, and extract from it ornaments which you wear, he said: these are pearls.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: That you may eat tender meat from it, meaning the whales of the sea.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Hammad told us, on the authority of Yahya, he said: Ismail bin Abdul Malik told us, he said:
m: A man came to Abu Jaʿfar and said: Is there any charity on women’s jewelry? He said: No, it is as God Almighty said: Ornament which you wear and see the ships meaning: the ships in which they ply and it is the plural of makhrah.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his saying late ones.
Some of them said: late ones means late ones.
Who said that?

c: Amr bin Musa Al-Qazzaz told us: Abdul-Warith told us: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you see the ships sailing through it
, he said: The ships sailing through it.

x: Others said about that, what:

c: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad told us: Muhammad ibn Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Asamm, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you see the ships moving forward in it
, he said: What is taken from the right and left of the ship from the water is the moving forward.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Makin, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And you see the ships moving through it
, he said: It is the ship moving through the water like this, meaning it splits it.

x: Others said about it: Muhammad bin Amr told me:

c: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And you see the ships plowing through it. He said: The winds plow the ships, and the wind does not plow the ships except the great ships.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that Al-Harith said in his hadith: And the winds do not plow ships.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement mawakhir he said: the wind blows.

x: Others said about it: Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And you see the ships moving forward therein sailing with one wind, coming and going.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: It flows forward and backward with one wind.

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, he said:
m: I heard Al-Hasan: And you see the ship moving forward and backward with one wind. He said: Coming and going forward with one wind. And makhr in the speech of the Arabs is the sound of the wind blowing, when its blowing is strong. In this context, it is the sound of the ship moving with the wind when it is strong and the water splits it at that time on its front. It is said from this: The ship moved forward, moving forward, and it is makhra. And it is said: The wind moved forward and moved forward, if you look from where it is blowing and listen to the sound of its blowing. From this is the saying of Wasil, the freed slave of Ibn Uyaynah: It was said: If one of you wants to urinate, let him move forward with the wind, meaning by that: let him look from where it is blowing and turn his back so that the urine does not come back on him and return to him. And His saying:
h
And that you may seek of His bounty
, God Almighty says: And that you may spend your time seeking your livelihood through trade, He has subjected it to you.

c: As Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And that you may seek of His bounty

. He said: Trade on land and sea. And His saying: And perhaps you will be grateful means: And to thank your Lord for what He has bestowed upon you of that, He has subjected to you what He has subjected to of these things that He has enumerated in these verses.

x: God the Almighty says: And among His blessings upon you, O people, is that He has placed firm mountains on the earth. This is the plural of rasiyah, which are the fixed mountains on the earth. And His statement, lest it should shake with you, means: that it should not shake with you. This is like His statement, God makes clear to you, lest you go astray, and the meaning is: that you should not go astray. This is because He, the Most High, has anchored the earth with mountains so that His creation on its surface would not shake. Rather, it was a table before it was anchored.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Qais bin Abbad,
m: that when God, the Blessed and Exalted, created the earth, it began to sway. The angels said: This does not have anyone on its back. So it became morning and its mountains were fixed.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abdullah bin Habib, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, who said:
m: When God created the earth, it trembled and said: O Lord, will You make the children of Adam commit sins and make me commit evil? He said: So God placed upon it mountains that you see and that you do not see, and its resting place was like swaying flesh. Al-Maid means turmoil and toppling. It is said: The ship swayed, swaying, if it tipped over with its people and tilted. And from this comes the dizziness that befalls a seafarer, which is vertigo. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: That it shakes with you means that it overturns you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And He has cast into the earth firm mountains

, lest it should shift with you, he said: The mountains, lest it should shift with you. Qatada said: I heard al-Hasan say: When the earth was created, it was about to shift, so they said: This is not stable for anyone to rest on its back. Then they woke up and found that the mountains had been created, and the angels did not know from what the mountains had been created. And his saying: And rivers means: And He made rivers in it, so He connected the rivers to the mountains, and He does in them what I do in the mountains, since the meaning of the speech and what is intended by it was understood, and that is similar to the saying of the rajaz poet: You hear images in their bellies, and in their hands there is emptiness and desolation. Dryness: so he connected with dryness to the sound, and dryness is not heard, since what was meant by it was understood, and that its meaning is that you see dryness in the hands. And His saying: And paths is the plural of path, just as roads is the plural of road. The meaning of the statement is: And He made for you, O people, paths and roads on the earth that you may take, and travel in them for your needs and to seek your livelihood, out of mercy for you, and as a blessing from Him to you. If He had blinded you to them, you would have perished in error and confusion. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his saying paths: meaning roads.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: paths he said:
m: roads. And His saying:
h
Perhaps you will be guided
means: So that you may be guided by these paths that He has made for you on earth to the places you intend and the locations you want, so that you do not go astray and become confused.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of the signs.

He meant by them the landmarks of the roads during the day. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And signs,
h
and by the stars they are guided
He means by the signs: the landmarks of the roads during the day,
h
and by the stars they are guided
at night.
Others said: He meant the stars.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: And signs,
h
and by the stars they are guided
. He said: Some of them are signs, and some of them are guided by them.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And signs,
h
and by the stars they are guided
. He said: Some of them are signs, and some of them are what guides.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Qubaysah told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: the same. Al-Muthanna said, he said:

c: Ishaq told us,
m: Qubaysah differed from Wakee’ in the chain of transmission.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And signs,
h
and by the stars they are guided

, and the signs are the stars, and God, the Blessed and Exalted, created these stars for three reasons: He made them an adornment for the sky, He made them a means of guidance, and He made them a means of stoning the devils. So whoever deals with them other than that has lost his vision, missed his share, wasted his portion, and assumed what he has no knowledge of.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And signs he said: the stars.

x: Others said: He meant the mountains.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Kalbi:
m: And signs he said: the mountains. The most correct of the sayings in this regard is to say: God Almighty mentioned a number of His blessings upon His servants, His favor upon them by what He made for them of signs by which they are guided in their paths and roads that they travel, and He did not specify some signs over others. So every sign by which people find their ways and the paths of their paths is included in His saying and signs. The paved roads: the trodden ones, a sign for the intended direction, and the mountains are signs by which one is guided to the intended path, and so are the stars at night. However, what is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse is that the signs are from the evidence of the day, since God had separated from them the evidence of the night by His saying:
h
And by the stars they are guided

. And since that is more similar and more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, then it is necessary to say in this regard what Ibn Abbas said in the report that we narrated from Atiyyah from him, which is that the signs are the landmarks of the roads and their indications by which one is guided to the straight path during the day, and that the star by which one is guided at night is Capricorn and Farqadaan, because they have Guidance travel without other stars. The interpretation of the words then is: And He has made, O people, signs by which you may be guided during the day on your paths in your journeys, and stars by which you may be guided at night on your ways.

x: God Almighty says: Is He who creates like he who does not create? Then will you not be reminded?

God the Almighty says to the idol worshippers: Is He who creates these wondrous creations which We have enumerated for you and bestows upon you these great blessings like He who does not create anything, nor bestows upon you a small or great blessing? He says: Do you associate this with the worship of this? He makes them aware of the greatness of their ignorance, their poor view of themselves, and their lack of gratitude to the One who bestowed upon them the blessings which He has enumerated for them, which no one else can count. He, the Most High, said to them, rebuking them: Do you not remember? O people? He says: Do you not remember the blessings of God upon you, and the greatness of His power and ability to do whatever He wills, and the weakness, incapacity, and humiliation of your idols, and that they do not bring benefit to themselves, nor ward off harm from themselves? So you will recognize the error of what you are doing in worshipping them and acknowledging their divinity.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: Is He who creates like he who does not create? So will you not be reminded? God is the Creator, the Provider, and these idols that are worshipped instead of God create, but do not create anything, and do not possess any harm or benefit for their people. God said: So will you not be reminded? It was said that like he who does not create is the idol and the statue, and of is specifically for those with discernment, so it was made in this place for others to distinguish, since it occurred in detail between he who creates and he who does not create. It is narrated from the Arabs: The rider and his camel were confused for me, so I did not know who was this and who was that, since they were brought together, and one of them is a human being, and both of them were good. And from this is the statement of God Almighty And among them are those who walk on their bellies, and among them are those who walk on two legs, and among them are those who walk on four. And His saying,
h
And if you should count the favors of God

, you could not enumerate them, you would not be able to express gratitude for them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, the Most High says: Indeed, God is Forgiving of what you have been negligent in expressing gratitude for some of that if you repent and return to His obedience and following what pleases Him. He is Merciful to you, lest He punish you for it after you have returned to Him and repented.

x: God Almighty says: And God knows what you conceal and what you declare.

God the Almighty says: And God, who is your God, O people, knows what you conceal in your hearts and what you hide from others, what you reveal with your tongues and limbs, and what you declare with your tongues, limbs and actions, and He is the one who records all of that against you, until He rewards you for it on the Day of Resurrection, the good among you for his good, and the evil among you for his evil, and He will question you about what you were thankful for in this world for His blessings which He bestowed upon you therein, which you have counted and which you have not counted. And His statement:
h
And those they invoke besides God do not create anything

, and they are themselves created. God the Almighty says: And your idols which you invoke besides God, O people, are gods that do not create anything and they are created, so how can there be a god that which was created and managed, and does not possess for itself benefit or harm.

The Almighty says to these polytheists from Quraysh 106:And those whom you call upon besides God, O people, are dead, not alive. And He, the Most High, made them dead, not alive, since there were no souls in them.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Dead, not alive, and they do not perceive when they will be resurrected, and they are these idols that are worshipped instead of God, dead, with no souls in them, and they do not possess any harm or benefit for their people. And there are two views regarding the raising of the dead: one of them is that it is report for those, and the other is a new beginning. And his statement, and they do not perceive, he says: And your idols that you call upon instead of God do not know when they will be resurrected. And it was said: What is meant by that are the disbelievers, that they do not know when they will be resurrected.

x: God Almighty says: Your deity who deserves your worship and obedience to Him alone, without all other things, is one deity, because worship is only appropriate for Him, so single out obedience to Him, and sincerely worship Him, and do not make any partner with Him other than Him.
h
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter

, their hearts are in denial. God Almighty says: Those who do not believe in God’s promise and threat, and do not acknowledge the return to Him after death, their hearts are in denial. God Almighty says: Denouncing what has been reduced to them of God’s power and greatness, and His beautiful blessings upon them, and that worship is only appropriate for Him, and that divinity is not for anything other than Him. He says: They are too arrogant to single out God in divinity, and to acknowledge His oneness, following what their ancestors did in the past of associating partners with God.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Those who do not believe in the Hereafter
, their hearts are in denial, is about this hadith that has passed, and they are arrogant about it.

x: He, the Most High, means by His statement:
h
There is no doubt that God knows what these polytheists conceal of their denial of the report that we mentioned in this surah

, and their belief in our denial of our saying to them: Your God is one God, and their arrogance towards God, and what they declare of their disbelief in God and their slander against Him. He does not love the arrogant. He says: God does not love those who are arrogant towards Him, that they make Him One and reject the gods and rivals besides Him.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us: Jaafar bin Awn told us: Misa’ar told us, on the authority of a man,
m: that Al-Hasan bin Ali used to sit with the poor, then say, He does not love the arrogant.

x: God Almighty says: And when it is said to those who do not believe in the Hereafter from among the polytheists, What has your Lord sent down? “What has your Lord sent down?” they say, He who sent down what the former ones before us wrote of falsehoods.
And that was as follows:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
What has your Lord revealed

? They said, Legends of the ancients. He said: The stories of the ancients and their falsehood. That was said by a group of polytheistic Arabs who used to sit on the road of whoever came to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and if one of the believers passed them, meaning the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they would say to them: Legends of the ancients, meaning: The stories of the ancients and their falsehood.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement legends of the ancients means: tales of the ancients.

x: God the Almighty says: These polytheists say to those who ask them, "What has your Lord revealed that our Lord revealed, according to what Muhammad claims: legends of the ancients," so that they may have their sins that they are committed in, from their denial of God, and their disbelief in what was revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from the sins of those who turn them away from belief in God, they go astray and are tempted by them without knowledge. And His statement,
h
How evil is that which they bear
, means: How evil is the sin that they commit, and the burden that they bear. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement,
h
That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection

, and among the burdens of those they led astray is their bearing of their own sins, and the sins of those who obeyed them, and that does not lighten the punishment for those who obeyed them in the slightest.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar, except that he said: And among the burdens of those whom they misguide is that they bear the sins of their own selves, and the rest of the hadith is similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection

, and also some of the burdens of those whom they led astray. He said: They will bear the sins of their own selves and the sins of those who obeyed them, but that will not lighten the punishment for those who obeyed them in the slightest.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection
, meaning their sins and the sins of those whom they led astray without knowledge.
h
How evil is that which they bear

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, my uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection
, and also some of the burdens of those whom they led astray without knowledge, meaning: They will bear their sins, and that is like his statement,
h
And burdens in addition to their burdens
, meaning: They will bear, along with their sins, the sins of those whom they led astray without knowledge.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: h
That they may bear their own burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection

, and also some of the burdens of those whom they led astray without knowledge. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.” He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Any caller who calls to misguidance and is followed will bear the burdens of those who followed him, without that diminishing from their burdens in the slightest. And any caller to guidance and is followed will have the same reward as them, without that diminishing from their reward in the slightest.”

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Suwaid told us, he said: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of a man, he said: Zaid bin Aslam said:
m: It reached him that the actions of the disbeliever appear to him in the form of the ugliest face and foulest smelling thing that God has created, so he sits beside him. Whenever something frightens him, it increases his fright, and whenever he fears something, it increases his fear. He says: What a bad companion you are, and who are you? He says: How do you know me? He says: No. He says: I am your actions, they were ugly, that is why you see me as ugly, and they were foul-smelling, that is why you see me as foul-smelling. Bow down to me so that I may mount you, for you often rode me in this world, so he mounts him, and this is His saying:
h
That they may bear their burdens in full on the Day of Resurrection

x: God the Almighty says: Those who were before these polytheists who hinder from the path of God, whoever wanted to follow the religion of God, plotted. They sought to overcome God by building his sons, wanting, according to their claim, to rise to the sky to fight those in it. And the one who sought that, as we have been told, was a tyrant from the tyrants of the Nabataeans.

Some of them said: He is Nimrod bin Canaan. And some of them said: He is Bukhtanasr. And some of their stories were mentioned in Surah Ibrahim. And it was said: The one mentioned in this place is the one mentioned by God in Surah Ibrahim.
Who said that?

c: Musa bin Harun told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: The one who argued with Abraham about his Lord ordered Abraham to be expelled, meaning from his city. He said: So he met Lot at the gate of the city, and he was his nephew, so he called him and he believed in him, and said: I am emigrating to my Lord, and Nimrod swore that he would seek the God of Abraham, so he took four chicks from the chicks of the eagles, and raised them with meat and bread until they grew big and thick and hurried, so he tied them in a coffin, and sat in that coffin, then he raised a leg of flesh for them, and they broke their fast, until when they went into the sky, he looked down to the earth, and he saw the mountains crawling like the crawling of ants, then he raised the flesh for them, then he looked and saw the earth surrounded by a sea as if it were a ship in water, then he was raised tall and fell into darkness, so he did not see what was above him or below him, so he was frightened, so he threw the flesh, and the mountains followed him, and when the mountains saw them, and they had come, they were falling, and I heard Their rustling, the mountains were frightened, and they were about to move from their places, but they did not do so. This is the saying of God Almighty And they plotted their plot, but with God is their plot, and their plot was such that mountains would move from it and it is in the reading of Ibn Masoud, and their plot was almost, so their flying towards him from the Holy House and their falling upon him on the Mountain of Smoke, so when he saw that he could not bear anything, he began to build the tower, so he built until when he built it to the sky, he climbed above it to look, claiming to be at the God of Abraham, so he innovated and he did not innovate, and God took his building from the foundations,
h
Then the roof fell upon them from above them

, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive, meaning: from their place of safety, and He took them from the foundation of the tower, so it collapsed with them, and it fell, so the tongues of the people were confused that day from the terror, so they spoke in seventy-three languages, and for this reason it was called Babylon. And the language of the people before that was Syriac.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Those before them plotted
, but God destroyed their building from the foundations, he said: It is Nimrod when he built the tower.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam:
m: The first tyrant on earth was Nimrod, so God sent a mosquito upon him, and it entered his nostril, and he remained for four hundred years hitting his head with hammers. The most merciful of people to him was the one who gathered his hands together, so he hit his head with them. He was a tyrant for four hundred years, so God punished him for four hundred years as his kingdom was, then God caused him to die. He was the one who had built a tower reaching to the sky, and he was the one about whom God said:
h
So God attacked their building from the foundations
, and
h
the roof fell upon them from above
them. As for His statement,
h
So God attacked their building from the foundations
, its meaning is: God demolished their building from its foundation. The foundations is the plural of base, which is the foundation.

x: Some of them used to say: This is an example of uprooting, but its meaning is: God uprooted them. He said: The Arabs say that when something is uprooted. His saying:
h
The roof fell upon them from above
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
The roof fell upon them from above
: the tops of their houses from above them.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Those before them plotted
, but God came to their building from the foundations. Yes, by God, God’s command came to it from its foundation. So
h
the roof fell upon them from above
them. The roof is the tops of houses, so their houses collapsed on them, so God destroyed them and ruined them. And the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive. Surat al-Nahl 16:26
h
Those before them plotted
, but God destroyed their building from its foundations, and
h
the roof fell upon them from above
them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then
h
the roof fell upon them from above
. He said: God attacked their building from its foundations, and the roof fell upon them.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Then God destroyed their building from the foundations, he said: The plot of Nimrod ibn Canaan who argued with Abraham about his Lord.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying:
h
The roof fell upon them from above is that the punishment came to them from the sky
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Then the roof fell upon them from above them

, meaning: A punishment from the sky. When they saw it, they surrendered and were humbled. The first of the two interpretations of the verse is the one that says: The meaning of that is: The roofs of their houses fell upon them, when the command of God came upon their foundations and bases, and their homes were destroyed by it, because that is the well-known statement of the foundations of a building, and the roof fell, and directing the meanings of God’s statement to the most famous and well-known of them is more appropriate than directing them to something else that has a way to it. And the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive. God Almighty says: And these who were plotted against by the polytheists of Quraysh, the punishment of God came to them from where they did not know that it came to them from it.

evidence.text: This is the saying of God Almighty And they plotted their plot, but with God is their plot, and their plot was such that mountains would move from it and it is in the reading of Ibn Masoud, and their plot was almost, so their flying towards him from the Holy House and their falling upon him on the Mountain of Smoke, so when he saw that he could not bear anything, he began to build the tower, so he built until when he built it to the sky, he climbed above it to look, claiming to be at the God of Abraham, so he innovated and he did not innovate, and God took his building from the foundations, Then the roof fell upon them from above them, and the punishment came upon them from where they did not perceive, meaning: from their place of safety, and He took them from the foundation of the tower, so it collapsed with them, and it fell, so the tongues of the people were confused that day from the terror, so they spoke in seventy-three languages, and for this reason it was called Babylon.

x: God the Almighty says: God did to those who plotted, whose affair God the Almighty described, what He did to them in this world, of hastening the punishment for them, and taking revenge for their disbelief and denial of His Oneness. Then, on the Day of Resurrection, He will disgrace them, humiliate them with a painful punishment, and say to them when they come to Him, Where are My partners about whom you used to quarrel? Its root is: Whoever quarrels with someone, he quarrels with me, and that is when each one of them does to his companion what is difficult for him. God the Almighty says on the Day of Resurrection, rebuking the polytheists for their worship of idols: Where are My partners? He says: That is, those whom you used to claim in this world were My partners today, why do they not come to you and repel from you the punishment that I am imposing on you? You used to worship them in this world, and you used to be their allies, and the guardian supports his guardian.
And their quarreling with God in their idols was their opposition to Him in their worship.

c: As Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Where are My partners about whom you used to dispute
? means: you used to oppose Me. His saying,
h
Those who were given knowledge said
