, ‘Indeed, disgrace and evil will be upon the disbelievers today.’ means: humiliation, disgrace, and evil, meaning: God’s punishment upon the disbelievers.

x: God Almighty says: Those who were given knowledge said: Indeed, disgrace and evil today will be upon those who disbelieved in God and denied His Oneness. Those whom the angels take in death means: those whose souls the angels take. Wrong with themselves meaning: while they were still disbelieving and associating partners with God. It was said: He meant by that those from Quraysh who were killed at Badr, and they were forced out to it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Yaqub bin Muhammad al-Zuhri told us, he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told me, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, he said:
m: There were people in Mecca who had acknowledged Islam but did not emigrate, so they were forced to go out with them to Badr, and some of them were killed, so God revealed about them: Those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves. And His saying, “So they threw down their peace,” means: So they submitted to His command and obeyed Him when they saw death descending upon them, We were not doing any evil, and in the speech there is an omission that the understanding of its listeners made it unnecessary to mention it, which is: They said: We were not doing any evil, He informs about them with that that they lied and said: We were not disobeying God, clinging to falsehood in the hope that they would be saved by that, so God belied them, and said: Rather, you were doing evil and turning people away from the path of God. Indeed, God is Knowing of what you were doing, meaning: God is All-Knowing of what you were doing in this world of His disobedience, and what you did in it that angered Him.

x: God Almighty says: He says to these oppressors themselves when they say to their Lord: We did not do any evil. Enter the gates of Hell, meaning: the levels of Hell. Eternally therein meaning: staying there. So evil is the abode of the arrogant. He says: So evil is the abode of the one who is arrogant towards God and does not acknowledge His Lordship and believes in His Oneness: Hell.
God the Almighty says: And it was said to the other group, who are people of faith and fear of God,
h
What has your Lord sent down
? They said, Good. He says: They said, He sent down good.

Some of the Arab scholars from Kufa used to say: The grammar differed in his saying They said, Legends of the ancients, and his saying, Good. The question before both answers is the same, which is his saying,
h
What has your Lord sent down

? Because the disbelievers denied the revelation, so they said when they heard it: Legends of the ancients, meaning that what you have brought is legends of the ancients, and God did not send down anything of it. As for the believers, they believed in the revelation, so they said, Good, meaning that He sent down good, so it was erected by the occurrence of the action from God on good, and for this reason they differed, then he began the report and said:
h
For those who do good in this world is good
. We have already explained the statement about that previously, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement:
h
For those who do good in this world is good

means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: For those who believed in God and His Messenger in this world, and obeyed Him in it, and called the servants of God to faith and to doing what God commanded, is good, meaning: an honor from God.

And the home of the Hereafter is better means: The home of the Hereafter is better for them than the home of this world, and the honor of God that He has prepared for them in it is greater than the honor that He hastened for them in this world. And excellent is the home of the righteous means: And excellent is the home of those who feared God in this world, so they feared His punishment by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, the home of the Hereafter. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “And it will be said to those who feared God, ‘
h
What has your Lord sent down
?’ They will say, ‘Good.
h
For those who do good in this world is good
.’” These are believers, so it will be said to them,
h
What has your Lord sent down
? They will say, “Good.
h
For those who do good in this world is good
.” That is, they believed in God and were commanded to obey God, and urged the people of God’s obedience to good and called them to it.

x: God Almighty means by His saying:
h
Gardens of Eden orchards for the place
. We have already explained the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the meaning of Eden in what has passed, so there is no need to repeat it.
h
They enter them

means: They enter the Gardens of Eden. There are three aspects to the raising of Gardens: One of them is that it is raised as a subject, and the other is by the pronoun referring to the male in His saying
h
They enter them
. The third is that it is the predicate of blessings, so the meaning is: If you make the predicate of blessings, then the good home of the righteous is the Gardens of Eden, and
h
They enter them

is in the position of a state, as it is said: The good home is a home that you live in. It may be permissible if the speech is with this interpretation: They enter it, from the connection to the Gardens of Eden. And His statement,
h
Underneath which rivers flow
, means: rivers flow beneath its trees.

They will have therein whatever they wish, meaning: for those who did good in this world, in the Gardens of Eden, whatever they wish of what their souls desire and their eyes delight in. Thus does God reward the righteous, meaning: just as God rewards those who did good in this world with what He has described to you, O people, that He will reward them with in this world and the Hereafter, thus does He reward those who feared Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience.

God Almighty says: Thus does God reward the righteous whose souls are taken by the angels of God, and they are pure, because God has purified them with the purity of faith and the purity of Islam during their life and death.

m: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.
Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us.
Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement:
h
Those whom the angels take in death while they are good
, he said: alive and dead, God has decreed that for them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. His saying: “They say, ‘Peace be upon you,’” means that the angels seize the souls of these righteous people, and they say to them: “Peace be upon you, go to Paradise,” a good report from God that the angels give them.

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, that
m: he heard Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi say: When the soul of the believing servant is filled with sorrow, an angel comes to him and says: Peace be upon you, O friend of God, God sends you peace, then he recites this verse:
h
Those whom the angels take in death while they are good
... to the end of the verse.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement: (So peace be upon you from the companions of the right) he said: The angels come to him with peace from God, and inform him that he is from the companions of the right.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Al-Ashb Abu Ali told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Muhammad bin Malik, on the authority of Al-Baraa’, he said:
m: His statement: (Peace be upon you, a word from a Merciful Lord), he said: He greets him at death. His saying: Because of what you used to do means: because of what you used to attain in this world during the days of your life in which you obeyed God and sought His pleasure.

evidence.text: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, that he heard Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi say: When the soul of the believing servant is filled with sorrow, an angel comes to him and says: Peace be upon you, O friend of God, God sends you peace, then he recites this verse: Those whom the angels take in death while they are good... to the end of the verse.

x: God Almighty says: Are these polytheists waiting for anything but the angels to come to take their souls, or for your Lord’s command to come to gather them for the Day of Resurrection? Thus did those before them. God Almighty says: Just as these people do by waiting for God’s angels to take their souls, or for God’s command to come, their predecessors among the disbelievers in God did, because that is the case with every polytheist in God: And God did not wrong them God Almighty says: God did not wrong them by inflicting His wrath, but they were wronging themselves by disobeying their Lord and disbelieving in Him, until they deserved His punishment, so He hastened it for them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqtada,
m: his statement,
h
Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them

? He said: With death. And he said in another verse: And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve and he is the Angel of Death, and he has messengers. God Almighty said: Or the command of your Lord should come that is on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Do they await anything but that the angels should come to them
? He said: at death when they take their souls, or that the command of your Lord should come? That is on the Day of Resurrection.

x: God Almighty says: Then those who did from the past nations what these polytheists from Quraysh did were afflicted with the evils of what they did, meaning the punishments of their sins and the wrath of the transgressions they acquired. And that which they used to ridicule befell them. He says: And the punishment of God befell them that which they used to ridicule and mock when the messengers of God warned them of that, and that befell them and not others of the people of faith in God.

God the Almighty says: And those who associated others with God and worshipped idols and statues besides God said: We do not worship these idols except because God has approved of our worship of these people, and we do not forbid what He has forbidden of the seas and the sawa'ib except that God willed from us and our fathers to forbid them and was pleased with it. Had it not been for that, He would have changed that with some of His punishments or by guiding us to other actions. God the Almighty says: Likewise did those who were before them from the polytheistic nations who followed their example, so they said the same as they said, and followed their path in denying the Messengers of God, and following the misguided actions of their fathers. And His statement:
h
Is there upon the messengers except the clear notification

? God the Almighty says: O you who say: If God had willed, we would not have associated others, nor our fathers, upon Our messengers whom We send to warn you of Our punishment for your disbelief, is there anything except the clear notification? He says: Except to convey to you the message We have sent to you. What he means by his saying: the clear is the one who explains its meaning to the one to whom it is conveyed, and the one to whom it is sent understands it.

God Almighty says: And We have certainly sent, O people, to every nation that came before you a Messenger, just as We sent among you, that you should worship God alone, with no partner for Him, and single out Him for obedience, and sincerely worship Him. And avoid Taghut means: And keep away from Satan, and beware that he misleads you, and turns you away from the path of God, so that you go astray. And among them are those whom God has guided means: Among those among whom We sent Our Messengers are those whom God has guided, so He guided them to believe in His Messengers, and accept them, and believe in God, and work in obedience to Him, so they succeeded and prospered, and were saved from the punishment of God. And among them are those upon whom error was due means: And among those among the nations to whom We sent Our Messengers are others upon whom error was due, so they deviated from the straight path, so they disbelieved in God, and denied His Messengers, and followed Taghut, so God destroyed them with His punishment, and sent down upon them His wrath that cannot be repelled.

About the criminal al-Nas 114:Travel through the land and see what was the end of those who denied. God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:If you, O people, do not believe our Messenger in what he tells you about these nations who were afflicted with what happened to them of our punishment because of their disbelief in God and their denial of His Messenger, then travel through the land they inhabited, the lands they inhabited, and the lands they inhabited, and see the effects of God on them and the effects of His wrath that descended upon them, how their denial of God’s Messengers was followed by what happened to them, for you will see the reality of that and know by it the truth of the report that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is telling you.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If you, Muhammad, are keen to guide these polytheists to faith in God and following the truth, God does not guide those who go astray. The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a fatha on the ya’ of yahdi and a damma on the ya’ of yahdi. The reciters also differed in the meaning of this.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa claimed that it means: whoever God has led astray will not be guided. He said: The Arabs say: the man has been guided, meaning he has been guided. Haddi and yahtada have the same meaning.

Others of them claimed that it means: whoever God has led astray will not be guided. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Ash-Sham and Basra read it as: lf God does not guide, with a damma on the ya’ of yahdi and yahdi, and a fatha on the dal of yahdi, meaning: whoever God has led astray will not have a guide. This reading is the more correct of the two readings in my opinion, because the meaning of is guided is rare in the speech of the Arabs and not widespread, and there is no benefit in someone saying: Whoever God leads astray, He does not guide him, because that is something that no one is ignorant of. Since that is the case, then the reading of what is widespread in the speech of the Arabs from the language, which contains great benefit, is more appropriate and more deserving. The interpretation of the statement: If the matter were as we have described: If you, O Muhammad, are keen on their guidance, then whoever God has led astray has no guide, so do not exhaust yourself in his matter, and convey to him what you were sent with so that the proof may be completed for him.

They will have no helpers. He says: And they will have no helper to help them against God if He wants to punish them, so that he may stand between God and what He wants of their punishment. In his saying: If you are keen, there are two dialects: Some Arabs say: Harasa yahras with a fatha on the ra in fa’al and a kasra on it in yaf’al. And Harasa yahras with a kasra on the ra in fa’al and a fatha on it in yaf’al. The reading is with a fatha in the past tense and a kasra in the future tense, and it is the dialect of the people of Hijaz.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in reading this.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a fatha on the ya’ of yahdi and a damma on the ya’ of yahdi.
The reciters also differed in the meaning of this.

The majority of the reciters of Medina, Ash-Sham and Basra read it as: lf God does not guide, with a damma on the ya’ of yahdi and yahdi, and a fatha on the dal of yahdi, meaning: whoever God has led astray will not have a guide.

This reading is the more correct of the two readings in my opinion, because the meaning of is guided is rare in the speech of the Arabs and not widespread, and there is no benefit in someone saying: Whoever God leads astray, He does not guide him, because that is something that no one is ignorant of.
Since that is the case, then the reading of what is widespread in the speech of the Arabs from the language, which contains great benefit, is more appropriate and more deserving.
The reading is with a fatha in the past tense and a kasra in the future tense, and it is the dialect of the people of Hijaz.

x: God Almighty says: And these polytheists from Quraysh swore by God with their strongest oaths, that God will not resurrect those who die after their death, and they lied and invalidated the oaths that they swore likewise, but God will resurrect them after their death, a promise that He has made to His servants that He will resurrect them, and God does not fail to fulfill His promise. But most of the people do not know. He says: But most of Quraysh do not know God’s promise to His servants, that He will resurrect them on the Day of Resurrection after their death, alive. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that? Bishr bin Muadh narrated: Yazid narrated: Saeed narrated: Qatada said: His statement,
h
And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies

, is a denial of God’s command or our command. People have become two groups regarding the al-Qiyamah 75:those who deny and those who believe. It was mentioned to us that a man said to Ibn Abbas: There are people in this Iraq who claim that Ali will be resurrected before the Day of Resurrection, and they interpret this verse differently. Ibn Abbas said: They are liars. This verse is for all people. By my life, if Ali were to be resurrected before the Day of Resurrection, we would not have married his women, nor would we have divided his inheritance.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: Some men say that Ali will be resurrected before the Day of Resurrection, and they interpret “
h
And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies

. Yes, it is a true promise binding upon Him, but most of the people do not know.” He said: If we knew that Ali would be resurrected, we would not have married his wives, nor divided his inheritance, but this applies to all people.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’,
m: regarding His statement:
h
And they swear by God their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies

, he said: A man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, swore in the presence of a man from among the liars, and said: By He who sends the soul after death, so he said: And you claim that you will be resurrected after death! And he swore by God his most solemn oath: God will not resurrect anyone who dies. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated:

c: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah, who said:
m: A Muslim man owed a polytheist a debt, so he came to him to collect it. Among the things he said was: And what I hope for after death is that it will be such and such. The polytheist said: You claim that you will be resurrected after death! So he swore by God with his most solemn oath that God will not resurrect anyone who dies. Then God revealed: “
h
And they swear by God with their most solemn oaths that God will not resurrect anyone who dies
. Yes, it is a promise binding upon Him, but most of the people do not know.”

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ata’ bin Abi Rabah, that he told him that
m: he heard Abu Hurayrah say: God said: The son of Adam insulted Me, and it was not right for him to insult Me, and he lied to Me, and it was not right for him to lie to Me. As for his lying to Me, He said: And they swear by God their most solemn oaths that God will not raise up anyone who dies. I said: Yes, it is a true promise binding upon Him. As for his insulting Me, He said: God is the third of three. I said: “Say: He is God, the One. God, the Self-Sufficient, He neither begets nor is born. And there is none comparable to Him.”

x: God Almighty says: Rather, God will surely resurrect whoever dies, a promise binding upon Him, to make clear to those who claim that God does not resurrect whoever dies, and to others who differ about God reviving His creation after their annihilation, and to let those who denied the truth of that and rejected its reality know that they were lying in their saying: God does not resurrect whoever dies.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: To make clear to them that over which they differ, he said: to the people in general.

x: God Almighty says: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, ‘Be,’ and it is.

God Almighty says: If We want to resurrect someone who has died, there is no effort or fatigue on Us in bringing them back to life, nor in anything else that We create, exist, and bring about, because when We want to create and bring them into being, We only say to them: Be, and they are. There is no difficulty in it, nor is there any cost to Us. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement:
h
It will be

i: Most of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read it as a beginning, and that his statement:
Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it
, ‘Be,’ is a complete statement, self-sufficient in what comes after it, then it begins and it is said:
x: He wants to express it and like it Some of the readers of the Levant and some of the later readers of Kufa read it as an accusative, in apposition to his statement: that we say to him.

It is as if the meaning of the statement according to their school of thought is: We do not say to a thing when we want except to say to it: Be, and it is. It has been narrated from the Arabs by hearing: I want to come to you, but the rain prevents me, in apposition to prevents me with I come to you. And His statement: And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged - We will surely settle them in this world with good God Almighty says: And those who left their people, their homes, and their homelands out of enmity towards them for the sake of God because of their disbelief, to others other than them after they had been wronged meaning: after they had been afflicted with hardships in themselves for the sake of God We will surely settle them in this world with good meaning: We will surely settle them in this world in a dwelling that they will be pleased with, good.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged - We will surely assign to them a place of refuge

. He said: These are the companions of Muhammad, whom the people of Mecca wronged, so they expelled them from their homes, until groups of them fled to Abyssinia, then God assigned them to Medina after that, making it a place of emigration for them, and He gave them supporters from among the believers.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Salam,
m: who said: Hisham narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud bin Abi Hind, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: We will surely grant them good in this world. He said: Medina.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they were wronged - We will surely assign to them good in this world
, he said: They are people who emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of Mecca after they had been wronged, and the polytheists had wronged them.

x: Others said: What he meant by his saying:
h
We will surely grant them good in this world is that we will provide them with good provision in this world
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: We will surely give them a place to live We will surely provide them with a good provision in this world.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Awam, on the authority of someone who told him that
m: when Umar ibn Al-Khattab gave a gift to a man from the Muhajireen, he would say: Take it, may God bless it for you. This is what God promised you in this world, and what He has stored up for you in the Hereafter is better. Then he recited this verse: We will surely give them good in this world,
h
and the reward of the Hereafter is greater

, if they only knew. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who said: The meaning of We will certainly settle them is: We will certainly settle them and inhabit them, because settlement in the speech of the Arabs means settling in a place and descending into it. From this is the saying of God Almighty And We had certainly settled the Children of Israel in a true settlement. It was said: This verse was revealed about Abu Jandal bin Suhayl.
b.via: on the authority of someone who

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Jaʿfar ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, he said:
m: And those who emigrated for the cause of God after they had been wronged… to His saying and upon their Lord they rely was revealed about Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl. And His saying:
h
And the reward of the Hereafter is greater

, if they only knew. He says: And God’s reward for them for their migration in it in the Hereafter is greater, because His reward for them there is Paradise, whose bliss is eternal and never perishes. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: God said,
h
And the reward of the Hereafter is greater
, meaning, by God, what God will reward them for from His Paradise is greater, if they only knew.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of his statement: It will be.

Most of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read it as a beginning, and that his statement: Our word to a thing when We intend it is only that We say to it, ‘Be,’ is a complete statement, self-sufficient in what comes after it, then it begins and it is said: It will be, as the poet said: He wants to express it and like it Some of the readers of the Levant and some of the later readers of Kufa read it as an accusative, in apposition to his statement: that we say to him.
Then he recited this verse: We will surely give them good in this world, and the reward of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.

x: God Almighty says: These are the ones whose characteristics We have described, and to whom We have given the reward that We have mentioned, who were patient for the sake of God in the face of what befell them in this world. And upon their Lord they put their trust. He says: And in God they trust in their affairs, and to Him they rely in the misfortunes that befall them.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We did not send before you, O Muhammad, to any nation, to call to Our Oneness, and to adhere to Our commands and prohibitions, except men from among the children of Adam to whom We revealed Our revelation, not angels. He says: So We did not send to your people except the like of what We sent to the nations before them of their kind, and on their path. So ask the people of the message. He says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:And if you do not know that those to whom We sent before you from among the nations were men from among the children of Adam like Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you say: They are angels - that is: you thought that God had spoken to them before - then ask the people of the message, and they are those who had read the books before them: the Torah and the Gospel, and other books of God that He sent down to His servants.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So ask the people of the remembrance. He said: The people of the Torah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Sufyan, who said:
m: I asked Al-A’mash about his statement,
h
So ask the people of knowledge
. He said: We heard that it was from the people of the Torah and the Gospel who converted to Islam.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We did not send before you except men to whom We revealed
h
so ask the people of the message if you do not know
, he said: They are the People of the Book.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
So ask the people of knowledge

if you do not know. He said: He said to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:Muhammad is in the Torah and the Gospel. Abu Kuraib narrated: Uthman ibn Saeed narrated: Bishr ibn Ammarah narrated: Abu Rawq narrated: Ad-Dahhak narrated: Ibn Abbas narrated: When God sent Muhammad as a Messenger, the Arabs denied it, or those among them denied it, and said: God is too great for His Messenger to be a human being like Muhammad. He said: Then God revealed: Is it a wonder to people that We have revealed to a man from among themselves? And He said: (And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed.
h
So ask the people of the message if you do not know

* By clear proofs and scriptures.) So ask the people of the message: meaning the people of the previous books, were the messengers who came to you human beings or angels? If they were angels, you would deny it, and if they were human beings, do not deny that Muhammad is a Messenger. He said: Then He said: And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed from the people of the towns: meaning they are not from the people of the heaven as you said.

x: Others said about this:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar:
m: h
So ask the people of knowledge
if you do not know. He said: We are the people of knowledge.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
So ask the people of the message if you do not know

, he said: The message is the Qur’an. And he recited, Indeed, it is We who sent down the message and indeed, We will be its guardian, and he recited, Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them… the verse.

x: God Almighty says: We sent with clear proofs and scriptures men to whom We revealed.
How was it said with clear proofs and scriptures, and what brought this ba’ in His statement with clear proofs? If you say: Its bringer is His statement
h
We sent and it is from its relative clause
, is it permissible for it to be the relative clause of what comes before except after it? And if you say: Its bringer is something else, what is it, and where is the verb that brought it?

The scholars of Arabic have differed on that, and some of them said: The ba’ in His statement with clear proofs is from the relative clause of We sent, and he said: Except in this place, and with denial and interrogation in every place has the meaning of other, and he said: The meaning of the statement is: And We did not send before you with clear proofs and scriptures other than men to whom We revealed, and he says on that: None struck except your brother Zaid, and did none spoke to anyone except your brother Amr, meaning: None struck Zaid other than your brother, and did none speak to Amr other than your brother?

And he argues for that with the statement of Aws bin Hajar: My sons, you are not a hand but a hand that has no arm He says: If it were except without meaning, the statement would be invalid, because the one who lowered the ba’ before except cannot repeat it after except by lowering the second hand, but the meaning of except is the meaning of other, and he also cites as evidence the statement of God Almighty If there were within them gods other than God and he says: except in the meaning of other in this place. And others used to say: This is based on two statements: He means: And We did not send before you except men whom We sent with clear proofs and scriptures. And he said: And similarly the statement of the one who says: None struck except your brother Zayd means: None struck except your brother, then he begins by hitting Zayd, and similarly none passed by except your brother Zayd, none passed by except your brother, then he says: He passed by Zayd, and he cites as evidence for that the verse of Al-A’sha: And there is no one who can help if he comes to the neighborhood fearing or saying, I am sorry.

He says: If that were based on a word, it would be a mistake, because the defect is due to the speaker’s connection, but that is permissible in two cases: And the rajaz poet said: I told them that they tortured their neighbor with fire. Who can torture anyone but God with fire? So the interpretation of the statement is: We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed. We sent them with clear proofs and scriptures, and We sent down to you the message. The clear proofs are the evidence and arguments that God gave His messengers, evidence of their prophethood, bearing witness to them of the truth of what they brought to them from God. The scriptures are the books, and they are the plural of Zabur, from zabarat al-kitab and dhabartuhu: if you wrote it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: with clear proofs and scriptures. He said: The scriptures are the books.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With clear proofs and scriptures. He said: The verses. And scriptures are the books.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The books are the zabar.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: and the scriptures, meaning: by the books. And His statement,
h
And We have sent down to you the Reminder

, means: And We have sent down to you, O Muhammad, this Qur’an as a reminder to the people and an admonition to them, that you may make clear to the people, means: so that you may make them aware of what was sent down to them of that, and that they may reflect, means: and that they may remember and take heed from it: that is, from what We sent down to you, and— Al-Muthanna told me, he said:

c: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Zarqaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, he said: Mujahid said:
m: And perhaps they will reflect, he said: They will obey. Surat al-Nahl 16:44 With clear proofs and scriptures. And We have sent down to you the message that you may make clear to the people what was sent down to them and that they might give thought.

x: God the Almighty says: Are those who wronged the believers among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and sought to tempt them away from their religion, from the polytheists of Quraysh who said - when it was said to them: What has your Lord revealed - legends of the ancients, turning away from the path of those who wanted to believe in God, secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up because of their disbelief and polytheism, or that the punishment of God will come to them from a place they do not perceive, and they do not know from where it will come? Mujahid used to say: He meant by that Nimrod bin Canaan.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid: Do those who plot evil deeds feel secure that God will not cause the earth to swallow them up? ... to His saying, or seize them in fear. He said: This is Nimrod ibn Canaan and his people.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. We chose the statement we made in interpreting that, because that is a threat from God to those who associate partners with Him, and it follows His statement, And We did not send before you, except men to whom We revealed, so ask the people of the message if you do not know. So the threat to those who did not acknowledge God’s proof, whose address was made before that, was more appropriate than the report about those whose mention was cut off from them. Qatada used to say about the meaning of bad deeds in this context:

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Then do those who plot evil deeds feel secure
? meaning polytheism.

x: God Almighty says: Or He may seize them in their confusion, then they will not be able to escape.
He, the Most High, means by His saying:
h
Or He seizes them in their turning

over or destroys them in their movement in the country, and their wandering in their travels, Then they will not be able to escape. The Most High says: For they will not be able to escape from that to God if He wills to seize them in this way. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
or He seizes them in their turning
about, meaning: in their differences.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Or He seizes them in their turning
, then they will not escape. He said: If you wish, take him on a journey.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Or He seizes them in their turning
in their travels.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same. Ibn Jurayj said about this:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: h
Or He seizes them in their turning

over. He said: Turning over means that He seizes them by night and by day. As for his saying: or he takes them with fear, he means: or he destroys them with fear, and that is by reducing their extremities and sides, little by little, until they are all destroyed. It is said from this: he feared spending so-and-so’s money: if he diminished it, and similar to his fear of fear means: diminishing, the saying of the poet: Sir Tamka is afraid of the monkey, just as the spring tree scares ships. He means by his saying: The journey is frightening: its hump is shortened. We mentioned on the authority of Al-Haitham bin Adi that he used to say: It is a language of Azd Shanu’a that is known to them, and from it is the saying of another: Fear their enemy, money and gifts, chains in their throats that clank Al-Farra’ used to say: I took it from its edges and sides. He said: This is what I heard. The explanation came with the letter ha and they are both in one meaning. He said: Similar to it is what was read in two ways, His statement: Indeed, for you during the day is swimming and salting. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that? Ibn Wakee’ narrated: My father narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Aamer bin Mas’oud, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Umar that he asked them about this verse: “
h
Or He seizes them in their turning

over and they will not be able to escape. Or He seizes them with fear.” They said: We do not think that it is except when he reduces what he repeats of the verses. Umar said: I do not think that it is except for what you reduce of the disobedience of God. He said: So he left those who were with Umar and met a Bedouin and said: O so-and-so, what did your Lord do? He said: You have frightened Him, meaning you have reduced Him. He said: So he returned to Umar and told him, and he said: May God detest that.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or he takes them due to fear. He said: If you wish, he takes him due to the death of his companion and fears that.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: On fear he said:
m: diminishment and fright.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Or He takes them on fear on the basis of deficiency.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: On fear, he said: It decreases.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or He takes them by force so He punishes or transgresses.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, Or He takes them in fear, he said: It was said: Fear means diminishing, He diminishes them from the countries from the outskirts.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Or He seizes them in fear, meaning: The punishment seizes one group and leaves another, and He punishes the town and destroys it, and leaves another beside it. And His statement: Indeed, your Lord is Most Kind and Most Merciful means: If your Lord does not seize these people who plotted evil deeds with a hastened punishment for them, and seize them with death and the decrease of some of them in succession of others, then He is Most Kind to His creation, Most Merciful to them, and out of His kindness and mercy towards them He does not cause the earth to swallow them up, nor does He hasten the punishment for them, but He frightens them and decreases them with death.

evidence.text: He said: Similar to it is what was read in two ways, His statement: Indeed, for you during the day is swimming and salting.

x: The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Madinah and Basra read it as or did they not see with a ya as a report about those who plotted evil deeds.

Some of the readers of Kufa read it as or did they not see with a ta as a address. The first of the two readings, in my opinion, is with the letter sab sab, which is the reading of the one who reads with the letter ya as a report about those who plotted evil deeds, because that is in the context of their stories and the report about them, then after that is the report about their abandonment of God’s proof against them and their abandonment of looking into His evidence and considering it. So the interpretation of the statement then is: Did not these who plotted evil deeds see what God created of an upright body, a tree or a mountain or something else, whose shadows seek shade to the right and the left? He says: It returns from one place to another, so it is in one state at the beginning of the day, then it shrinks, then it returns to another state at the end of the day.
A group of interpreters said about the right and left sides:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Have they not seen what God has created of things
, whose shadows extend to the right and the left, prostrating to God? As for the right: it is the beginning of the day, and as for the left: it is the end of the day.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: His shadows are cast to the right and the left. He said: In the morning and the evening, when the shadows fall, the shadows of everything prostrate to God in the morning, and when they fall in the evening, they prostrate to God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And its shadows will be spread on the right and the left

, meaning: in the morning and the evening. The shadows prostrate to God in the morning until the shadows are spread, then they prostrate to God until the night, meaning: the shadow of everything. Ibn Abbas used to say about his saying,
h
He seeks shade in its shade
, what:

c: Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, and seeks shade from its shadows, meaning: it sways. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of his saying, prostrating to God.

x: Some of them said: The shadow of everything is its prostration.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He seeks shade in its shadow. He said: The shade of everything is its prostration.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ishaq Al-Razi told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
He seeks shade in its shade
. He said: The shade of the believer prostrated willingly, and the shade of the unbeliever prostrated unwillingly.

x: Others said: Rather, what he meant by his saying:
h
He seeks shade from its shadows is both the right and the left in the state of prostration
. They said: The prostration of things is not their shadows.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us, and Nasr bin Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi told me, they said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of al-Dahhak,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
Have they not seen what God has created of things seeking shade
? He said: When the shade is extended, everything turns in prostration towards the qiblah, whether plants or trees. He said: So they used to prefer to pray at that time.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hammani told us, he said: Yahya bin Yaman told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God, and seeks shade in its shade, he said: When the sun declines, everything prostrates to God Almighty.

x: Others said: Rather, what God described as prostrating in this verse is the shadows of things, so only their shadows prostrate, not those that have shadows.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Have they not seen what God has created of things that seek shade in their shadows
? He said: It is the Surat al-Nahl 16:48
h
Have they not seen what God has created of things

whose shadows turn to the right and the left, prostrating to God while they are humbled? prostration of the shadows, the shadows of everything in the heavens and on the earth of creatures. He said: The prostration of the shadows of creatures, and the shadows of everything.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Have they not seen what God has created of things seeking shade

? What He has created of everything to His right and left, so He said what He said to the right and left, he said: Have you not seen that when you pray Fajr, what is between the rising of the sun and its setting is a shadow, then God sends the sun as a guide for it, and God takes away the shadow. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God informed in this verse that the shadows of things are what prostrate, and their prostration is their inclination and rotation from side to side, and from one direction to another, as Ibn Abbas said. It is said of this: the palm tree prostrated when it leaned, and the camel prostrated and prostrated: when it leaned to be ridden. We have explained the meaning of prostration in other places in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it. His saying, and they are humbled, means: and they are submissive. It is said from this: So-and-so humbled himself for God, he humbles himself and submits, and from this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: There is nothing left but a burrow in a hole in a land other than yours. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And they are humbled means humiliated.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they are humbled: meaning, humiliated.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same. As for the singularization of the right in his statement, on the right and the left, he pluralized them. This came about because the meaning of the statement is:
h
Have they not seen what God has created of things

, which seek shade in the shadows of what He has created of things on its right: meaning what He has created, and its left. So the word what is a single word, but its meaning is the meaning of the plural. So he said: on the right means: on the right of what He has created, then he returned to its meaning in the left.

x: Some of the Arabs used to say: The Arabs only do that because most speech is confronting one person, so it is said to a man: Take on your right. He said: So it is as if if he singularizes it, he goes to one of the people, and if he pluralizes it, it is that which is not questioned.

i: And he cited as evidence for the Arabs’ action the saying of the poet: In the mouths of the gloating rock, if a calamity has brought me down, my cub is hidden among the lions He said:
x: With the mouths of the two who gloat, and he did not say: With the mouths.
And the other said: The people of Al-Wardun and Taym in the valley of Saba, their necks were bitten by buffalo hides. He did not say: skins.

evidence.text: The readers differed in reading this.
The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Madinah and Basra read it as or did they not see with a ya as a report about those who plotted evil deeds.
Some of the readers of Kufa read it as or did they not see with a ta as a address.

The first of the two readings, in my opinion, is with the letter sab sab, which is the reading of the one who reads with the letter ya as a report about those who plotted evil deeds, because that is in the context of their stories and the report about them, then after that is the report about their abandonment of God’s proof against them and their abandonment of looking into His evidence and considering it.

x: God Almighty says: To God submits and surrenders to His command whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures that creep upon it, and the angels in the heavens, and they are not too proud to humble themselves before Him in obedience And those who do not believe in the Hereafter - their hearts are in denial, and they are arrogant and their shadows spread out to the right and the left, prostrating to God, and they are humbled.

Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: Mentioning one of the animals is sufficient instead of mentioning all of them. The meaning of the statement is: To God prostrates everything in the heavens and on the earth of animals and angels, just as it is said: What a man came to me, meaning: What a man came to me.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: It was said: from a beast because ma even though it may be in the manner of alladhi which, it is not specific, so if it is not specific it is similar to the penalty, and the penalty is included in what comes after it from an indefinite noun, so it is said: whoever strikes him from a man, strike him. And min is not dropped from this position out of aversion to it being similar to being a state of man and ma, so they made it min to indicate that it is an explanation of ma and min because they are not specific, so the inclusion of min in what comes after them is an explanation of their meaning, and the inclusion of man indicates what is not specific from man and ma, so for this reason they were not abolished.

God Almighty says: These angels in the heavens and on the earth, and every creature on earth, fear their Lord above them, lest He punish them if they disobey His command and do what they are commanded. He says: And they do what He commands them to do, so they fulfill His rights and avoid His wrath.

God Almighty says: And God said to His servants: Do not take a partner for Me, O people, and do not worship other gods, for if you worship other than Me along with Me, you will be making a partner for Me, and I have no partner. There is only one God, and one god, and I am that, so fear Me. He says: So fear Me and fear My punishment for disobeying Me if you disobey Me and worship other than Me, or associate a partner in your worship of Me.

God Almighty says: And to God belongs the dominion of whatever is in the heavens and the earth. He has no partner in any of that. It is He who created them, and it is He who provides for them, and in His hand is their life and their death. And His statement,
h
And to Him belongs the religion
, always and absolutely, God Almighty says: And to Him belongs obedience and sincerity, always and absolutely obligatory. It is said from this:
h
And to Him belongs the religion

, always and absolutely, as Ad-Dailami said: I do not seek praise that lasts a day, but I will always be blamed for all eternity. And from it is the saying of God And for them is a lasting punishment, and the saying of Hassan: The wind has changed him, and his thunder has raged and poured. As for pain, it is said: The man became tired and weary, meaning he became exhausted and bored. From this comes the poet’s saying: He does not bite his leg from where, nor does he pour it, nor does he bite his yellow ribcage.
The interpreters differed in the interpretation of Al-Wasib.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: what we said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Al-Aghar bin Al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifa bin Husayn, on the authority of Abu Nadhra, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And to Him belongs the religion
, always. He said: Always.

c: Ismail bin Musa told me: Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And to Him belongs the religion
, always. He said: Always.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Ya’la bin Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Always.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And to Him is the religion, always. He said: Always.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And to Him belongs the religion
, always. He said: Always.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abda and Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
And to Him belongs the religion
, always. He said: Always.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Amr bin Awn told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And to Him belongs the religion
always: meaning always, for God, the Blessed and Exalted, did not leave any of His creation except that it worshipped Him willingly or unwillingly.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Constantly he said:
m: Always. Do you not see that he says persistent torment: meaning permanent?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And to Him belongs the religion
, always, he said: Always, and al-wasib means permanent.

x: Others said: The imperative in this case is: the obligatory.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Qais, on the authority of Yaʿla ibn al-Nuʿman, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to Him belongs the religion

, obligatory. He said: Obligatory. Mujahid used to say: The meaning of religion in this context is sincerity. We have already mentioned the meaning of religion in other contexts, so there is no need to repeat it.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And to Him belongs the religion
, devotedly he said: sincerity. Surat al-Nahl 16:52 And to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is the religion that is pure. Then
h
do you fear other than God

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Religion is sincerity. And His statement:
h
Do you fear other than God
? God Almighty says:
h
Do you fear other than God

, O people? That is, do you fear and beware lest He deprive you of God’s blessing upon you through your sincere worship of your Lord, your singling out obedience to Him, and you have no benefit other than Him.

x: Arabists differed about the reason for the introduction of the letter fa' in the phrase from God. Some Basrans said: The letter fa' was introduced because ma is like min, so the predicate was made with the letter fa'. Some Kufians said: ma has the meaning of recompense, and it has an implied verb, as if you said: Whatever blessing you have is from God, because recompense must have a verb in the jussive mood.

i: If it appears, it is in the jussive mood, and if it does not appear, it is implied, as the poet said:
x: The mind in our money is not limited by an arm, and if we are patient, we know patience He said: He wanted: If the mind is hidden, he concealed it.

He said: And if you made what is in you in the meaning of which is permissible, and made its connection to you and what in the place of raising by his saying: Then from God and inserted the fa’, as he said Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you and every connected noun like man, what and which, it is permissible to enter the fa’ in its predicate because it is a present tense of the recompense, and the recompense may be answered with the fa’, and it is not permissible for your brother, so it is standing, because it is a non-relative noun, and likewise you say: what is yours for me, so if you say: what is yours, it is permissible for you to say: what is yours for it is mine, and if you drop the fa’ then it is correct. The interpretation of the statement: Whatever you have in your bodies, O people, of wellness, health, and safety, and in your wealth of growth, then it is God who bestows that blessing upon you and no one else, because that is up to Him and in His hand.

Then when harm befalls you means: when sickness, disease, an accidental illness, or hardship in life befalls you in your bodies, then to Him you cry out means: then to God you cry out in supplication and seek help from Him, so that He may remove that from you. Its origin is: from the roaring of the bull, from which it is said: the bull roared, roaring, and that is when it raises a loud voice from hunger or something else, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: And I will not wear out the temple he built and was crucified in and became The prayers of prayer range from one stage of prostration to one stage of humility By al-Juwar it means shouting, either by supplication or by reading. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement: To Him you cry out in supplication, he said: You implore in supplication.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: may God be pleased with them both, he said: Ad-Darr means illness.

x: God Almighty says: Then when the hardship is removed from you, at once a party of you associate others with their Lord.

God Almighty says: Then when your Lord grants you well-being, and removes from you the illness that has befallen you in your bodies, and the hardship in your livelihood, and relieves you of the affliction, A party of you will associate others with their Lord meaning: A group of you will make a partner with God in their worship, so they will worship idols, and slaughter sacrifices for them in gratitude to someone other than Him who has blessed them with relief from their distress, so that they may disbelieve in what We have given them meaning: so that they may deny God’s blessing in what He has given them of removing their distress, so enjoy yourselves, and you will soon know. This is a warning from God to those whose characteristics He has described in these verses, and a threat to them. He, the Most High, says to them: Enjoy yourselves in this worldly life until your appointed times come to you, and you reach the appointed time for your life and your enjoyment in it, for from that you will go to your Lord, and you will know by meeting Him the consequences of what your hands have earned, and you will know the evil consequences of your affair. And you regret when regret is of no use to you.
God Almighty says: These polytheists among the idolaters give a share to that which they know neither harmful nor beneficial.

He says: A portion and a reward for what We have provided them of wealth, as a result of their associating with Him the One they know created them, and He is the One who benefits them and harms them, and no one else, like the One who:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And they assign to that of which they have no knowledge a share of what We have provided for them

, he said: They know that God created them, and that it harms them and benefits them, then they assign to that which they do not know will harm them and not benefit them a share of what We have provided for them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And they assign to that of which they have no knowledge a share of what We have provided for them
, and they are the polytheists of the Arabs, they assigned to their idols a share of what We have provided for them, and they assign a portion of their wealth to their idols.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And they assign to that of which they have no knowledge a share of what We have provided for them

, he said: They assigned to their gods, which have no share or anything, a share of what God has said about the crops and livestock, they call upon them by their names and slaughter for them. And His statement: By God, you will surely be asked about what you used to invent. God Almighty says: By God, you polytheists who make gods and rivals a share in what We have provided for you, as a form of association with God and disbelief, God will ask you on the Day of Resurrection about what you used to invent in this world. That is, you invent falsehood and slander against God by claiming a partner for Him and making your idols a share in what He has provided for you. Then He will punish you with a punishment that will be a reward for your ingratitude for His blessings and your invention of falsehood against Him.

x: God Almighty says: And they attribute to God daughters - glory be to Him - while they have for themselves whatever they desire.

God the Almighty says: And from the ignorance of these polytheists and the evil of their actions, and the ugliness of their slander against their Lord, is that they attribute to the One who created them, managed them, and bestowed blessings upon them, and thus He deserved thanks for His blessings upon them, and deserved praise for them: daughters. And it is not appropriate for God to have a son, male or female, glory be to Him. He, the Most High, has thereby purified Himself from what they have added to Him and attributed to Him of daughters, so they were not satisfied with their ignorance when they added to Him what should not be added to Him. And it is not appropriate for Him to have a son, that they add to Him what they desire for themselves, and love for themselves, but they added to Him what they hate for themselves, and do not accept for themselves of daughters, such that they kill them if they have them.

As for the word ma in his statement, and they will have what they desire, there are two aspects of Arabic: the accusative case, in apposition to daughters, so the meaning of the statement, if that is intended, is: And they attribute to God daughters and to themselves the sons that they desire, so ma is for the sons. The nominative case, based on the statement being the subject of his statement, and they will have what they desire, so the meaning of the statement is: And they attribute to God daughters and to themselves the sons. And his saying, And when one of them is given the good report of a female child, his face darkens, meaning: And when one of those who attributed daughters to God is given the good report of the birth of something that He attributes to Himself, his face darkens from his hatred of it, and he is full of grief, meaning he has suppressed his grief and is filled with sorrow over her birth to him, so he does not show that.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And they attribute to God daughters, glory be to Him, and for themselves what they desire, then he said:
h
And when one of them is given the report of a female

, his face darkens, and he is filled with inward grief… to the end of the verse. And he says: They attribute to God daughters, you are pleased with them for me, and you are not pleased with them for yourselves. That is because in the Age of Ignorance, if a female slave was born to a man among them, he would keep her with disgrace, or he would bury her in the dirt while she was alive.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when one of them is given the report of a female

, his face darkens, and he is filled with inward grief, this is the action of the polytheists of Arabia. God, the Most High, informed them of the evil of their actions. As for the believer, he deserves to be satisfied with what God has apportioned for him. God’s decree is better than a person’s decree for himself. By my life, he does not know that it is better. A girl may be better for her family than a boy. God has only informed you of their actions so that you may avoid them and desist from them. One of them used to feed his dog and bury his daughter alive.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: And he is suppressing his grief he said: Sad.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement, And he is Kazeem, he said: Kazeem means the one who is suppressed. We have explained that with its supporting evidence in other places.

x: God Almighty says: This one who was given good report of the birth of a female child for him will disappear from the people, and will be out of their sight because of the evil of the good report he was given. That is, because of his harming him, tempting him to keep him in humiliation: that is, in disgrace. And that is also the case in the language of the Quraysh, as I was told. They say for humiliation: disgrace. And from that is the saying of Al-Hutay’ah: When I feared humiliation and the donkey was held back against his will, the rope did not hold its hoof steady. Some of Banu Tamim made Hawn a source for something easy. Al-Kisa’i mentioned that he heard them say: If you are of little means, ease the burden since today. He said: And I heard “Hawan in a similar meaning. I heard one of them say to his camel: There is nothing wrong with it except its ease, meaning that it is of low price.

So if they said: He walks easily, they would not say it except by opening the ha, as God Almighty said: And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth easily. “Or does He bury him in the dust?” He said: He buries him alive in the dust and buries him alive.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj:
m: Should he keep him in humiliation or bury him in the dirt? He buried his daughter alive. And His saying,
h
How evil is their judgment

, means: How evil is the judgment that these polytheists make, because they attributed to God what they would not be pleased with for themselves, and they attributed to what neither benefits them nor harms them a partner in what God has provided for them, and they worshipped other than He who created them and bestowed blessings upon them.

x: This is report from God, the Most High, that His saying, And when one of them is given the report of a female, his face darkens, and he is filled with inward grief, and the verse that follows it is an example that God gave to these polytheists who attributed daughters to God. He explained with His saying,
h
For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is an evil example

, that it is an example, and what He meant by His saying, the Most High, For those who do not believe in the Hereafter, is for those who do not believe in the Resurrection, reward, and punishment from the polytheists, an evil example, which is the ugly example, and what is bad for the one who is given that example, And to God belongs the highest example, meaning: And to God belongs the highest example, which is the best, the kindest, the best, and the most beautiful, and that is monotheism and submission to Him that there is no god but Him.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And to God belongs the highest example. He said: The testimony that there is no god but God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
For those who do not believe in the Hereafter is an evil example

, but to God belongs the highest example is sincerity and monotheism. And His statement, And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise, God Almighty says: And to God belongs the Might, with which it is not impossible for Him to punish these polytheists whose description He described in these verses, nor to punish those whom He wills to punish for their disobedience to Him, and nothing that He wills and desires is impossible for Him, because creation is His creation, and the command is His command, and He is Wise in His management, so no defect or error enters into His management.

x: God Almighty says: And if God were to punish the sinners of the children of Adam for their sins He would not leave upon it meaning upon the earth any living creature that crawls upon it but He defers them meaning: but with His forbearance He defers these oppressors and does not hasten their punishment until a specified term meaning: until the time that He has set for them, and when their term comes meaning: when the time that He has set for their destruction comes they will not delay from destruction for an hour so that they are given respite nor will they advance it until they have fulfilled their terms. And in the same way as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, who said:
m: The dung beetle was almost punished for the sin of the sons of Adam, and he recited: If God were to punish people for their wrongdoing, He would not leave on the earth a single creature.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ismail ibn Hakim al-Khuza’i told us: Muhammad ibn Jabir al-Ja’fi told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Abi Katheer, on the authority of Abu Salamah, who said:
m: Abu Hurairah heard a man saying: The oppressor harms no one but himself. He said: So he turned to him and said: Yes, by God, the houbara bustard dies in its nest, emaciated, because of the oppression of the oppressor.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Abu Ubaidah Al-Haddad told us, he said: Qura bin Khalid Al-Sadosi told us, on the authority of Al-Zubayr bin Adi, he said: Ibn Masoud said:
m: The sin of the son of Adam killed the dung beetle.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, who said: Abdullah said:
m: The dung beetle almost perished in its hole because of the sin of the son of Adam.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri,
m: God said: And when their time comes, they will not delay it an hour, nor will they advance it. He said: We see that when his time comes, he will not delay it an hour, nor will he advance it, as long as his time has not come, for God delays what He wills, and advances what He wills.

x: God the Almighty says: And these polytheists attribute to God what they hate for themselves, and they claim that they have the best, which they hate for themselves, the daughters they attribute to God the Almighty, and they claimed that the angels are the daughters of God.
