As for the best that they attribute to themselves: it is the male children, and that is because they used to bury their female children alive, and keep the male children, and they would say: We have the males and God has the daughters, and it is similar to His statement:
h
And they attribute to God daughters - glory be to Him - and to themselves what they desire
. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And their tongues describe falsehood, that they will have the best. He said: The saying of the Quraysh 106:We have the sons, and God has the daughters.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, except that he said: The words of the infidels of Quraysh.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And they attribute to God what they hate and their tongues describe falsehood
: that is, they say that they have the best: that is, the young boys.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: They will have the best. He said: The young boys. And His saying:
h
There is no doubt that they will have the Fire and that they will be transgressors

. God Almighty says: It is a necessary truth that these people who say that God has daughters, who give Him what they hate for themselves, and for their own souls, will have the best with God on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:the Fire. We have explained the interpretation of God’s saying There is no harm in more than one place in this book of ours with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: regarding this: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: No crime means: Yes. And his saying: La Jarm Some of the Arabists used to say: Jarm was not placed in the accusative case without the letter la as the letter mim was placed in the accusative case in the saying: La ghulam lak There is no slave for you. He said: But it was placed in the accusative case because it is a past tense verb, like the saying of the speaker: So-and-so sat down and jals sit down. And the speech: There is no response to their speech, meaning that the matter is not like this. Jarm: earned, like his saying: La aqsam I swear, and the like. And some of them used to say: Jarm was placed in the accusative case without the letter la but it means: There is no need and There is no inevitability, but it has become so common in speech that it has become like haqq truth. And His statement:
h
And that they are negligent
, God Almighty says: And that they are left behind and abandoned in the Fire, forgotten in it.

x: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and most of them said something similar to what we said about this: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding this verse: There is no doubt that they will have the Fire and that they will be neglectful. He said: They will be forgotten and neglectful.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Zaid bin Habbab told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Bahz bin Asad told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Abu Bishr told me, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr,
m: the same.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
There is no doubt that they will have the Fire and that they will be neglected
, he said: They will be abandoned in the Fire, forgotten in it.

c: Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, Husayn said:
m: He told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And that they are neglectful, he said: forgotten.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us:
m: Abda, Abu Mu’awiyah, and Abu Khalid told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
h
And that they are negligent
. He said: They are abandoned in the Fire.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Al-Qasim, on the authority of Mujahid: Excessive he said:
m: forgotten.

c: Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Hussein, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And that they are excessive meaning: they are multiplied.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Badal told us: Ibad bin Rashid told us:
m: I heard Dawud bin Abi Hind, regarding the statement of God: And that they are neglectful, he said: They are forgotten in the Fire.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that they are hastening to the Fire and are heading towards it. They went in this to the saying of the Arabs: We have gone too far in seeking water if they have sent him to fix the buckets and the ropes, and to arrange what they need when they arrive at him, so he is farit. As for the one who is ahead himself, he is farit. It is said: So-and-so has gone ahead of his companions yafartuhum farut wa farut, if he has preceded them. The plural of farit is farat. From this is the saying of al-Qatami: They hastened us and they were among our companions, just as the camel hurried to its destination. And from this is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: I will precede you to the Cistern. That is, I will precede you to it and outpace you until you reach it.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And that they are the ones who are the most excessive meaning: they are hastening to the Fire.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And that they are excessive. He said: They have been excessive in the Fire: that is, they are hastening.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: they are banished to Hell.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Ash’ath Al-Samman, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed:
m: And that they are the ones who are the most neglectful. He said: They are humiliated and banished. The first of the sayings in this regard is the one we have chosen, which is that the excess that means precedence is only said of someone who precedes to correct what he is presented to until the time of the arrival of the one who preceded him to him, and he is not preceded by someone who precedes to the Fire from its people to correct something in it for a visitor who will come to it in it and agree with him as a reformer, but rather he precedes the one who precedes to it for a punishment that is hastened for him. So if the meaning of that excess that is the interpretation of hastening is corrupted, then it is not correct to have a face for its validity, then the other meaning is correct, which is the excess that means leaving behind and abandoning. This is because it is said of the Arabs: I did not leave behind anyone behind me, meaning I did not leave him behind, and I did not neglect him, meaning I did not leave him behind. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Egypt, Kufa and Basra, recited it as: And that they are excessive with a lightened or a fatha on the ra’, meaning that the doer of the word is not named, from exaggerated, so he is excessive. I have explained the difference in the recitation of this as well in the interpretation. Abu Ja’far al-Qari’ recited it as: And that they are excessive with a kasra on the ra’ and a shaddah on it, with the interpretation: that they are excessive in performing the duty that God had upon them in this world, of obeying Him and fulfilling His rights, neglecting that, from the statement of God the Most High: Oh, how I regret what I neglected in the side of God. Nafi’ ibn Abi Nu’aym recited: And that they are excessive with a kasra on the ra’ and a lightened one.

c: Yunus told me
m: this, on the authority of Warsh, on his authority, with the interpretation: that they are excessive in sins and transgressions, extravagant towards themselves and doing a lot of them, from their saying: So-and-so went too far in speech: if he exceeded his limit and went too far in it. Surat al-Nahl 16:62 And they attribute to God that which they hate, and their tongues describe falsehood, that they shall have the best [reward]. There is no doubt that they shall have the Fire, and that they are transgressors. The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of those whose reading we mentioned from the people of Iraq, because it agrees with the interpretation of the people of interpretation that we mentioned before, and the other readings depart from their interpretation.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their recitation of this.

The majority of the reciters of Egypt, Kufa and Basra, recited it as: And that they are excessive with a lightened or a fatha on the ra’, meaning that the doer of the word is not named, from exaggerated, so he is excessive.
I have explained the difference in the recitation of this as well in the interpretation.

Abu Ja’far al-Qari’ recited it as: And that they are excessive with a kasra on the ra’ and a shaddah on it, with the interpretation: that they are excessive in performing the duty that God had upon them in this world, of obeying Him and fulfilling His rights, neglecting that, from the statement of God the Most High: Oh, how I regret what I neglected in the side of God.

The most correct of the readings in this regard is the reading of those whose reading we mentioned from the people of Iraq, because it agrees with the interpretation of the people of interpretation that we mentioned before, and the other readings depart from their interpretation.

x: God Almighty says, swearing by Himself, the Exalted, the Majestic, to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: By God, O Muhammad, We have sent messengers before you to their nations with the same as We sent you to your nation, calling to the oneness of God, sincere worship of Him, submission to Him in obedience, and the rejection of rivals and gods. But Satan made their deeds seem attractive to them. He says: Satan made their disbelief in God and the worship of idols seem good to them, until they denied their messengers and rejected what they brought them from their Lord. So he is their protector today. He says: Satan is their supporter today in this world, and what a bad protector he is. And for them is a painful punishment. In the Hereafter, when they come before their Lord, Satan’s protectorship will not benefit them then, nor will it benefit them in this world, but rather it will harm them in it, and it will be more harmful to them in the Hereafter.

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We did not send down, O Muhammad, Our Book and sent you as a Messenger to Our creation except to make clear to them what they differed about in the religion of God, so that you may know what is correct in it, and what is true from what is false, and establish against them with what is correct in it the proof of God with which He sent you. And His statement:
h
And guidance and mercy for a people who believe

, meaning: And guidance as clarification from misguidance, meaning by that the Book, and mercy for a people who believe in it, so they believe in what is in it, and acknowledge what it includes of God’s commands and prohibitions, and act upon it. And the guidance is connected to the position of to clarify, because its position is accusative. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: And We have not sent down to you the Book except as clarification for the people concerning that in which they differed, as guidance and mercy.

God Almighty says, alerting His creation to His arguments against them in His Oneness, and that no divinity is appropriate except for Him, and that worship is not appropriate for anything other than Him: O people, your deity is the one to whom worship is due, above all else. He sent down water from the sky meaning: rain. He says: Then He caused to grow, with what He sent down from that water from the sky, the dead earth that has no plants, grass, or vegetation after its death after it was dead with nothing in it. Indeed in that is a sign. God Almighty says: Indeed in Our reviving the earth after its death with what We sent down from the sky of water is clear evidence and a conclusive argument that excuses whoever thinks about it. For a people who listen. He says: For a people who hear this statement, ponder it, understand it, and obey God in what He has guided them to.

God Almighty says: And indeed, O people, there is a lesson for you in the livestock which We give you drink from what is in their bellies. The reciters differed in the recitation of the phrase We will give you drink. The majority of the people of Mecca, Iraq, Kufa and Basra, except for Asim, and from the people of Medina Abu Jaʿfar read it as Nasqiyyum with a damma on the nun, meaning: He gave them a drink of milk. Al-Kisa'i used to say: The Arabs say: Asqaynahum nahrun, and asqaynahum laban, if they made it a drink of milk. So when they meant that they gave it a drink, they said: Nasqaynahum fa-na-na-qiyyum without an alif. The majority of the reciters of Medina, except for Abu Jaʿfar, and from the people of Iraq Asim read it as na-qayyum with a fatha on the nun from saqahullah, so he gives it to him. The Arabs sometimes include the alif in what is not a drink of drink of drink of drink, and they remove it from it, although the most famous of the two expressions according to them is what Al-Kisa'i said.

What we have said is indicated by the statement of Labid in describing the clouds: He watered my people, Bani Majd, and watered Namir and the tribes from the crescent moon. So he combined both languages in one meaning, so if that is the case, then whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct, except that the most amazing of the two readings is the reading with the damma of the noon, because I mentioned that most of the two speeches among the Arabs in what was permanent from watering is asqa with the alif, so he is yasqi, and what God watered His servants from the bellies of the livestock is permanent for them and not cut off from them. As for his saying: from what is in his bellies, he mentioned the livestock before that, and it is a plural, and the ha in the bellies is unified. The Arabs have sayings about that, so some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: the blessings and the livestock are one thing, because they are both plurals, so he returned the speech in his saying from what is in his bellies to the management, intending by it the meaning of blessings, since it was performed from the livestock, and he cites as evidence for his saying that the verse of some of the Bedouins: If you see stars from the lion's forehead or the dung beetle and the shoulder Bal Suhail in the scandal, so it spoiled, and the milk of the camel became good, so it cooled He says: He returned with his saying:
h
So he returned to the meaning of milk
, because milk and dairy products can have one meaning, and in reminding of blessings, the other said: Common food, yes, you turn it into a pollinator and produce it.

He mentioned the blessings, and others among them said: He only said from what is in their bellies because he meant: from what is in the bellies of what we mentioned, and he recites a rajaz poem by some of them about that: Like chickens, we pluck their crops. And the saying of Al-Aswad bin Ya’far: Fate and death both pay off the sins, they watch my blackness He said: Both of them, and he did not say: Both of them, and the saying of Al-Saltani Al-Abdi: Generosity and chivalry guaranteed a grave in Merv on the clear road. And the other said: Afraa is the person who is the least affectionate to me, and Afraa is the one who turns away from me and is lazy He did not say: the slow-moving one, and the other said: If people are people and the country is happy, and if Umm Ammar is a helpful friend He says: All of that is in the sense of this thing and this person and blackness, and the like. He says that from that is the saying of God Almighty And when he saw the sun rising, he said, This is my Lord meaning: this rising thing.

And His saying It is a reminder, so whoever wills may remember it and he did not say remember it, because its meaning is: whoever wills may remember this thing. And His saying (And indeed, I am sent to him as guidance, and I will see with what the messengers return. * So when Solomon came) and he did not say came.

Some of the Basrans used to say: From what is in their bellies because the meaning is: We give you drink from whatever livestock is in their bellies. He also said: The milk is implicit, meaning: He is given a drink from whatever has milk, because not all of them have milk, but rather he is given a drink from those that have milk. The first two sayings are more correct in their interpretation of the speech of the Arabs than this third saying. And His statement: from between excrement and blood, pure milk. He says: We give you milk to drink, which We bring forth for you from between excrement and blood, pure: He says: It is free from mixing with blood and excrement, so they do not mix with it. Permissible to those who drink it. He says: It is permissible for whoever drinks it, so he does not choke on it, as a choker chokes on some of the foods he eats. And it was said that no one has ever choked on milk.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the recitation of the phrase We will give you drink.

The majority of the people of Mecca, Iraq, Kufa and Basra, except for Asim, and from the people of Medina Abu Jaʿfar read it as Nasqiyyum with a damma on the nun, meaning: He gave them a drink of milk.
The majority of the reciters of Medina, except for Abu Jaʿfar, and from the people of Iraq Asim read it as na-qayyum with a fatha on the nun from saqahullah, so he gives it to him.

So he combined both languages in one meaning, so if that is the case, then whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct, except that the most amazing of the two readings is the reading with the damma of the noon, because I mentioned that most of the two speeches among the Arabs in what was permanent from watering is asqa with the alif, so he is yasqi, and what God watered His servants from the bellies of the livestock is permanent for them and not cut off from them.

x: God the Almighty says: And for you also, O people, is a lesson in what We give you to drink of the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines, from which you take intoxicant and good provision, along with what We give you to drink from the bellies of livestock, of milk that comes out from between the excrement and the blood. And the noun was omitted from His statement,
h
And of the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines
, and the meaning is what was described, which is:
h
And of the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines

, what you take, because of the indication of who is it, because the one who enters into the speech is hated, so he dispensed with its indication and the knowledge of the listeners of what is required by mentioning the noun with it. And some of the grammarians of Basra used to say in the meaning of the speech:
h
And of the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines

, something from which you take intoxicant, and he said: The ha’ was mentioned in His statement, you take from it, because it was intended to mean something, and in our view it refers to what was left out, which is what.
And His statement, you take is from the description of what was left out.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement,
h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision

Some of them said: What is meant by intoxicant is wine, and what is meant by good provision is dates and raisins. He said: This verse was revealed before wine was forbidden, then it was forbidden afterwards.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Ayoub bin Jaber Al-Suhaimi told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
. He said: Intoxicant is what is forbidden from its drink, and good provision is what is permissible from its fruit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ and Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ Al-Razi told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
. He said: Good provision is what is permissible of its fruit, and intoxicant is what is forbidden of its fruit.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Umar ibn Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Naim Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad Ibn Qays, who said:
m: I heard a man narrating on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse:
h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
. He said: Intoxicant is what is forbidden from their two fruits, and good provision is what is permissible from their two fruits.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Al-Hasan bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Ghassan told us, he said: Zuhair bin Muawiyah told us, he said: Al-Aswad bin Qais told us, he said: Amr bin Sufyan told me, he said:
m: I heard Ibn Abbas say, and this verse was mentioned to him: And from the fruits of the palm trees and the grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision. He said: Intoxicant is what is forbidden from them, and good provision is what is permissible from them.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Qais, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan Al-Basri, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
. He said: As for good provision, it is what is permissible of their fruit, and as for intoxicant, it is what is forbidden of their fruit.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hammani told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan Al-Basri, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
. He said: Intoxicant is its forbidden thing, and good provision is its permissible thing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Abbas bin Abi Talib told us, he said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Al-Aswad, on the authority of Amr bin Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Sugar is what is forbidden from their fruit, and good provision is what is permissible from their fruit.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Good sustenance, and intoxication: the forbidden.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr:
m: h
You take from it an intoxicant and good provision
. He said: What is forbidden of their fruit, and what is permissible of their fruit.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: Drunkenness is wine, and good sustenance is lawful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Misa’ar and Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Haseen, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: Good sustenance is lawful, and drunkenness is unlawful.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr,
m: regarding this verse:
h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
. He said: Intoxicant is what is forbidden, and good provision is what is permissible.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Abu Razin:
m: h
You take from it an intoxicant and good provision
. He said: This was revealed while they were drinking wine, so this was before the prohibition of wine was revealed.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: Al-Sha’bi, and Abu Razin. They said: It was abrogated in this verse:
h
You take from it an intoxicant and good provision

c: Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Abu Qatan told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: Al-Sha’bi, and Abu Razin, similarly.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You take from it an intoxicant and good provision
, he said: It was abrogated, abrogated by the prohibition of alcohol.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Hudha told us: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You take from it an intoxicant and good provision
, he said: God mentioned His blessing in intoxication before the prohibition of wine.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur and Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: Sugar is what God has forbidden, and sustenance is what God has permitted.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: Good sustenance is lawful, and intoxication is unlawful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, who said:
m: Good sustenance is lawful, and intoxication is unlawful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abu Kadina Yahya ibn al-Muhallab, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Sugar is wine, and good provision is dates and grapes.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sharik told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: You make an intoxicant from it. He said: It is wine before it was forbidden.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And
h
you take from it an intoxicant
he said: wine before it was forbidden. And good provision he said: food.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision

. As for intoxicant: it is the wine of these non-Arabs. As for good provision: it is what you make of wine, what you pickle, and what you eat. This verse was revealed and wine was not forbidden on that day, but rather its prohibition came after that in Surat Al-Ma’idah.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abda bin Sulayman told us:
m: I read to Ibn Abi Udhra, who said: This is how I heard Qatada:
h
You take from it an intoxicant and good provision
. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Bishr.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Sakra he said:
m: It is the wines of the Persians, and it was abrogated in Surat al-Ma’idah, and the good provision: He said: What you make fermented wine, pickle, and eat.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you make intoxicant and good provision. This is because the people used to call wine sakkar and they used to drink it. Ibn Abbas said: Men passed by Wadi al-Sakran where the Quraysh used to gather when they met their travelers when they came from Ash-Sham, and they would go with them and accompany them until they reached Wadi al-Sakran and then return from it. Then God called it wine after that when it was forbidden. Ibn Abbas used to claim that it was wine, and he used to claim that the Abyssinians used to call vinegar sakkar. Surat al-Nahl 16:67
h
And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision
h
Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason
. By this he meant: the permissible dates and raisins, and whatever was permissible does not intoxicate.

x: Others said: Sugar is like wine in terms of prohibition, but it is not wine. They said: It is the infusion of dates and raisins when it becomes strong and intoxicates the drinker.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam Ibn Bashir told us: Amr told us,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And from the fruits of the palm trees and grapevines you take intoxicant and good provision
, Ibn Abbas said: This was before the prohibition of wine was revealed, and intoxicant is forbidden like wine, but as for what is permissible from it, it is raisins, dates, vinegar, and the like.

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
You take from it an intoxicant

, then God forbade after that, meaning what was revealed in Surat Al-Baqarah of mentioning wine, gambling, idols, and arrows, intoxication along with the prohibition of wine because it is from it. He said, and good provision, so it is the permissible from vinegar and wine, and the like, so God approved it and made it permissible for the Muslims.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Musa:
m: He said: I asked once about sugar, so he said: Abdullah said: It is wine.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Farwa, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila, he said:
m: Sugar: wine.
b.via: Abu Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Laila

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Sugar: wine.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Hasan bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim and Abu Razin, they said:
m: Sugar is wine.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
You take from it intoxicant
meaning: what intoxicates from grapes and dates, and good provision meaning: its fruit.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
You take from it intoxicant and good provision
, he said: What was permissible was what was permissible until they changed it and made intoxicant from it.

x: Others said: Sugar is everything that is permissible to drink, such as permissible wine, vinegar, and dates. Good provisions include dates and raisins.
Who said that?

c: Dawud al-Wasiti told me, he said: Abu Usamah told us, Abu Rawq told me, he said:
m: I said to Shu’bi: What do you think of the words of God Almighty: You make from it intoxicant. Is this the intoxicant that the Nabataeans make? He said: No, this is wine. Rather, the intoxicant that God Almighty mentioned is wine and vinegar, and the good provision is dates and raisins.

c: Yahya bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Usama told us, he said:
m: Mujalid mentioned, on the authority of Amer, something similar.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Mandil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: You make from it intoxicant and good provision. He said: What they used to make from the palm trees is wine, and good provision is what they used to make from raisins and dates.

c: Ahmad told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Mandal told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: I said to him: What do you make sugar from? He said: They used to make it from wine and vinegar. I said: And good sustenance? He said: They used to make it from dates and raisins.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah and Ahmad ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: Sugar is wine, and good provision is the dates that were eaten. According to this interpretation, the verse has not been abrogated, rather its ruling remains the same. This interpretation, in my opinion, is the first of the sayings to interpret this verse, and that is because intoxication in the speech of the Arabs is in one of four ways: One of them: what intoxicates from the drink. The second: what is tasted from the food, as the poet said: I made the faults of the most generous people a sugar. Any taste. The third: stillness from the poet’s saying: Made the hot eye drunk We have explained this previously. Fourth: The source of their saying: So-and-so became intoxicated, he became intoxicated, he became intoxicated, he became intoxicated, he became intoxicated, he became intoxicated, if that is the case, and the intoxicating drink is forbidden, as we have shown in our book entitled: Latif al-Qawl fi Ahkam Shara’i’ al-Islam, and it was not permissible for us to say: It is abrogated, since the abrogated is that which the abrogating ruling negated, and that which the ruling and its abrogator cannot be combined with, and there was no evidence in the ruling of God, the Most High, mentioning that alcohol is forbidden, that intoxication, which is other than alcohol, and other than that which intoxicates from the drink, is forbidden, since intoxication was one of its meanings among the Arabs, and the one in whose tongue the Qur’an was revealed is everything that is tasted, and it was not with that, since there was no evidence in the revelation itself that it was abrogated, or a report from the Messenger that it was abrogated, nor did the nation agree on it, then it is obligatory to say what we said, that the meaning of intoxication in this place is: the intoxication of that which is permissible to drink, from that which is taken from the fruit of the palm tree and the vine, and it is invalid that its meaning is alcohol or that which intoxicates from the drink, and it is excluded from its meaning being Sugar itself, since sugar is not something that is made from palm trees and vineyards, and it does not mean stillness. And His statement:
h
Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reason

. He says: In what We have described to you of the blessings that We have given you, O people, of livestock, palm trees, and vineyards, there is a clear indication and a clear sign for a people who understand God’s arguments, and understand His admonitions, and take heed from them.

x: God Almighty says:
h
And your Lord inspired the bee

, O Muhammad, by inspiring it, Take for yourself in the mountains, houses, and in the trees, and in what they construct. Meaning: in what they build of roofs, so they raised it up with construction. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Marwan told us, on the authority of Ishaq al-Tamimi,
m: who is the son of Abi al-Sabah, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And your Lord inspired the bee
. He said: He inspired it with inspiration.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us:
m: It reached me, in his statement,
h
And your Lord inspired the bees
, he said: He cast into their souls.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told me, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of his companions,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And your Lord inspired the bees
, he said: He cast into their souls the idea of building houses in the mountains.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And your Lord inspired the bee

... to the verse, he said: He commanded it to eat from the fruits, and He commanded it to follow the ways of its Lord humbly. We have explained the meaning of suggestion and the differences of opinion among those who differed about it in the past with its evidence, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, as well as the meaning of his saying they erect. Ibn Zayd used to say about the meaning of they build a pergola:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement, they build trellises, he said: the vineyard.

x: God Almighty says: Then eat, O bee, of the fruits. And follow the ways of your Lord. He says: Then follow the paths of your Lord. Submissive. He says: Submissive to you. Submissiveness is the plural of submissive. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told us: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me: Abu Hudhayfah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God Almighty: So follow the ways of your Lord made easy for you, he said: No place you follow will be difficult for you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: So follow the ways of your Lord made easy. He said: Easy paths. He said: No place you take is difficult for you. According to this interpretation that Mujahid interpreted, easy is a description of the ways. The interpretation of his saying:
h
So follow the ways of your Lord with ease
. Easy for you means that the path you have taken will not be difficult for you. Then the alif and lam were dropped, so it was in the accusative case as a state.

x: Others said about this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
So follow the ways of your Lord in submission
: meaning obediently.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
So follow the ways of your Lord with submission

, he said: Submissive is that which is led and taken where its owner wants. He said: So they go out with the bees, taking them for pasture and going, and they follow them. And he recited, Have they not seen that We have created for them from what Our hands have made, livestock, so that they are their owners? And We have subdued them to them... the verse. According to this statement, submissive is a description of the bees, and both statements are not far from being correct in terms of their correctness. There are two possible explanations, except that we chose it to be a description of the paths because they are closer to them. And His statement,
h
There comes forth from their bellies a drink of varying colors
, God Almighty says: There comes forth from the bellies of the bees a drink, which is honey, of varying colors, because it contains white, red, and black, and other colors.

x: Ashar: different colors, such as white tending toward red. His saying,
h
In it is healing for people
The people of interpretation differed as to what the ha in his saying, in it, refers to.
Some of them said: It refers to the Qur’an, and that is what is meant by it.
Who said that?

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman told us: Al-Maharbi told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
In it is healing for people
. He said: In the Qur’an is healing.

x: Others said: Rather, it means honey.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
There comes forth from their bellies a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for people
, so in it is healing, as God Almighty said, from diseases. And he used to forbid the dispersal of bees, and the killing of them.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: “A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned that his brother had a stomach ache. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Go and give your brother honey to drink.’ Then he came to him and said: ‘It has only made him more severe.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Go and give your brother honey to drink, for God has spoken the truth and your brother’s stomach has lied.’ So he gave him honey to drink, and it was as if he had been freed from shackles.”

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: There emerges from their bellies a drink of varying colors in which there is healing for people. He said: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: There are two cures: honey is a cure for every illness, and the Qur’an is a cure for what is in the chest.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
In it is healing for people

honey. This statement: I mean the statement of Qatada, is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse, because his statement in it is in the context of the report about honey, so the ha is from the mention of honey, since it was in the context of the report about it, more deserving of it than anything else. And His statement,
h
Indeed in that is a sign for a people who give thought

. God Almighty says: Indeed in God bringing forth from the bellies of these bees: the different drink, which is a cure for people, is a clear indication and proof of the One who subjected the bees and guided them to eat the fruits that they eat, and to make the houses that they carve out of mountains, trees, and vines, and brought forth from their bellies what He brought forth of healing for people, that He is the One who has no equal, and that He should not have a partner, and that divinity is not valid except for Him.

x: God Almighty says: And God created you, O people, and brought you into existence, and you were nothing, not the gods that you worship besides Him, so worship the One who created you and none other. Then He takes you means: Then He takes you.
h
And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age

means: And among you is he who grows old, and reaches the most decrepit age, which is the worst of it. It is said about it: The man is decrepit and old, he is decrepit and lowly, and I am his decrepit one. And it was said: That he becomes like that in seventy-five years.

c: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Fazari told me: Muhammad bin Suwar told us: Asad bin Imran told us, on the authority of Saad bin Tarif, on the authority of Al-Asba’ bin Nabatah, on the authority of Ali,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit age

, he said: Seventy-five years. And His statement: So that he may not know anything after having known anything means: We return him to the worst part of life so that he may return ignorant as he was in his childhood and youth. After having known something means: So that he may not know anything after having known something in his youth, which was lost with age and he forgot, so he does not know anything of it, and his mind was stripped away, so that after having had a mind he does not understand anything. Indeed, God is Knowing and Competent means: God does not forget, nor does His knowledge change. He is Knowing of everything that was and will be, Competent over whatever He wills. He is not ignorant of anything, and nothing that He wills is beyond His power.

x: God the Almighty says: By God, O people, He has favored some of you over others in the provision that He has provided for you in this world. So what about those whom God has favored over others in what He has provided for them? They prefer their provision to those whom their right hands possess means: with the polytheists who own their kingdoms in what He has provided for them of money and wives. They are equal in it means: until they and their slaves are equal in that. God the Almighty says: They are not satisfied that they and their slaves should be equal in what He has provided for them, and they have made My slaves partners in My kingdom and authority. This is an example that God the Almighty has given for those who associate partners with God. It has been said: What He meant by that are those who said: The Messiah is the son of God from the Christians. And His statement:
h
Then do they deny the favor of God
God the Almighty says:
h
Then do they deny the favor of God

that He has bestowed upon these polytheists in the provision that He has provided for them in this world by associating others with God from His creation in His authority and kingdom? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, “
h
And God has favored some of you over others in provision

. So those who are favored will not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess,” meaning: They did not share their wealth and women with their slaves, so how can they share My slaves with Me in My authority? That is what His statement means,
h
Then do they deny the favor of God

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: This verse is about Jesus, son of Mary, meaning himself. Jesus is only a servant, so God says: By God, you do not associate your servants with those who are yours, so that you and they are equal, so how can you be pleased with me with what you are not pleased with for yourselves?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together,
m: Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement,
h
And their provision is provided for by those whom their right hands possess
, he said: Like the false gods with God, may He be exalted.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: “
h
And God has favored some of you over others in provision

. So those who are favored would not give their provision to those their right hands possess, so they are equal therein. So is it the favor of God that they deny?” This is an example that God has given. Is there anyone among you who shares his wife and bed with his slave, so that you equate God with His creation and His servants? If you are not satisfied with this for yourself, then God is more deserving of being exalted than you are with yourself, and do not equate anyone of His servants and creation with God.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Then those who are given preference will not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess. He said: This is the one who is given preference in wealth and love, and his servant does not share his wealth and his wife, saying: I am satisfied with that for God, and you are not satisfied with it for yourself, so you have made a partner for God in His kingdom and creation.

x: God Almighty says, And God is He who has made for you, O people, from among yourselves mates, meaning that He created from Adam his wife Eve, and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And God has made for you mates from among yourselves: meaning, God created Adam, then created his wife from him, then made for you sons and grandchildren.

x: The interpreters differed about the meaning of the grandchildren.
Some of them said: They are the two sisters, the two sisters of a man over his daughters.
Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us: Abaan bin Taghlib told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Ibn Habish, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: Sons and grandchildren. He said: The two sisters.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Warqa’a:
m: I asked Abdullah: What do you say about the grandchildren? Are they the man’s household, O Abu Abd al-Rahman? He said: No, but they are the two sisters.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us, and Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us, both of them said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Asim bin Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur bin Habish, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The grandchildren are the two sisters.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same. Ibn Bashar, Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi, Ibn Wakee’, Suwar ibn Abdullah al-Anbari, Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Kharash, and al-Hasan ibn Khalaf al-Wasiti told us:

c: Yahya ibn Saeed al-Qattan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, who said:
m: The grandchildren are the two sisters.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: The grandchildren are the two sisters.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Sons and grandchildren. He said: The grandchildren are the two sisters.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: The grandchildren are the son-in-law.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: The two sisters.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The two sisters.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: And grandchildren, he said: the in-laws.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, he said: Hammad told me, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Zur, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, he said:
m: The grandchildren are the two sisters.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi al-Najud, on the authority of Zur bin Hubaish, who said:
m: Abdullah bin Masoud said to me: Who are the grandchildren, O Zur? I said: They are the grandchildren of a man from his children and his children are his children. He said: No, they are the in-laws.

x: Others said: They are the man's helpers and servants.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash told me: Salim bin Qutaybah told me, on the authority of Wahb bin Habib al-Asadi, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: who was asked about his statement: sons and grandchildren. He said: Whoever helps you has given you grandchildren. Haven’t you heard the poet say: The grandchildren gathered around them and surrendered to the crisis of beauty in their hands Hanad told us:

c: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: sons and grandchildren, he said: The grandchildren are the servants.

c: Muhammad bin Khalid bin Khidash told me: Salim bin Qutaybah told me, on the authority of Hazim bin Ibrahim Al-Bajali, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: He said: The grandchildren are the servants. Surat al-Nahl 16:72 And God has made for you mates from among yourselves and has made for you from your mates sons and grandchildren and has provided for you from the good things. Is it then in falsehood that they believe and in the favor of God that they deny?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Imran bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Hisayn, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: They are those who help a man from among his children and servants.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: And grandchildren. He said: Grandchildren are those who serve you from among your children.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Salam bin Saleem, and Qais told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: They are the servants.

c: Ahmad told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Salam Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Khalid told me: Salamah told me, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement: sons and grandchildren, he said: Sons and grandchildren’s children, whoever helps you from family and servants has become your grandchild.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr bin Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: They are the servants. Muhammad bin Khalid, Ibn Wakee’, and Ya’qub bin Ibrahim told me:

c: Ismail bin Aliyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The grandchildren are the servants.

c: Ahmad bin Ishaq told us: Abu Ahmad told us, and Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, and Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us,
m: all on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Sons and grandsons he said: his son and his servant.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, sons and grandchildren, he said: Helpers, assistants, and servants.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Zama’a told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: The grandchildren are the servants.

c: Ibn Bashar told us
m: again, he said: His son and his servant.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: h
And He has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren
a profession that they will care for you and serve you from your children, an honor with which God has honored you.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Saddī, on the authority of Abu Malik:
m: The grandchildren, he said: the helpers.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hiseen, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: Those who help him.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement: sons and grandchildren, he said: The grandchildren are those who serve you from your children and your children’s children.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn al-Taymi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Hasan, he said:
m: The grandchildren are the servants.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Naim told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Sons and grandchildren he said: his children who help him.

x: Others said: They are the man’s son and his son is his son.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And grandchildren he said: They are the children and the children’s children.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: and Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: sons and grandchildren. He said: The grandchildren are the sons.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ghundar told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Abu Bakr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: Your children when they take care of you, support you, help you and serve you, Hamid said: The grandchildren surrounded them and surrendered to their hands the crisis of beauty Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
And He has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren

, he said: The grandchildren are the servants from the man’s children, they are his children, and they serve him. He said: And the slaves are not from the wives, how can a slave be from my husband? Rather, the grandchildren are the man’s children and his servants.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, in his statement, sons and grandchildren, meaning: a man’s children who serve him and serve him, and the Arabs were only served by their male children.

x: Others said: They are the sons of a man's wife from another man.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
And He has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren

, meaning: The sons of a man’s wife are not from him, and it is said: The grandchildren: the man who works for the man, he says: So-and-so is a grandchild for us, and some men claim that the grandchildren are the two sisters of a man. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God Almighty informed His servants of His blessings upon them, in what He has given them of wives and children, so He Almighty said: And God has made for you wives from among yourselves and has made for you from your wives sons and grandchildren.

c: So He informed them that
m: He has made for them from their wives sons and grandchildren. Grandchildren in the speech of the Arabs is the plural of Hafidh, just as Kadhbah is the plural of Kadhhab, and Fasqa is the plural of Fasiq. Hafid in their speech is the one who is light in service and work. Hafid is the lightness of work. It is said: The camel passed by Yahfid Hafidanan: if it passed by quickly in its pace. And from this is their saying: We run to you and hasten: meaning we hasten to work in your obedience. It is said from this: Hafid lahu yahfid Hafidan, Hafidun, and Hafidanan. And from this is the saying of the shepherd: She charged her unknown with Yemeni camels, if the camels were to be worn by the camels’ shepherds If the meaning of the grandchildren is what we mentioned, that they are those who hasten to serve a man and are light in it, and God, the Most High, has informed us that among the blessings He has bestowed upon us is that He has made for us grandchildren who will serve us, and our sons and wives who are fit to serve from us and from others, and our sisters who are the husbands of our daughters from our wives, and our servants from our slaves, if they serve us, then they deserve the name grandchildren, and God, the Most High, did not indicate by the apparent meaning of His revelation, nor on the tongue of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor by rational argument, that He meant by that a type of grandchildren, without a type of them, and He has bestowed all of that upon us, then it is not for us to direct that to a specific type of grandchildren and not a general type, except what the nation has agreed upon that it is not included among them. If that is the case, then all the sayings that we have mentioned from those we have mentioned have a way of being correct, and a way out in interpretation. However, what we have chosen is more correct than the saying, because of the evidence we have explained. And His statement:
h
And He has provided you with good things

means: And He has provided you with lawful sustenance, provisions, and sustenance. Then will they believe in falsehood? God Almighty says: Satan’s allies forbid them from the lakes, the swā’ib, and the wasā’il, so these polytheists believe in God. And in the favor of God they are ungrateful. He says: And in what God has made lawful for them of that, and has bestowed upon them by making it lawful. They are ungrateful. He says: They deny that it is lawful, and they deny that God has made it lawful.

x: God Almighty says: And they worship besides God that which possesses for them no provision from the heavens or the earth, nor are they able to do so.

God the Almighty says: And these polytheists worship, besides Him, idols that do not possess for them any provision from the heavens, because they are not able to send down rain from it to revive the dead of the earths. And the earth means: Nor does it possess for them any provision from the earth because it is not able to bring forth anything from its plants or fruits for them, nor anything of what God the Almighty has enumerated in this verse that He has bestowed upon them. And they are not able means: Nor do their idols possess anything from the heavens and the earth, rather they and everything in the heavens and the earth belong to God. And they are not able means: Nor are they able to do anything. His saying,
h
So do not make comparisons for God
, means:
h
So do not make comparisons for God
, and do not liken Him to similarities, for He has no likeness or resemblance. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: The examples are the similarities.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, So do not make for God any likenesses, meaning their taking idols, he says: Do not make with Me a god other than Me, for there is no god other than Me.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And they worship besides God that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens or the earth, nor are they able to do so, he said: These idols that are worshipped besides God do not possess for those who worship them any provision, nor harm, nor benefit, nor life, nor resurrection. And His statement,
h
So do not make comparisons for God

, for He is One, Eternal, Who did not beget, nor was He begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. Indeed, God knows, while you do not know, he says: God, O people, knows the error and correctness of what you represent and make of comparisons, and other than that of all other things, and you do not know what is correct from what is incorrect. The Arabists differed about the accusative in the word something.

x: Some of the Basrans said: It is accusative as a substitute for provision, and it means: They do not possess provision, little or much.

Some of the Kufians said: It places the accusative of something because provision falls upon it, as God Almighty said: Have We not made the earth a receptacle * For the living and the dead meaning: It suffices the living and the dead. Similar to this is God Almighty’s statement: Or feeding on a day of severe hunger an orphan near of kin * Or a needy person covered with dust He said: If provision were with the thing, it would have been permissible to lower it, Nothing from the heavens possesses provision for you, and similar to it is: Then the recompense is like that of the livestock that was killed.

God the Almighty says: And He has made for you, O people, a likeness of the disbeliever among His slaves, and the believer among them. As for the disbeliever: he does not act in obedience to God, nor does he do good, nor does he spend anything of his money in the way of God, because God has abandoned him, like the owned slave, who is not able to do anything so he spends it. As for the believer in God, he acts in obedience to God, and spends his money in His way, like the free man to whom God has given wealth, so he spends from it secretly and openly, saying: with the knowledge of the people and without knowledge. Are they equal? He says: Is the slave who does not own anything and is not able to do it equal, and this free man whom God has provided with good provision, so he spends as described? Likewise, the disbeliever who commits sins against God and disobeys His commands, and the believer who knows that he obeys Him, are not equal.
In a similar manner to what we said about that, some scholars said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “
h
God presents an example

: a slave owned by someone who has no power over anything.” This is an example that God presented for the disbeliever. He gave him wealth, but he did not do any good with it, nor did he work with it in obedience to God. God, the Most High, said, And whoever We have provided from Us with a good provision. So this believer, God gave him wealth, so he worked with it in obedience to God, and took it with gratitude, and knowledge of God’s right, so God rewarded him for what He provided him with a permanent and permanent provision for his family in Paradise. God, the Most High, said, Are they equal in comparison? By God, they are not equal.
h
Praise be to God
h
but most of them do not know

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A slave owned by someone who has no power over anything. He said: He is the disbeliever who does not act in obedience to God, nor does he spend good. And whom We have provided from Us with a good provision. He said: The believer obeys God in himself and his wealth.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, “
h
God sets forth an example

: a slave owned by someone who has no power over anything,” meaning: the disbeliever who is unable to spend money in the way of God, and whoever We have provided from Us with a good provision, he spends from it secretly and publicly, meaning the believer, and this example is about spending. And His saying:
h
Praise be to God
means: Complete praise is to God, purely and exclusively, without what you people call upon other than Him of idols, so praise Him and not them. And His saying:
h
But most of them do not know

means: The matter is not as you do, nor is the statement as you say. The idols have no hand or favor with them, so they should be praised for it. All praise is to God, but most of these disbelievers who worship them do not know that this is so, so they, in their ignorance of what they do and leave, make them partners with God in worship and praise. Mujahid used to say: God gave this example, and the other example after it is for Himself and the gods that are worshipped besides Him.

x: This is an example that God Almighty gave for Himself and the gods that are worshipped besides Him. God Almighty said: And God presents an example of two men, one of them dumb, unable to do anything. He means by that the idol that it does not hear anything, nor does it speak, because it is either carved wood, or manufactured copper, unable to benefit those who serve it, nor to ward off harm from them, and he is entirely dependent on his master. He says: And he is dependent on his cousin, his allies and his people, so likewise the idol is all on whoever worships it, he needs to carry it, put it down and serve it, like the mute among people who is not able to do anything, so he is all on his allies from his cousins and others. Wherever he turns it, it does not bring good.

Wherever he turns it, it does not bring good, because it does not understand what is said to it, and it is not able to express itself as it wants, so it does not understand, and it is not understood from it, so likewise the idol, it does not comprehend what is said to it, so it obeys the command of whoever commands it, and it does not speak, so it commands and forbids. God the Most High says: Is he equal to he who commands justice?

Meaning: Is this mute equal to his master who does not bring good wherever he turns, and he who is a speaker and a talker who commands the truth and calls to it, while He is God, the One, the Subduer, who calls His servants to His Oneness and obedience? He says: He, the Most High, is not equal to the idol whose description is as described. His saying,
h
And he is on a straight path
, means: And with his command to justice, he is on a path of truth in his call to justice, and his command to it is straight, he does not deviate from the truth, nor does he deviate from it.
The people of interpretation differed about the person for whom this example was given.
Some of them said something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: He has no power over anything. He said: It is the idol. Is he equal to one who commands justice? He said: God commands justice.
h
And he is on a straight path
. And this is what Mujahid used to say, except that he used to say: God also gave the first example for Himself and for the idol.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, A slave owned by someone who has no power over anything, and one whom We have provided from Us with a good provision, “Two men, one of whom is mute,” And whoever commands justice, he said: All of this is like the true God, and what is claimed besides Him is falsehood.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: And God presents an example of two men, one of whom was mute. He said: This is an example that God presented.

x: Others said: Rather, both examples are for the believer and the unbeliever, and this is a statement narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and we have mentioned the narration on his authority regarding the first example in its place.
As for the other example:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And God presents an example of two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, and he is a burden on his master... to the end of the verse. By the mute he means: the one who is a burden on his unbelieving master. And by His saying:
h
And whoever enjoins justice the believer

. And this example is in deeds. Al-Hasan bin Al-Sabah Al-Bazzar narrated: Yahya bin Ishaq Al-Sulayhini narrated: Hammad narrated: Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim narrated: Ibrahim narrated: Ikrimah narrated: Yaʿla bin Umayyah narrated: Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, “God sets forth a parable: a slave owned by a slave,” he said: It was revealed about a man from Quraysh and his slave. And regarding His statement, The parable of two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, until His statement,
h
and he is on a straight path

, he said: He is Uthman bin Affan. He said: The mute who does not bring any good wherever he is directed, that is the client of Uthman bin Affan. Uthman used to spend on him and take care of him and provide for him, and the other hated Islam and refused it and forbade him from giving charity and doing good, so it was revealed about them both. We chose the statement that we chose in the first example because the Almighty likened the disbeliever to the slave whose attributes He described, and likened the believer to the one whom He provided with good provision, so he spends from what He provided him secretly and openly, so it is not permissible for that to be an example for God, since God only likened the disbeliever who is not able to do anything to the fact that He did not provide him with provision from which he spends secretly, and the believer whom God guided to obey Him and guided him to the right path, so he does what pleases God, is like the free man for whom He has provided abundantly, so he spends from it secretly and openly, and God, the Almighty, is the Provider and not the one provided for, so it is not permissible to liken His favor and generosity to the one provided spending good provision. As for the second example, it is an example from Him, the Almighty, of the mute who is not able to do anything, and there is no doubt that among the disbelievers are those who have great wealth, and those who sometimes cause great harm through their corruption, so it is not possible for that which is not able to do anything, as God, the Almighty, said as an example for the one who has power over many things. If that is the case, then the most appropriate meaning is to represent what is not capable of anything, as God Almighty said, with the likeness of what is not capable of anything, and that idol that is not capable of anything, with the mute, all upon his Master who is not capable of anything, as He said and described.

x: God Almighty says: And to God, O people, is the kingdom of what is hidden from your sight in the heavens and the earth, apart from your gods that you call upon besides Him, and apart from everything else besides Him. No one owns that except Him. And the matter of the Hour will not be but as the blink of an eye. He says: And the matter of the Resurrection and the Hour in which creation will be resurrected to stand in the place of Resurrection will not be but as a glance of an eye, because that is only when it is said to it: Be, and it is.

c: As Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Except for the blink of an eye, or even closer. And the Hour: is like the blink of an eye, or even closer.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And the matter of the Hour will not be but as the twinkling of an eye. He said: It is that He says: Be, and it is as the twinkling of an eye, so the matter of the Hour will be as the twinkling of an eye or even closer, meaning He says: or it is closer than the twinkling of an eye. His saying: God is capable of all things means: God is capable of establishing the Hour in the blink of an eye, and of doing whatever He wills of all things. Nothing He wills is impossible for Him.

x: God the Most High says: And God taught you what you did not know after He brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, you neither reasoned nor knew anything, so He provided you with minds with which you understand and with which you distinguish good from evil, and with which you see what you did not see before, and He gave you hearing with which you hear sounds, so some of you understand from others what you converse with among yourselves, and sight with which you see people, so you get to know each other, and with which you distinguish some from others.
