And hearts: He says: And the hearts with which you know things, so you memorize them, and think and understand with them. That you may be grateful: He says: We did that to you, so thank God for what He bestowed upon you of that, without the gods and rivals, so you made partners for Him in gratitude, and He had no partner in what He bestowed upon you of blessings. His statement:
h
And God brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers not knowing a thing is an endless statement

. Then the story began, and it was said: And God gave you hearing, sight, and hearts. We only said that because God, the Most High, mentioned, made worship, hearing, sight, and hearts before He brought them forth from the wombs of their mothers. He only gave them knowledge and reason after He brought them forth from the wombs of their mothers.

God Almighty says to these polytheists: Have you not seen, you polytheists, the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? Meaning: in the atmosphere of the sky between it and the earth, as Ibrahim bin Imran Al-Ansari said: Woe to her mother from the air of the atmosphere, she is not sought after like that which is on earth Meaning: In the air of the sky None holds them up except God He says: Their flight in the air is only by God, and by His subjugation of them in that, and if He took away from them what He gave them of flight, they would not be able to rise high. And His statement
h
Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe He says

: Indeed in God’s subjugation of the birds, and His enabling them to fly in the air of the sky, there are signs and indications that there is no god but God alone, with no partner, and that idols and statues have no share in divinity for a people who believe meaning: for a people who acknowledge the existence of what their eyes witness and their senses sense. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, subjected in the atmosphere of the sky: meaning in the middle of the sky.

x: God Almighty says: And God has made for you, O people, from your houses, which are made of stone and mud, a place of residence, in which you reside during your stay in your homes and countries. And He has made for you from the hides of livestock, houses, which are the houses made of carpets and pavilions made of hair, wool, and fur. Which you find light, He says: You find light carrying and transporting, on the day of your departure, from your countries and cities for your travels, and on the day of your settlement, in your countries and cities, and from their wool, fur, and hair, furnishings. And similar to what we said about the meaning of dwelling, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: From your houses as a dwelling place, he said: You live in it.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. As for poetry, it is poetry whose first letter is heavy or light, and the singular of poetry is hair. As for furniture, it is the furnishings of the house, and it has not been heard of as having a singular, and it does not have a singular like furnishings. It has been reported from some grammarians that he used to say: The singular of furniture is its furnishings, and I have not seen the people of knowledge of the Arabic language know that. And among the evidence that furniture is furnishings is the saying of the poet: The caravans stirred you up when they appeared with this beautiful furniture It is narrated: In Dhi Al-Zayy, and I see the origin of furniture is the gathering of some goods together until the hair of the Atith increases, which is the abundant and damaged hair. It is said from it, the hair of so-and-so increases, if it increases, intertwines, and gathers together. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying furniture means by furniture: money.

c: Muhammad bin Omar told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty furniture, he said: goods.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Furnishings he said:
m: It is money.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah bin Harb Al-Razi told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, on the authority of Hamid bin Abd Al-Rahman,
m: regarding his statement: furniture, he said: clothing. His saying:
h
And provision for a time means that He made that a provision for them
, so that they would be provided with it and be satisfied with it until their appointed time for death.

c: As Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And provision for a time, meaning: adornment. He says: They benefit from it for a time.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And provision for a time he said: until death.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And provision for a time means a term and a language.

x: God Almighty says: And among the blessings of God upon you, O people, is that He made from what He created of trees and other things shades under which you may seek shelter from the intense heat. It is the plural of shade. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
From what He created shadows
, he said: trees.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And God has made for you, from what He has created, shades. Yes, by God... from trees and other things. And His saying:
h
And He made for you in the mountains places of refuge
. He says: And He made for you in the mountains places in which you live, and it is the plural of kun.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And He has made for you shelters in the mountains
means: shelters in the mountains to live in. And He has made for you
h
garments to protect you from the heat
meaning cotton, linen, and woolen clothing and shirts.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And He made for you garments to protect you from the heat of cotton
, linen, and wool.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Garments to protect you from the heat
. He said: Cotton and linen. His saying:
h
Garments that protect you from your violence
means: And armor that protects you from your violence. Violence is war, and the meaning is: The weapons protect you from your violence from reaching you.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And garments to protect you from your violence from this iron.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And garments to protect you from your violence. He said: They are garments of iron. And His statement:
h
Thus does He perfect His favor upon you that you may submit

. The Most High says: Just as your Lord has given you these things that He has described in these verses as a favor from Him to you, so He perfects His favor upon you that you may submit. He says: So that you may submit to God in obedience, and your souls may humble themselves in believing in His Oneness, and you may devote your worship to Him alone. It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to recite perhaps you may submit with the opening of the ta’.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad told us, he said: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hanzala, on the authority of Shahr ibn Hawshab, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas used to say: Perhaps you will be safe. He said: He meant from wounds.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim bin Salam told us: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Hanzala Al-Sadosi, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: that he recited it, Perhaps you will be safe from wounds. Ahmad bin Yusuf said: Abu Ubaid said: He meant with the opening of the ta’ and the lam. The interpretation of the speech according to this reading of Ibn Abbas is: Thus He completes His favor upon you by making for you
h
garments that protect you from your violence
, that you may be safe from weapons in your wars. The reading that I do not permit is the reading other than it with the damma of the ta’ in His saying:
h
Perhaps you will be safe and the kasra of the lam in I have submitted

, you will be safe, O this one, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions on it. The interpretation of the speech according to this reading of Ibn Abbas is: Thus He completes His favor upon you by making for you
h
garments that protect you from your violence
, that you may be safe from weapons in your wars. The reading that I do not permit is the reading other than it with the damma of the ta’ in His saying:
h
Perhaps you will be safe and the kasra of the lam in I have submitted
, you will be safe, oh this, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions on it.

q.l: If someone were to say to us:
x: How did He make for you
h
garments to protect you from the heat

, and specifically mention the heat and not the cold, and they protect from the heat and the cold? Or how was it said: And He made for you shelters in the mountains and left out mentioning what He made for them in the plains?

a.l: It would be said to him:
x: There is disagreement about the reason for which the revelation came in this way, and we will mention what was said about that, then we will indicate the most correct of the sayings about that.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani
m: regarding this matter: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Muhammad bin Katheer told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Ata’, on the authority of his father, he said: The Qur’an was revealed according to the extent of their knowledge. Do you not see the statement of God Almighty, And God has made for you, from what He has created, shades and has made for you shelters in the mountains. And what He has made for them of the plains is greater and more, but they were people of mountains. Do you not see His statement, And of their wool and their fur and their hair is furnishings and provision for a time. And what He has made for them of other things is greater and more, but they were people of fur and hair. Do you not see His statement, And He sends down from the sky, from mountains, hail. They are amazed by that, and what He sent down of snow is greater and more, but they did not know about it. Do you not see His statement,
h
Garments to protect you from the heat

. And what protects from the cold is greater and more, but they were people of heat. So the reason why God Almighty singled out garments as protecting from the heat and not the cold according to this statement is that those addressed by that were people of heat, so God Almighty mentioned His blessing upon them with what would protect them from the harm that they were in. They knew that it was disliked, but they did not know the extent of the dislike, and the same applies to all other letters.

x: Others said: He mentioned that specifically because mentioning one of them was sufficient to mention the other, since it was known to those addressed by it that its meaning was: And the garments that protect from the heat also protect from the cold. They said: That is present in the speech of the Arabs, used, and they cited as evidence for their statement the words of the poet: I do not know, if I set my face towards goodness, which of the two is more suitable for me. He said: Which one is more suitable for me: he wants good or evil. He only mentioned good if he wants good, so he avoids evil. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of those who said: The people were addressed according to their level of knowledge, even though mentioning some of that indicates what was left out, for those who know what was mentioned and what was left out. This is because God Almighty mentioned only the number of His blessings that He bestowed upon those intended to be mentioned in this surah and not others, so He mentioned His favors to them.

evidence.text: Ahmad bin Yusuf told us: Al-Qasim bin Salam told us: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Hanzala Al-Sadosi, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he recited it, Perhaps you will be safe from wounds.

The interpretation of the speech according to this reading of Ibn Abbas is: Thus He completes His favor upon you by making for you garments that protect you from your violence, that you may be safe from weapons in your wars.

The reading that I do not permit is the reading other than it with the damma of the ta’ in His saying: Perhaps you will be safe and the kasra of the lam in I have submitted, you will be safe, O this one, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions on it.

The interpretation of the speech according to this reading of Ibn Abbas is: Thus He completes His favor upon you by making for you garments that protect you from your violence, that you may be safe from weapons in your wars.

The reading that I do not permit is the reading other than it with the damma of the ta’ in His saying: Perhaps you will be safe and the kasra of the lam in I have submitted, you will be safe, oh this, due to the consensus of the proof from the readers of the regions on it.

x: God Almighty says: But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear notification.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: If these polytheists, O Muhammad, turn away from the truth with which I sent you to them, and do not respond to you and turn away from it, then there is no blame or reproach upon you, because you have done what was required of you in that regard. All you have to do is convey to them what you were sent with. What He means by His statement: the clear is the one who makes clear to whoever hears it so that they understand it. As for his saying:
h
They recognize the blessing of God and then deny it
, the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the blessing that God Almighty informed these polytheists about, that they deny it, despite their knowledge of it.
Some of them said: It is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, whose prophethood they recognized and then denied and called him a liar.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: They recognize the blessing of God, then they deny it. He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Suddi,
m: the same.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they know that the blessings that God Almighty mentioned in this Surah are from God, and that God is the One who bestowed them with that, but they deny that, and claim that they inherited it from their fathers.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: They recognize the favor of God, then they deny it. He said: It is the dwellings and the livestock and what they are provided with from them, and the garments of iron and clothing. The infidels of Quraysh recognize this, then they deny it by saying: This was for our fathers, so let us live on it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: in a similar manner, except that he said: They inherited it from us, and he added to the hadith on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Jurayj said: So Abdullah bin Kathir: They know that God created them and gave them what He gave them, so it is their knowledge of His blessing, then their denial of it is their disbelief afterwards.

x: Others said about that, what:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Awn ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah:
m: They recognize the blessing of God, then they deny it. He said: Their denial of it is that a man says: If it were not for so-and-so, such-and-such would not have happened, and if it were not for me, I would not have attained such-and-such.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is that if the infidels are asked: Who provided for you? They acknowledge that it is God who provided for them, then they deny that by saying: We were provided with that through the intercession of our gods. The first of the sayings in this regard that is correct, and most similar to the interpretation of the verse, is the saying of those who said: What is meant by the blessing that God mentioned in His statement:
h
They recognize the favor of God is the blessing upon them by sending Muhammad

, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them calling them to His mission by calling them to Him. This is because this verse is between two verses, both of which are reports about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and about what he was sent with. So what is most likely between them is to be in the meaning of what came before it and what came after it, since there was no meaning indicating its turning away from what came before it and what came after it.

What came before this verse is His statement: “But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear notification. * They will recognize the favor of God, then they will deny it” and what comes after it is And the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness who is its Messenger. If that is the case, then the meaning of the verse is: These polytheists recognize the favor of God upon them, O Muhammad, by you, then they deny it Surat al-Nahl 16:83 They recognize the favor of God, then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers. and reject your prophethood. And most of them are disbelievers means: And most of your people are those who deny your prophethood, not those who acknowledge it.

God Almighty says: They recognize the blessing of God, then they deny it today and reject it. And on the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness, who is the witness over them for what they answered God’s caller, and he is their Messenger who was sent to them. Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, meaning: Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved to apologize, so they apologize for what they used to disbelieve in God and His Messenger. Nor will they be asked to repent, so they will abandon returning to this world, so they will repent and turn back. This is as God Almighty said: This is a Day on which they will not speak, nor will permission be given to them to apologize. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness
, and its witness is its prophet, that he has conveyed the messages of his Lord. God Almighty said, And We have brought you as a witness over these.

x: God Almighty says: And when those who denied you, O Muhammad, and rejected your prophethood, and the nations who followed the path of the polytheists of your people, see the punishment of God, nothing will save them from the punishment of God, because they will not be given permission to apologize, and the punishment will not be lightened for them by the excuse they claim. Nor will they be reprieved. He says: Nor will they be reprieved by the punishment, because the time for repentance and turning back has passed, so that is not the time for them, but rather it is the time for the reward for deeds, so no reprieve will be given to reproach in order to be reprieved by repentance.

God Almighty says: And when the polytheists see on the Day of Resurrection what they used to worship besides God of gods and idols and other things, they will say: Our Lord, these are our partners in disbelief in You, and the partners whom we used to call gods besides You. God Almighty says: Then throw them away, meaning: their partners whom they used to worship besides God Almighty. He says: They will say to them: You are indeed liars, O polytheists. We did not call you to worship us. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: So cast the word to them, he said: Tell them.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

x: God the Almighty says: And the polytheists will submit to God on that Day in submission. He says: They will surrender on that Day and be humbled by His judgment over them, and their gods which they used to call upon in this world besides God will not avail them, nor will their people or their clans who used to defend them in this world. The Arabs say: I submitted to him so-and-so, meaning I said to him. And His statement:
h
And what they used to invent will be lost to them
, means: And what they hoped for from their gods to intercede with God for salvation will be lost to them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And they will submit to God on that Day
, meaning: they will be humbled and surrendered on that Day,
h
and what they used to invent will be lost to them

x: God Almighty says: Those who denied, O Muhammad, your prophethood and called you a liar in what you brought them from your Lord, and turned away from belief in God and His Messenger, and whoever wanted it, We will increase their punishment on the Day of Resurrection in Hell, on top of the punishment they were in before they were increased. And it was said: That increase that God promised them would be scorpions and snakes.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: We increased their punishment upon their punishment. He said: Scorpions with fangs like palm trees.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah and Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah:
m: We increased their punishment upon their punishment. He said: They were increased by scorpions with fangs like tall palm trees.

c: Ibrahim bin Yaqoub Al-Jawzjani told us: Jaafar bin Awn told us: Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Abdullah bin Marra, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Israel told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: We increased their punishment upon their punishment. He said: Snakes.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Al-Saddī, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who said:
m: Snakes in the fire.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: the same.

c: Mujahid bin Musa and Al-Fadl bin Al-Sabah told us: Jaʿfar bin ʿAwn told us: Al-Aʿmash told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of ʿUbayd bin ʿUmair, who said:
m: Hell has pits in which there are snakes the size of camels and eagles the size of black mules. The people of Hell cry out to those pits or to the shore, and they leap at them and seize them by their lips and their blades to their feet. They cry out to the Fire from it and say: The Fire, the Fire. It follows them until it feels its heat and then returns. He said: And it is in swarms.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Huyayy ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, he said:
m: Hell has coasts in which there are snakes and scorpions with necks like the necks of camels. And His saying: Because they were corrupting means: We increased that punishment upon what they had of punishment because of what they were corrupting, because they were disobeying God in this world and ordering His servants to disobey Him. That was their corruption. O God, we ask You for well-being, O Owner of this world and the everlasting Hereafter.

x: God Almighty says, And the Day We will raise up in every nation a witness over them from among themselves. He says: We will ask their prophet whom We sent to them to call to obedience to Us. He said, from among themselves, because God Almighty used to send prophets to nations, from among them, what did they answer you, and what did they respond to you with. And We have brought you as a witness over these. He says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We have brought you, O Muhammad, as a witness over your people and your nation to whom I sent you, regarding what they answered you, and what they did with what I sent you to do. And His statement,
h
And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things

, meaning: He sent down to you, O Muhammad, this Qur’an as clarification for all that people need of knowledge of what is lawful and what is unlawful, reward and punishment, and guidance from misguidance, and mercy for whoever believes in it and acts according to what is in it of God’s limits, His commands and prohibitions, so he makes lawful what He has made lawful and makes unlawful what He has made unlawful, and good tidings for the Muslims, meaning: And good tidings for whoever obeys God and submits to Him in monotheism, and submits to Him in obedience, giving him good tidings of His abundant reward in the Hereafter and His great honor.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, he said: Abaan bin Taghlib told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
An explanation of everything
he said:
m: of what is permissible and what is forbidden.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Abaan bin Taghlib, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: clarifying everything of what was permitted to them and what was forbidden to them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
An explanation of everything
, he said: What he commanded and what he forbade.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things
, he said: What they were commanded to do and what they were forbidden from doing.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of a man, he said: Ibn Mas’ud said:
m: All knowledge was revealed in this Qur’an, and everything has been explained to us in the Qur’an, then he recited this verse.

evidence.text: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Muhammad bin Fadil told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of a man, he said: Ibn Mas’ud said: All knowledge was revealed in this Qur’an, and everything has been explained to us in the Qur’an, then he recited this verse.

x: God Almighty says: God commands in this book that He sent down to you, O Muhammad, justice, which is fairness. Part of fairness is acknowledging the One who bestowed His blessings upon us, thanking Him for His favors, and giving praise to those who are worthy of it. If that is justice, and the idols and statues do not have a hand in our view that deserves praise, then it is ignorance of us to praise and worship them, while they do not bestow blessings so that we should be thanked, nor do they benefit so that we should be worshipped. So it is necessary for us to bear witness that there is no god but God alone, with no partner for Him. Therefore, whoever said justice in this context said: bearing witness that there is no god but God.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me:
m: They said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, God commands justice and doing good, he said: The testimony that there is no god but God. And his saying, and goodness, the goodness that God Almighty commanded, along with the justice whose characteristic we have described, is patience for God’s sake in obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden, in hardship and ease, in difficulty and in pleasure, and that is performing His obligations.

c: As Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me, they said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And goodness means: performing the obligatory duties. His saying,
h
And giving to relatives
, means:
h
And giving to relatives
the right that God has made obligatory upon you because of kinship and blood relations.

c: As Al-Muthanna and Ali told me, they said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And giving to relatives
meaning: the wombs. And his saying,
h
And forbids immorality
, he said: Immorality in this context means adultery.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And He forbids immorality, meaning: adultery. We have explained the meaning of immorality with its evidence in what came before. And his saying: And oppression. It was said: What is meant by oppression in this place is arrogance and injustice.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And transgression means arrogance and injustice. The root of transgression is to transgress and exceed the limit and the extent of everything, and we have explained that previously. And His saying, He admonishes you that you may remember, means: O people, your Lord reminds you so that you may remember, so that you may repent to His commands and prohibitions, and recognize the truth for its people.

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: He admonishes you means: He advises you, that you may remember. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah that he used to say in interpreting that: The meaning of justice in this context is the equality of the secret and the public of every worker for the sake of God, and the meaning of ihsan is that his secret is better than his public, and that indecency and evil are that his public is better than his secret.

c: It was reported on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud
m: that he used to say about this verse: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj told us, he said: Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, he said: I heard Mansur bin Al-Nu’man, on the authority of Amer, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl, he said: I heard Abdullah say: The most comprehensive verse in the Qur’an is in Surat al-Nahl 16:Indeed, God commands justice, doing good, and giving to kith and kin... to the end of the verse.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Shatir bin Shakl, who said:
m: I heard Abdullah say: The most comprehensive verse in the Qur’an for good or evil is the verse in Surat al-Nahl 16:Indeed, God commands justice and doing good... the verse.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, God commands justice, the doing of good, and liberality to kith and kin... the verse, that there is no good character trait that all the people of ignorance practiced and approved of, except that God commanded it, and there is no bad character trait that they used to taunt each other about, except that God forbade it and presented it. Rather, He forbade the basest and most reprehensible morals.

x: God the Almighty says: And fulfill the covenant of God when you have confirmed it, and His contract when you have made it, and have imposed upon yourselves a right for whomever you have made a covenant with and have made a covenant with.
h
And do not break oaths after confirming them

. He says: And do not contradict the matter in which you have contracted oaths, meaning after you have confirmed the oaths upon yourselves, so that you break your oaths and lie in them, and break them after you have fulfilled them. It is said from this: So-and-so confirmed his oath, confirming it, if he strengthened it, and this is the language of the people of Hijaz. As for the people of Najd, they say: I confirmed it, I confirm it, confirming. And His statement:
h
And you have made God a guarantor over you

. He says: And you have made God, by fulfilling what you have contracted upon yourselves, a shepherd who watches over those among you who fulfill the covenant of God that he has promised to fulfill and those who break it.
In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, with differences among themselves, about who this verse refers to and in what it was revealed.
Some of them said: It refers to those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Islam, and it was revealed about them.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amara al-Asadi told me: Abdullah ibn Musa told us: Abu Laila told us, on the authority of Buraydah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant

, he said: This verse was revealed regarding the pledge of allegiance to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Those who had accepted Islam had pledged allegiance to Islam, and they said,
h
And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant

, this is the pledge that you had pledged to Islam, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, the pledge. So do not let the small number of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and the large number of polytheists, lead you to break the pledge that you had pledged to Islam, even though there were few of them, and the polytheists were many among them.

x: Others said: It was revealed regarding the oath that the polytheists had made in the pre-Islamic era, and God Almighty commanded them in Islam to fulfill it and not break it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
And do not break oaths after confirming them
, he said: Making them stronger in swearing.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Bishr told me, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And do not break oaths after confirming them
, meaning: after emphasizing and making them more severe.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: These were people who were allies of a people who had made an alliance and some of them had given a covenant, then a people came to them and said: We are more numerous, more powerful and more powerful, so break the covenant with these people and return to us, so they did, and that is the saying of God Almighty: And do not break oaths after their confirmation,
h
and you have made God a guarantor over you

, that one nation is more numerous than another nation, more numerous because these people were more numerous than those people, you broke the covenant between you and these people, so this was in this.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, he said: Nafi’ bin Yazid told us, he said:
m: I asked Yahya bin Saeed, about the statement of God, And do not break oaths after their confirmation, he said: Covenants. The correct thing to say about this is that God the Most High commanded His servants in this verse to fulfill the covenants they make upon themselves, and He forbade them from breaking the oaths after confirming them upon themselves to others, with contracts that are between them in truth, which God does not dislike. It is possible that it was revealed about those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbidding them from breaking their allegiance, out of caution against the small number of Muslims and the large number of polytheists, and that it was revealed about those who wanted to transfer their alliance from their allies due to Surat al-Nahl 16:91 And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made it, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, although you have made God a guarantor over you. Indeed, God knows what you do. their small number to others due to their large number. It is possible that it was for something else, and there is no report that proves the argument that it was revealed about one of these and not another, and there is no indication in the Book or rational argument as to which of these it meant, and no statement about this is more worthy of the truth than what we have said due to its apparent indication of it, and that the verse was revealed for a reason, and the ruling with it is general in everything that was in the meaning of the reason for which it was revealed.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And you have made God a guarantor over you

. He said: A trustee. And His statement, Indeed, God knows what you do, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: Indeed, God, O people, knows what you do in the covenants that you pledge to God to fulfill, and the oaths and oaths that you affirm upon yourselves, whether you are righteous in them or break them, and other than that of your actions. He has examined all of that against you, and He will question you about it and about what you did in it. He says: So beware of God lest you meet Him having disobeyed His command and prohibition in them, and thereby deserve from Him what you cannot bear of His painful punishment.

x: God the Almighty says, forbidding His servants from breaking oaths after confirming them, and commanding the fulfillment of covenants, and illustrating the one who breaks that with the one who breaks her spinning after tightening it, and the one who breaks it after perfecting it: And do not be, O people, in breaking your oaths after confirming them and giving God the covenants and agreements, like the one who breaks her spinning after it has become strong. Meaning: after tightening it.
Some of the Arab scholars used to say: Strength is what is spun at one speed and not doubled. It was said that the one who used to do that was a foolish woman known in Mecca.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Abdullah bin Katheer told me:
m: Like the one who undoes her spinning after it was strong. He said: A clumsy woman was in Mecca, undoing it after twisting it.

c: Al-Muthanna told us: Ishaq told us: Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Sadaqah, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: And do not be like the one who untwists her spun thread after it was strong, using your oaths as a means of deception between you. He said: She was a woman in Mecca who, when she had spun her thread, would untwist it.

x: Others said: This is a parable that God gave for someone who broke a covenant, so He likened him to a woman who does this action. They said, in the meaning of she unraveled her spinning after it had been strong, something similar to what we said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And do not be like she who untwists her yarn after it has been strong

, into separate parts. If you heard of a woman untwisting her yarn after it had been tightly spun, you would say: How foolish she is! This is an example that God has given for someone who breaks his covenant.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And do not be like the one who undoes what she has spun after it has become strong. He said: Her spinning is her rope, she undoes it after she has twisted it, and she does not benefit from it after that.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Like the one who untwists her spinning after it had become strong. He said: She untwisted her rope after it had been made strong.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And be not like she who untwists her spun thread after it had become strong, he said: This is a parable that God has given to one who breaks the covenant that he gave them. God has given this parable to him like the one who spun and then untwisted what he had spun. She gave them something and then went back, so she broke the covenant that she had given them. And His statement, unwound, means: ruins. And everything that is untwisted after spinning is ankath. The singular is nakath, whether it is a rope or a yarn. It is said from it: So-and-so unwound this rope, so he unwound it, a breaking. And the rope is unwound if its strength is broken. And what is meant by it in this place is the breaking of a covenant and a contract. And His statement,
h
You take your oaths as a means of deception among you

, lest one nation should be more numerous than another nation, the Most High says: You make your oaths, which you swear that you will fulfill your covenant with those you have made, a means of deception among you, meaning: deception and illusion, so that they may feel secure with you, while you are harboring treachery towards them, and abandoning the fulfillment of the covenant, and transferring from them to others because others are more numerous than them. Deception in the speech of the Arabs: every matter that is not correct, from which it is said: I know the deception of so-and-so and his deception, and the deception of his matter and his deception and his secret. As for his saying:
h
That one nation is more plentiful than another nation

, his saying more plentiful is derived from usury. It is said: This is more plentiful than this and more plentiful than it, if it is more than it. From this is the saying of the poet: And my steps are dark, as if my heels were the seeds of reeds, and I am more than ten cubits long. It is said: So-and-so has taken usury from this, and that is because of the increase that he gives to his creditor on top of his capital. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
That one nation should be more numerous than another nation
, meaning: more numerous.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
That one nation should be more numerous than another nation
means: People more numerous than people.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement:
h
That one nation should be more numerous than another nation

, he said: They used to make alliances with allies, and they would find that they were more numerous and more powerful than them, so they would break the alliance of these and make alliances with those who were more powerful than them, so they were forbidden from doing that.
Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ishaq told us: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid.

c: Al-Qasim told me: Al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jarj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
You take your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves
means: treachery and betrayal among yourselves.
h
That one nation should be more numerous than another nation
means that one people should be more powerful and numerous than another.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Abu Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They entered between you he said:
m: Treachery between you.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
You take your oaths as a means of deception between you

, he deceives with it, he gives him a covenant that makes him feel secure, and he brings him down from his place of safety, so his foot slips while he is in safety, then he returns intending to betray him, he said: The first Bedouins of this were a people who were allies of a people who had made an alliance, and some of them gave each other a covenant, then a people came to them and said: We are more numerous, stronger and more powerful, so break the covenant of these people, and return to us, so they did, and that is the statement of God Almighty: And do not break oaths after their confirmation, while you have made God a guarantor over you “lest there be a nation more numerous than a nation” more numerous: more numerous because these were more numerous than those, you broke the covenant between you and these, so this was in this, and the other matter was in the one who makes a covenant with him, so he brings him down from his fortress, then breaks it, the first verse is in these people, and it is its beginning, and the other is in this.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: Concerning His statement:
h
That one nation should be more numerous than another nation

, he said: More, he said: So you must fulfill the covenant. And His statement: God is only testing you with it means, the Most High said: God is only testing you by His command to you to fulfill God’s covenant when you make a covenant, so that He may distinguish the obedient among you who abides by His command and prohibition from the disobedient who disobeys His command and prohibition. And He will make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ means, the Most High said: And your Lord will make clear to you, O people, on the Day of Resurrection when you come to Him by rewarding each group of you for their deeds in this world, the good among you for his goodness, and the evildoer for his evil, that over which you used to differ. And that over which they used to differ in this world was that the believer in God would acknowledge the Oneness of Surat al-Nahl 16:92 And do not be like the one who untwists her spun thread after it has been strong, taking your oaths as a means of deception among yourselves, lest one nation should be more numerous than another. God only tests you thereby, and He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ. God and the Prophethood of His Prophet, and would believe in what He sent His prophets with, while the disbeliever would deny all of that. So that was their difference in this world, which God, the Most High, promised His servants that He would make clear to them when they came to Him with the explanation we have described.

x: God Almighty says: And if your Lord had willed, O people, He would have been kind in fulfilling His commands, so that you would all become one group and people of one religion, not differing or separating. But He Almighty created differences between you and made you people of different religions, by guiding some to believe in Him and working in obedience to Him, so they were believers, and He let down those and deprived them of His guidance, so they were disbelievers. And God will ask you all on the Day of Resurrection about what you did in this world in what He commanded you and forbade you, then He will reward you with the reward of the obedient among you for obeying Him, and the disobedient for disobeying Him.

God the Almighty says: And do not use your oaths as a means of deception and trickery between you, by which you mislead people, lest your foot slip after it had been firmly established. He says: So that you perish after you had been safe from perdition.

i: This is an example for every afflicted person after being well, or someone who falls into trouble after being safe, and the like: his foot slipped, as the poet said:
x: It will prevent you from being ahead if you are ahead and it will ruin you if you slip And His statement, And taste the evil, means: And you taste the evil.

That evil is the punishment of God with which He punishes the people of His disobedience in this world, and that is some of what He punished the people of disbelief with. Because you have turned away from the path of God, means: because you have tempted those who wanted to believe in God and His Messenger from believing. And for you is a great punishment in the Hereafter, and that is the fire of Hell. This verse indicates that the interpretation of Buraydah that we mentioned about him, in His statement, And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made a covenant, and the verses that follow it, that he meant by that: those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Islam, from leaving Islam due to the small number of its people and the large number of the polytheists, is correct, not what Mujahid said: that they meant by it, because in the transfer of a people who have made an alliance from their allies to others other than them, there is no turning away from the path of God, nor straying from guidance.

And God, the Most High, has described in this verse those who do that, that they have taken oaths as a means of interfering between them, and their breaking their oaths after Confirming it, they are turning people away from the path of God, and that they are people of misguidance in the previous one, and this is the description of the people of disbelief in God, not the description of the people who transfer the oath from one people to another.
God Almighty says: “And do not exchange the covenant of God for a small price. Indeed, what is with God is better for you, if you only knew.”

God the Almighty says: And do not break your covenants, O people, and the contracts that you have made, confirming them with your oaths, seeking by breaking them a small worldly gain, but fulfill the covenant of God which He has commanded you to fulfill, and God will reward you for fulfilling it, for what is with God as a reward for fulfilling that is better for you if you only knew. The difference between the two exchanges, one of which is the small price that you buy by breaking the covenant of God in this world, and the other is the great reward in the Hereafter for fulfilling it. Then God the Almighty explained: The difference between the two exchanges and the difference between the two rewards, and He said: What you have, O people, is what you possess in this world, even if it is much, it is fleeting, and what is with God for those who fulfill their covenant and obey Him of good things is lasting and will not perish, so work for what is with Him and be keen on what remains that does not perish.
And His statement,
h
And We will surely reward those who were patient with the best of what they used to do

. God Almighty says: And God will surely reward those who were patient in their obedience to Him in prosperity and adversity, with their reward on the Day of Resurrection for their patience and their hastening to please Him, with the best of what they used to do of deeds, not the worst of them, and God will surely forgive them their bad deeds by His grace.

God Almighty says: Whoever acts in obedience to God, and fulfills God’s covenants when he makes a covenant, whether male or female, from among the children of Adam, and he is a believer: He says: and he believes in God’s reward that He promised to those who obey Him for obedience, and in the threat that He threatens those who disobey Him for disobedience,
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
The people of interpretation differed about what God meant by the good life that He promised these people that He would give them.
Some of them said: He meant that He would give them life in this world as long as they lived in it with lawful sustenance.
Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: The good life is lawful sustenance in this world.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Malik and Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Sami’, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Concerning His statement:
h
Whoever does righteousness
, whether male or female, while he is a believer -
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
, he said: Good provision in this world.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: The good provision in this world.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Al-Fadl bin Dukayn told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: The good provision in this world.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Whoever does righteousness
, whether male or female, while he is a believer -
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
, meaning in this world.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: Good, lawful sustenance.

c: Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me: Awn bin Salam Al-Qurashi told us: Bishr bin Amara told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Al-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
, he said: He will eat what is lawful and wear what is lawful.

x: Others said: Let us give him a good life by granting him contentment.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Khalifa, on the authority of Abu Khuzaymah Sulayman Al-Tammar, on the authority of someone
m: who mentioned it on the authority of Ali: Then
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
. He said: Contentment.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Issam told us, on the authority of Abu Saeed, on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, he said:
m: The good life is contentment.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by the good life is the life of believing in God and acting in obedience to Him.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
, meaning:
h
Whoever does righteousness

while he is a believer in poverty or ease, his life will be good. But whoever turns away from the remembrance of God and does not believe or do righteousness, his life will be difficult and there is no good in it.

x: Others said: The good life: happiness.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
, he said: happiness.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: life in Paradise.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Hudha told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: No life is good for anyone less than Paradise.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: Life is not good for anyone except in Paradise.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
Whoever does righteousness
, whether male or female, while he is a believer -
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
. God does not will an action except with sincerity, and He requires whoever does that with faith, God Almighty said:
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
, which is Paradise.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
Then We will cause him to live a good life
. He said: The Hereafter. He will cause them to live a good life in the Hereafter.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
Whoever does righteousness
, whether male or female, while he is a believer -
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
, he said: The good life in the Hereafter is Paradise, that is the good life. He said:
h
And We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do

, and he said: Do you not see him say: Oh, I wish I had sent forth for my life, he said: This is his Hereafter. And he also recited: And indeed, the home of the Hereafter - that is the life, he said: The Hereafter is a home of life for the people of Hell and the people of Paradise. There is no death in it for anyone of the two groups.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Whoever does righteousness

, whether male or female, while he is a believer, he said: Faith is sincerity to God alone, so he made clear that no deed is accepted except with sincerity to Him. The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said: The interpretation of that is:
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life

with contentment. That is because whoever God makes content with what He has allotted him of provision will not have much toil in this world, nor will his hardship in it be great, nor will his life be troubled in it by pursuing what he has missed of it and being eager for what he may not attain in it. I said: This is the most appropriate interpretation of this verse, because God, the Most High, mentioned Him, had threatened a people before it for their disobedience to Him, that if they disobeyed Him, He would make them taste evil in this world and torment in the Hereafter. God, the Most High, said: And do not take your oaths as a means of deception between you, lest a foot slip after it had been firmly established, and you taste evil for having averted [people] from the way of God. This is for them in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have a great torment. This is for them in the Hereafter. Then He followed that with what is for those who fulfill their covenant with God and obey Him, so God, the Most High, said: What is with you will come to an end, and what is with God will remain. So the One who caused this evil, by His wisdom, followed that promise for the people of His obedience with goodness in this world and forgiveness in the Hereafter, and God, the Most High, mentioned Him, did the same. As for the provision that was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that it is lawful provision, it is possible that its meaning is what we said about that, that the Almighty satisfies him in this world with what He provides him from what is lawful, even if it is little, so his soul does not call him to a lot of it from what is not lawful, not that He provides him with a lot of what is lawful, and that is because most of those who work for the sake of God the Almighty with what pleases Him from deeds, we have not seen them provided with a lot of lawful provision in this world, and we have found that the narrowness of life is more common than the abundance. And His saying,
h
And We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do
, there is no doubt that this is in the Hereafter, and the people of interpretation said the same.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do
. He said: When they go to God, He will reward them according to the best of what they used to do.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu Malik and Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: similarly.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Samee’, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And We will surely give them their reward. He said: In the Hereafter.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Sami’, on the authority of Abu al-Rabi’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do
. He says: He will reward them in the Hereafter according to the best of what they used to do. Surat al-Nahl 16:97
h
Whoever does righteousness
, whether male or female, while he is a believer -
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
h
and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do

. It was said: This verse was revealed because of people from different religions who were boasting, so the people of each religion said: We are better, so God showed them the best people of the religions.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ya’la ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Salih, who said:
m: Some people from the people of idols, the people of interpretation, and the people of the Gospel sat down.

x: Some of them said: We are better, and some of them said: We are better. Then God Almighty revealed: “
h
Whoever does righteousness
, whether male or female, while he is a believer -
h
We will surely cause him to live a good life
h
and We will surely reward them according to the best of what they used to do
God Almighty says: So when you recite the Qur’an, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed.
God Almighty says: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord.

God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him): And if you, O Muhammad, are reciting the Qur'an, then seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. Some Arab scholars claim that it is from the word Mu'akhr which means to bring forward. It seems that the meaning of the statement according to him is: And if you seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, then recite the Qur'an. There is no basis for what he said of that, because if that were the case, then whenever someone sought refuge from the accursed Satan, he would be obligated to recite the Qur'an. However, its meaning is what we have described, and his saying Then seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan is not an obligatory command. Rather, it is a notification and an encouragement. This is because there is no disagreement among all that whoever recites the Qur'an and does not seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan before or after reciting it has not wasted an obligatory duty.
Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we have said about that.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
So when you recite the Qur’an

, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed, he said: This is evidence from God Almighty that He has guided His servants to it. As for his statement: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord, he means by that: Satan has no argument over those who believe and His Messenger, and do what God has commanded, and refrain from what God has forbidden. And rely upon their Lord, meaning: And rely upon their Lord in what befalls them of their important affairs.
h
His authority is only over those who take him as an ally
, meaning: His argument is only over those who worship him.
h
And those who associate others with Him
, meaning: And those who associate others with God. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: His authority he said:
m: His proof.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
His authority is only over those who take him as an ally
, he said: They obey him.

x: The interpreters differed regarding the meaning for which Satan was not given power over the believer.

Some of them said: It was narrated on the authority of Waqid bin Sulayman, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement, Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord, he said: He has no authority to force them to commit an unforgivable sin.

Others said: It is seeking refuge, because if he seeks refuge with God, He will prevent him from it and will not give him power over it. He cited as evidence for the validity of his statement the words of God Almighty: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” We have mentioned the narration about that in Surat Al-Hijr.
Others said about this, including:

c: Al-Muthanna told me: Ishaq told us: Abdullah bin Abi Jaʿfar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ,
m: regarding His statement: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord to His statement:
h
and those who associate others with Him

. It is said that the enemy of God, Satan, said: I will surely mislead them all, except for Your chosen servants among them. So these are the ones over whom Satan has no power, and his authority is only over a people who took him as a friend and associated him in their actions.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement: Indeed, he has no authority over those who have believed and put their trust in their Lord, meaning: Authority over those who take Satan as their friend and commit acts of disobedience to God.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, His authority is only over those who take him as a guardian, meaning: those who obey him and worship him. The most correct of the sayings about this is the saying of those who said: Its meaning is that he has no authority over those who believe, so they sought refuge in God from him, as God Almighty has urged seeking refuge, and upon their Lord they rely, from what happened to them of his thoughts and whispers. We said: This is the most appropriate interpretation of the verse, because God Almighty followed this statement with:
h
So when you recite the Qur’an

, seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. And He said in another place: “But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.” So it was clear from that that He only urged His servants to seek refuge from him in these situations in order to protect them from his power. As for his saying:
h
And those who associate others with Him
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said what we said, that its meaning is: And those who associate others with God.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
and those who associate others with Him
, he said: They equate Him with the Lord of the Worlds.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And those who associate others with Him
he said: They equate others with God.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
And those who associate others with Him
, that they equated Iblis with their Lord, so they associate others with God.

x: Others said: The meaning of this is: Those who associate partners with Him have associated Satan with their actions.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah bin Abi Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Al-Rabi’:
m: h
And those who associate others with Him

they associate Him with their deeds. The first statement, I mean the statement of Mujahid, is the more correct of the two statements in this regard, and that is that those who take Satan as allies only associate partners with God in their worship, their sacrifices, their food and their drink, not that they associate partners with Satan. If the meaning of the speech was what al-Rabi’ said, then the revelation would have been: those who associate others with Him, and there was no mention of it in the speech. So it would have been if the revelation had been like that,
h
and those who associate others with Him

in their actions, unless the meaning of the speech is directed to the fact that the people were believing in the divinity of Satan, and associating God with him in their worship of him, then the meaning of the speech is correct, and it is outside of what the revelation came with in the rest of the Qur’an. That is because God Almighty described the polytheists in the rest of the Qur’an as having associated with God what He had not sent down to them as an authority for, and He said in every place that preceded them with a warning against that: Do not associate anything with God, and we did not find in any of the revelation: Do not associate anything with God, nor in any of the Qur’an, any report from God about them that they associated anything with God. So it is permissible for us to direct the meaning of His statement,
h
and those who associate others with Him
to and those who associate others with Satan are polytheists with God. So it is clear, since that is the case, that the ha in His statement,
h
and those who associate others with Him
refers back to the Lord in His statement, and upon their Lord they rely.

x: God Almighty says: And if We abrogate the ruling of a verse, then We substitute in its place another ruling - and God knows best what He sends down. He says: And God knows best what is best for His creation in what He changes and alters of His rulings. They say: You are only a fabricator. He says: The polytheists who disbelieved in God and His Messenger said to His Messenger: You, O Muhammad, are only a fabricator, meaning: a liar who fabricates falsehood about God. God Almighty says: Rather, most of those who say to you, O Muhammad, you are only a fabricator are ignorant, because what you bring to them from God is its abrogator and its abrogated, and they do not know the truth of its authenticity. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement:
h
And when We substitute one verse for another
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’ all together, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And when We substitute a verse in place of another verse
, We raise it up and send down another.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: And when We substitute a verse for another verse, he said: We abrogated it, replaced it, removed it, and established another.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And when We substitute one verse for another
, is like his statement, We do not abrogate a verse or cause it to be forgotten.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And when We substitute one verse for another

, they said: You are only a fabricator, you bring something and then revoke it, then bring something else. He said: This substitution is abrogating, and We do not substitute one verse for another except by abrogation.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you: You are only a liar in what you recite to them of the verses of Our Book, which the Holy Spirit has sent down. He says: Say: Gabriel brought it from my Lord in truth. I have explained in other places the meaning of: the Holy Spirit, so there is no need to repeat it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?
