c: Abdul-A’la bin Wasil told me: Ja’far bin Awn Al-Omari told us, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah Al-Rabdhi, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said:
m: The Holy Spirit is Gabriel. And His statement:
h
To strengthen those who believe

, God Almighty says: Say, “This Qur’an, its abrogator and its abrogated parts, was sent down by the Holy Spirit upon me from my Lord, as a confirmation for the believers and a strengthening of their faith, so that they may increase in their belief in its abrogating and abrogated parts, in faith for their faith, and as guidance for them from misguidance, and as good tidings for the Muslims who have submitted to God’s command, and obeyed His commands and prohibitions, and what He has sent down in the verses of His Book, so they have acknowledged all of that and believed in it in word and deed.”

x: God the Almighty says: And indeed, We know that these polytheists say, out of ignorance: Only a human being from among the children of Adam knows this, and it is not from God. God the Almighty says, refuting their statement: Do you not know that what you say is false? The language of the one you attribute to - He says: Do you incline towards him that he teaches Muhammad is foreign? That is because, as mentioned, they claimed that the one who taught Muhammad this Qur’an was a Roman slave. Therefore, God the Almighty said: The language of the one they attribute to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language. He says: And this Qur’an is a clear Arabic language. In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, with their differences, about the name of the one whom the polytheists claimed was teaching Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, this Qur’an from among the humans.
Some of them said: His name was Balaam, and he was a blacksmith in Mecca, a Christian.
Who said that?

c: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi told me: Abu Asim told us: Ibrahim ibn Tahman told us, on the authority of Muslim ibn Abdullah al-Mala’i, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, taught a blacksmith in Mecca, and he was a foreigner, and his name was Balaam. The polytheists would see the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he entered upon him and when he left him, and they said: It is only Balaam who teaches him. So God, the Most High, revealed:
h
And We certainly know that they say
, ‘It is only a human being who teaches him.’ The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.

x: Others said: His name is Yaish.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to teach a foreign boy of Banu Al-Mughira. Sufyan said: I think he was called Ya’ish. He said: That is what he said: The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We certainly know that they say

, ‘It is only a human being who teaches him,’ and the Quraysh said: It is only a human being who teaches him, a slave of Banu al-Hadrami called Ya’ish. God Almighty said, The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language. Ya’ish used to read books.

x: Others said: Rather, his name was Jabr.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as I have been informed, often used to sit at Al-Marwah with a Christian boy called Jabr, a slave of the Banu Bayadah Al-Hadrami. They used to say: By God, Muhammad does not know much of what he does except Jabr the Christian, the boy of Al-Hadrami. So God Almighty revealed regarding their statement:
h
And We certainly know that they say
, ‘It is only a human being who teaches him.’ The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Abdullah Ibn Kathir said:
m: They used to say: Only a Christian teaches him on Al-Marwah, and Muhammad is taught by a Roman, they say his name is Jabr, and he was a scribe, a slave of Ibn Hadrami. God Almighty said: The language of the one they refer to is foreign. He said: And this is the saying of Quraysh 106:Only a human being teaches him. God Almighty said: The language of the one they refer to is foreign, and this is a clear Arabic language.

x: Others said: Rather, they were two boys, one of them Surat al-Nahl 16:103
h
And We certainly know that they say
, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language. named Yasar and the other Jabr.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Amr ibn Awn told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muslim al-Hadrami,
m: that they had two slaves from the people of ‘Ayr in Yemen, and they were children. One of them was called Yasar and the other Jabr. They used to recite the Torah, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would sometimes sit with them. The infidels of Quraysh said: He only sits with them to learn from them. Then God Almighty revealed: The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ma’n bin Asad told us, he said: Khalid bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abdullah bin Muslim Al-Hadrami,
m: something similar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Hiseen, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muslim, who said:
m: They were two young boys who were reading a book of theirs in their own language. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass by them and stand to listen to them. The polytheists said: He is learning from them. Then God Almighty revealed what he denied them with, saying: The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language.

x: Others said: Rather, it was Salman Al-Farsi.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement,
h
The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign
, they used to say: Only Salman Al-Farsi knows him.

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said: Shibl told us, and Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq told us, he said: Abdullah told us, on the authority of Warqa’,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And We certainly know that they say

, ‘It is only a human being who teaches him.’ He said: The statement of the infidels of Quraysh 106:It is only Abd ibn Al-Hadrami who teaches Muhammad, and he is the owner of a book. God says: The language of the one they refer to is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic language. It was said that the one who said that was a scribe for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had apostatized from Islam.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab told me that
m: the one who mentioned God was only taught by a human being. He was only tempted because he was writing the revelation, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would dictate to him: All-Hearing, All-Knowing, or All-Mighty, All-Wise, and other endings of the verses. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would be distracted from it while he was receiving the revelation, so the Messenger of God would ask him, saying: All-Mighty, All-Wise, or All-Hearing, All-Knowing, or All-Mighty, All-Knowing? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would say: Whichever of these you wrote, it is like that. That tempted him, so he said: Muhammad entrusts that to me, so write whatever you wish. And that is what Saeed bin Al-Musayyab mentioned to me of the seven letters. The readers differed in their reading of his statement: they object, so the majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it as the tongue of the one who object to it, with a damma on the ya from al-had ilhadan, meaning they object, turn to it, and ascend to it, from the words of the poet. My leader is not a stingy atheist, but a supporter of the two Khabaybains. The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as the tongue of the one who inclines towards it with the opening of the ya, meaning: they incline towards it from the lahad of so-and-so to this matter, yalhadu lahudan and lahudan, and in my opinion they are two languages with the same meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in both. It was said, And this is a clear Arabic tongue, meaning: the Qur’an, as the Arabs say about a poem that a poet recites: This is the tongue of so-and-so, meaning his poem, as the poet said. The evil tongue brings it to us and you yearn, and you did not expect that you would revive us It means the poem and the word.

evidence.text: The readers differed in their reading of his statement: they object, so the majority of the readers of Medina and Basra read it as the tongue of the one who object to it, with a damma on the ya from al-had ilhadan, meaning they object, turn to it, and ascend to it, from the words of the poet.

The majority of the readers of Kufa read it as the tongue of the one who inclines towards it with the opening of the ya, meaning: they incline towards it from the lahad of so-and-so to this matter, yalhadu lahudan and lahudan, and in my opinion they are two languages with the same meaning, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct in both.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who do not believe in the verses of God - God will not guide them, and they will have a painful punishment.

God the Almighty says: Indeed, those who do not believe in God's proofs and evidence, and believe in what they indicate, God will not guide them meaning: God will not grant them success in finding the truth, nor will He guide them to the path of right guidance in this world. And for them in the Hereafter and with God when they come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, there will be a painful and grievous punishment. Then God the Almighty informed the polytheists who said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: You are only a slanderer, that they are the people of slander and lying, not the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers in him. He disavowed his Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from that, saying: Only those who do not believe in God's proofs and His information fabricate lies, because they do not expect reward for truthfulness, nor fear punishment for lying. They are the people of slander and fabrication of lies, not those who hope for a great reward from God for truthfulness, and fear a painful punishment for lying. And His saying,
h
And those are the liars
, means: And those who do not believe in the verses of God are the liars, not the believers.

Arabists differed about the factor in min in his saying whoever disbelieves in God, and in his saying but whoever opens his heart to disbelief, some of the grammarians of Basra said: His saying upon them became the predicate of his saying but whoever opens his heart to disbelief, and his saying
h
whoever disbelieves in God after his belief
, so he informed them with one predicate, and that indicated the meaning.

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: These are two parts that came together, one of them is linked to the other, so their answer is one, like the saying of the speaker: whoever comes to us, whoever does good, we will honor him, meaning: whoever does good among those who come to us, we will honor him. He said: And likewise every two parts that come together, the second is connected to the first, so the answer to them is one. And another from the people of Basra said: Rather, his saying, Whoever disbelieves in God is raised in response to those in his saying, Only those who do not believe in the signs of God invent falsehood, and the meaning of the speech according to him: Only those who disbelieve in God after their belief invent falsehood, except for those of these who are forced, and their hearts are at peace with faith. This is a statement that has no basis, because if the meaning of the statement was as the one who said this statement said, then God, the Most High, would have excluded from those who fabricated lies in this verse those who were born in disbelief and remained in it, and never believed, and He specified with it those who had believed at one time, then returned to disbelief after believing, and the revelation indicates that He did not specify with that these without the rest of the polytheists who were remaining in polytheism, because God, the Most High, informed the story of a group of them who attributed fabrication of lies to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so He said And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and God knows best what He sends down - they say, You are only an inventor.

Rather, most of them do not know and all the polytheists lied by their fabrication of lies against God, and He informed that they are more deserving of this description than the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so He said: Only those who do not believe in the verses of God invent lies, and those are the liars. If those meant by this verse were those who disbelieved in God after their belief, then it would be necessary that those who said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, You are only an inventor when God substituted A verse instead of a verse, they were the ones who disbelieved in God after believing in Him specifically, not others from the rest of the polytheists, because this is the context of the report about them, and that is a statement that if someone said it, then its corruption would be clear with its departure from the interpretation of all the people of knowledge of interpretation.

The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the one who raises the first and second is his saying, upon them is the wrath of God. The Arabs do this with the letters of recompense when they start one after another. He mentioned that this verse was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir and a group of people who had converted to Islam, but the polytheists tempted them to abandon their religion.
Some of them remained steadfast in Islam, and some were tempted.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief

, except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith… to the end of the verse. That is because the polytheists captured Ammar ibn Yasir and tortured him, then left him alone. He returned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him what he had encountered from the Quraysh, and what he had said. Then God, the Exalted, revealed his excuse,
h
Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief
… to His statement,
h
And for them is a great punishment
. Surat al-Nahl 16:106
h
Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief
, except for one who is forced [to disbelieve] while his heart is at rest with faith. But as for those who open their breasts to disbelief, upon them is wrath from God,
h
and for them is a great punishment

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief

, except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith. He said: It was mentioned to us that it was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir. Banu al-Mughira took him and threw him in the well of Maymun and said: Disbelieve in Muhammad. So he followed them in that, and his heart was reluctant. So God, the Most High, revealed: “Except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith. But whoever opens his breast to disbelief”: that is, whoever comes to disbelief by choice and desirability, upon them is wrath from God,
h
and for them is a great punishment

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn Yasir, who said:
m: “The polytheists took Ammar ibn Yasir and tortured him until he showed disloyalty to them in some of what they wanted. He complained about that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘How do you find your heart?’ He said: ‘Reassured by faith.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘If they return, then return.’”
b.via: Abu Ubaidah ibn Muhammad ibn Ammar ibn Yasir

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Except for one who is forced [to do so] while his heart is at rest with faith
, he said: It was revealed about Ammar bin Yasir.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said:
m: When Al-A’bad was tortured, they were given what they asked for except for Khabbab bin Al-Arat. They would lay him down on the embers and they would not take anything from him. The interpretation of the statement then is:
h
Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief

, except for one who is forced to disbelieve, so he utters the word of disbelief with his tongue while his heart is at peace with faith, certain of its truth, his resolve is sound, and his heart is not open to disbelief. But whoever opens his heart to disbelief and chooses it and prefers it over faith, and declares it willingly, then upon them is wrath from God,
h
and for them is a great punishment
. In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas.

c: Ali bin Dawud told me: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Except for one who is forced while his heart is at rest in faith

c: So God Almighty informed us that
m: whoever disbelieves after his belief, upon him is God’s wrath, and for him is a great punishment. As for the one who is forced and his tongue speaks it, but his heart contradicts it in faith in order to be saved from his enemy, then there is no blame upon him, because God Almighty only takes the servants by what their hearts are resolved upon.

x: God Almighty says: God’s wrath descended upon these polytheists, and a great punishment was due to them, because they chose the adornments of worldly life over the bliss of the Hereafter, and because God does not grant success to the people who deny His signs while they persist in denying them.
God Almighty says: “Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing and vision God has sealed. And it is those who are the heedless.”

God Almighty says: These polytheists whose description I have described to you in these verses, O people, are the people whose hearts God has sealed, so they do not believe, nor are they guided. He has made their ears deaf, so they do not hear God’s caller to guidance, and He has made their eyes blind, so they do not see God’s proofs with a vision that takes heed and is admonished. And those are the heedless. He says: And those in whom God has placed these actions are the ones who are heedless of what God has prepared for their likes among the people of disbelief, and of what is intended for them. His saying,
h
There is no doubt that they
, in the Hereafter, are the losers, the doomed ones, who cheated themselves of their share of God Almighty’s honor.

God Almighty says: Then your Lord, O Muhammad, is for those who emigrated from their homes, dwellings, and tribes from the polytheists, and moved away from them to the homes of the people of Islam, their homes, and the people of their guardianship, after the polytheists who were among them before their emigration from their religion had tempted them, then they fought the polytheists after that, supporting them with the sword and with their tongues by disavowing them and what they worshipped besides God, and they were patient in their struggle against them, Indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful. He says: Indeed, your Lord, after this action of theirs, is Forgiving, He says: He has concealed what they did from giving the polytheists what they wanted from them of the word of disbelief with their tongues, while they were concealing something other than it, and believing in faith, He is Merciful towards them, that He does not punish them for it with their return to God and their repentance.

It was mentioned by some of the people of interpretation that this verse was revealed about a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who had stayed behind in Mecca after the Prophet’s migration, may God bless him and grant him peace. The polytheists were harsh with them until they tempted them away from their religion, so they despaired of repentance. So God revealed this verse about them, so they migrated and joined the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief, except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith, he said: People from the people of Mecca believed, so some of the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wrote to them in Medina, saying: Migrate, for we do not see you as one of us until you migrate to us, so they left intending to go to Medina, but the Quraysh caught up with them on the road, so they tempted them and they disbelieved under duress, so this verse was revealed about them.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar. Ibn Jurayj said: God Almighty said, Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief, then He abrogated and made an exception, saying, Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed

, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful. He mentioned to us that when God revealed that the people of Mecca would not accept Islam until they emigrated, the people of Medina wrote about it to their companions from the people of Mecca. When that came to them, they pledged allegiance among themselves that they would leave, and if the polytheists from the people of Mecca caught up with them, they would fight them until they escaped or joined God. So they left, and the polytheists caught up with them, and they fought them, and some of them were killed, and some of them escaped, so God Almighty revealed, Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted.... the verse. Ahmad bin Mansur narrated: Abu Ahmad Al-Zubayri narrated: Muhammad bin Sharik narrated: Amr bin Dinar narrated: Ikrimah narrated: Ibn Abbas narrated: There were some people from Mecca who had converted to Islam, but they were hiding their Islam. The polytheists expelled them on the day of Badr, and some of them were injured and some were killed. The Muslims said: These people of ours were Muslims, and they were forced, so they asked forgiveness for them. Then this verse was revealed: Indeed, those whom the angels take while they are wronging themselves ... to the end of the verse. He said: And this verse was written to those Muslims who remained in Mecca, saying: They have no excuse. He said: So they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them, and they gave them trial. Then this verse was revealed: And of the people is he who says, We believe in God, but when he is harmed for the sake of God, He considers the trial of the people to be like the punishment of God ... to the end of the verse. So the Muslims wrote to them about that, so they went out Surat al-Nahl 16:110 Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful. and despaired of all good. Then this verse was revealed about them: (Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient. Indeed, your Lord is of the believers.) ... to the end of the verse. Then He is Forgiving and Merciful.” So they wrote to them about that: God has made a way out for you, so they went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and fought them, then those who escaped escaped, and those who were killed were killed.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: This verse was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi’ah, and Al-Walid ibn Al-Walid: Then your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient.

x: Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed regarding Ibn Abi Sarh.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told me: Yahya bin Wadh told us, on the authority of Al-Husayn, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, they said
m: in Surat al-Nahl 16:“Whoever disbelieves in God after his belief, except for one who is forced thereto and whose heart is at rest with faith. But those who open their breasts to disbelief - upon them is wrath from God, and for them is a great punishment.” Then it was abrogated and an exception was made, and He said: Then indeed, your Lord is for those who emigrated after they were persecuted and then strove and were patient - indeed, your Lord, thereafter, is Forgiving and Merciful. He is Abdullah bin Abi Sarh, who used to write for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Satan made him slip, so he joined the disbelievers, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to be killed on the day of the conquest of Mecca, so Abu Amr sought protection for him, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, granted him protection.

x: God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful. On the Day every soul will come arguing for itself, and will argue on its behalf with what it did in the world of good or evil, faith or disbelief, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did in the world of obedience and disobedience, and they will not be wronged. He says: Nothing will be done to them except what they deserve and are entitled to for what they did of good or evil. The doer of good will not be rewarded except for what he did in the past of evil. The doer of good will not be punished, nor will the reward for his good be diminished, and the doer of evil will not be rewarded except for the reward of his work. The Arabists differed about the reason for which it was said Tajadal and the feminization of all.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It was said because the meaning of all soul is all human beings, and it was made feminine because soul is both masculine and feminine. It is said: There came to me not one soul, nor one.

Some of the Arabists considered this statement by its speaker to be a mistake and said: All if it is added to a single indefinite noun, the verb is derived according to the number of the indefinite noun: Every woman is standing, Every stone is standing, Every two women are standing, Every two men are standing, Every women are standing, Every man is standing, so it is derived according to the number of the indefinite noun and its feminization and masculinity, and there is no need to feminize or masculinize the soul.

God the Almighty says: And God has given an example of Mecca, whose inhabitants are polytheists. It is a city that was safe and secure. Its security was that the Arabs used to fight each other, kill each other, and take each other captive. The people of Mecca were not subject to raids or wars in their own country. That was its security. His statement, safe and secure means: stable with its people. Its people do not need to move around, as the people of the desert needed it. Its provision comes to it in abundance means: its people’s livelihoods come to it in abundance. His statement, from every place means: from every pass of this city, and from every side of it. And similar to what we said about the village mentioned in this place meaning Mecca, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, “
h
And God presents an example
: a city that was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location,” meaning: Mecca.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: A village that was safe and secure. He said: Mecca.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “
h
And God sets forth an example
: a city that was safe and secure.” He said: It was mentioned to us that it was Mecca.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: A village that was safe. He said: It is Mecca.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, “
h
And God presents an example
: a city that was safe and secure”... to the end of the verse, he said: This is Mecca.

x: Others said: Rather, the village that God mentioned in this place is the city of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told me: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Nafi’ ibn Yazid told us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shuraih told me that Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith al-Hadrami told us that
m: he heard Mushrah ibn Aahan say: I heard Salim ibn Numayr say: We set out from Hajj with Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Uthman was besieged in Madinah. She was asking about him and what had happened, until she saw two riders, so she sent to them asking them. They said: He was killed. Hafsah said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is the city, meaning the city about which God the Most High said: “
h
And God presents an example
: a city that was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location.
h
But it denied the favors of God
.” He recited it. Abu Shuraih said: Abdullah ibn al-Mughira informed me on the authority of someone who told him that he used to say: It was Madinah. And His statement:
h
But it denied the favors of God
means: The people of this city denied the favors of God that He bestowed upon it. The Arabists differed about the singular of an'am.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The plural of an'am is an'am, as God said until he reaches his prime, so he claimed that it is the plural of hardship. Another of them said the singular is na'am, and he said: It is said: days of taste and na'am, meaning: bliss. He said: It is possible that its meaning is: so she was ungrateful for God's bliss to her.

i: And he cited as evidence for that the saying of the poet:
x: I have loans, both good and bad, so misery for the one who is miserable and blessings for the one who is blessed Some of the people of Kufa used to say: An’am is the plural of Na’ama, like Basa’ and Abwas, and Dhra’ and Adhar.
As for Ashdh, he claimed that it is the plural of Shadd. And His saying:
h
So God made them taste the garment of hunger and fear

means, the Most High said: So God made the people of this town taste the garment of hunger, and that is a hunger whose harm mixed with their bodies, so God, the Most High, made that, because of its mixing with their bodies, like a garment for them, and that is because hunger was imposed upon them for successive years by the supplication of Surat al-Nahl 16:112
h
And God presents an example
: a town that was safe and secure, its provision coming to it in abundance from every location,
h
but it denied the favors of God

. So God made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do. the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they ate the ‘alahaz and the carcasses - Abu Ja’far said: The ‘alahaz is the fur kneaded with blood and the ticks eat it - and as for the fear, that was their fear of the raids of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that were surrounding them.

And His saying, because of what they were doing means: because of what they were doing of disbelief in the blessings of God, and denying His signs, and calling His Messenger a liar. And He said: because of what they were doing, and the speech from the beginning of the verse to this place proceeded in a good manner about the town, because the report, even though it proceeded in speaking about the town, dispensed with mentioning its people so that the listeners would know what was meant by it, for what was meant were its people, so that is why it was said, because of what they were doing They make the report is returned to the people of the village, and this is similar to his saying Our punishment came to her at night or while they were asleep and he did not say speaking, and he said before it Our punishment came to her", because he returned the report to informing about the people of the village, and there are many similar examples of that in the Qur’an.

evidence.text: He recited it.

x: God the Almighty says: And there came to the people of this town, whose description God described in the verse before this verse, A Messenger from among themselves He says: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from him. He says: From among themselves, they knew him, and they knew his lineage and the truthfulness of his speech, calling them to the truth and to the straight path. But they denied him and did not accept what he brought them from God. So the punishment seized them This is the cloak of hunger and fear instead of the security, tranquility and abundant provision that they had been provided with before that, and they were killed by the sword while they were wrongdoers He says: And they were polytheists, and this is because their leaders were killed by the sword on the day of Badr for polytheism. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqatada:
m: And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, yes, by God, they knew his lineage and his affair, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers, so God seized them with hunger, fear, and killing.

x: God Almighty says: So eat, O people, of the livestock which God has provided for you, lawful for you, good, slaughtered, not forbidden to you. And be grateful for the favor of God. He says: And be grateful for the favors that He has bestowed upon you in making lawful what He has made lawful for you of that, and for other favors of His. If it is Him that you worship. He says: If you worship God, then you obey Him in what He commands you and forbids you.
Some of them said: What he meant by his saying,
h
So eat of what God has provided for you

, lawful and good, was food that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent to the polytheists of his people during the years of famine and drought, out of compassion for them. So God, the Most High, said to the polytheists:
h
So eat of what God has provided for you

from this which He has sent to you, lawful and good. This is a far-fetched interpretation of what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates, because God, the Most High, followed that with his saying, He has only forbidden you dead animals and blood… and the verse that follows it. Thus, he made clear that his saying,
h
So eat of what God has provided for you

, lawful and good, was an announcement from God to His servants that what the polytheists were forbidding of the bahīr, the sawa’ib, the wasā’il, and other things that we have explained before, has no meaning, since that was from the steps of the devil, for all of that is lawful and God has not forbidden anything of it.

God Almighty says, refuting the polytheists who used to forbid what we mentioned of lakes and other things: God has forbidden you, O people, nothing except dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which is slaughtered for idols, and the name of someone other than God is mentioned over it, because that is from the slaughterings of those whose slaughtering is not permissible to eat. So whoever is forced to do that or to some of it due to famine that has come and eats it, neither transgressing nor exceeding limits, then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He says: He is the One who conceals it from holding him accountable for eating that in a state of necessity, and He is Merciful to him from punishing him for it. We have explained the difference of opinion among those who differed regarding his statement, neither transgressing nor exceeding limits. The correct statement in our view is that it is based on evidence from what has passed, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
He has only forbidden you dead animals

, blood, and the like, the verse, he said: Indeed, Islam is a religion that God purifies from every evil, and He has made for you, O son of Adam, in it, ease if you are forced to do something of that. His statement,
h
But whoever is forced [by necessity]
, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], not desiring in his eating nor transgressing in going beyond what is permissible to what is forbidden, and he finds an alternative to it.

x: God Almighty said: "And do not say about what your tongues describe falsely, 'This is lawful and this is unlawful,' to invent a lie against God. Indeed, those who invent a lie against God will not succeed."

The readers differed in reading this, so the majority of the readers of Hijaz and Iraq read it as And do not say to what your tongues describe as lying so it describes the lie, meaning: And do not say to what your tongues describe as lying, so ma is in the sense of the source, and it was mentioned from Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read And do not say to what your tongues describe as lying this with the lowering of the lie, meaning: And do not say to the lie that your tongues describe this is lawful and this is unlawful so he makes the lie a translation of what is in lama, so he lowers it with what he lowers ma. And it was narrated from some of them that when your tongues describe as lying with the raising of the lie, so he makes the lie an attribute of the tongues, and it is derived from the verb as a plural of kadhb and dhabh, like shukoor and shukr. The correct reading in my opinion is to put the lie in the accusative case because of the consensus of the proof of the reciters on it.

So the interpretation of the statement, since that is the case, is for what we mentioned: And do not say, in describing with your tongues the lie about what God has provided for His servants of foods: This is lawful and this is unlawful, in order to invent a lie about God with your saying, for God has not forbidden what you forbid, nor has He permitted much of what you permit. Then He advanced to them the threat for their lie about Him, and He said: Indeed, those who invent a lie about God meaning: Indeed, those who invent and fabricate lies about God will not abide in this world, nor will they remain in it, but will enjoy it for a little while. And He said: A little enjoyment so He raised it because the meaning that they are in from this world is a little enjoyment, or they will have a little enjoyment in this world. And His statement:
h
And for them is a painful punishment
means: Then to Us is their return and their return, and for them, for their lie and invention of God with what they invent, is a painful punishment when they return to Him.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: When your tongues describe falsehood, this is lawful and this is unlawful in Al-Buhayrah and Al-Sa’ibah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: The lakes and the swab.

evidence.text: The readers differed in reading this, so the majority of the readers of Hijaz and Iraq read it as And do not say to what your tongues describe as lying so it describes the lie, meaning: And do not say to what your tongues describe as lying, so ma is in the sense of the source, and it was mentioned from Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read And do not say to what your tongues describe as lying this with the lowering of the lie, meaning: And do not say to the lie that your tongues describe this is lawful and this is unlawful so he makes the lie a translation of what is in lama, so he lowers it with what he lowers ma.
The correct reading in my opinion is to put the lie in the accusative case because of the consensus of the proof of the reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says: And We had forbidden before you, O Muhammad, to the Jews what We had informed you of before in Surat Al-An'am, and that was every animal with claws, and from the cows and sheep We had forbidden them their fat, except what was on their backs or entrails, or what was mixed with a bone. And We did not wrong them by forbidding that to them, but they were wronging themselves so We recompensed them for that because of their transgression against their Lord, and their wronging themselves by disobeying God, so that caused them to incur God’s punishment. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We have forbidden to those who are Jews what We have related to you before
, he said: In Surat Al-An’am.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We have forbidden to those who are Jews what We have related to you before
, he said: In Surat Al-An’am.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We have forbidden to those who are Jews what We related to you before
, he said: What God Almighty related in Surat Al-An’am where He says, And We have forbidden to those who are Jews all animals having claws..... the verse.

x: God Almighty says: “Indeed, your Lord is to those who disobeyed God and were ignorant of their committing what they committed of disobedience to God, and were foolish about that, then they returned to obeying God and regretted it, and sought forgiveness and repented from it, after what they had done in the past of committing disobedience, and they reformed and did what God requires and is pleased with, “Indeed, your Lord, after that,” meaning: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, after their repentance to Him, is Forgiving and Merciful.
God Almighty says: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.

God Almighty says: Indeed, Abraham, the friend of God, was a teacher of goodness, followed by the people of guidance, obedient, obedient to God, upright in the religion of Islam. And he was not of the polytheists. He says: He did not associate anything with God, so he would be among the allies of the polytheists. This is an announcement from God Almighty to the polytheists of Quraysh that Abraham is innocent of them and that they are innocent of him. Grateful for His favors. He says: He sincerely thanked God for what He bestowed upon him, and did not make a partner with Him in His favors upon him from among the gods, rivals, and other than that, as the polytheists of Quraysh do. He chose him. He says: He selected him and chose him for his friendship. And guided him to a straight path. He says: He directed him to the straight path, and that is the religion of Islam, not Judaism or Christianity.
And similar to what we said about the meaning of a devout nation, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Zakariya bin Yahya told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn,
m: that he came to Abdullah and said: Whom shall we ask if we do not ask you? Ibn Masoud seemed to feel sorry for him, so he said: Tell me about the Ummah. He said: The one who teaches people good.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn,
m: that he asked Abdullah bin Masoud about the obedient slave woman. He said: The slave woman is the one who teaches goodness, and the obedient slave is the one who obeys God and His Messenger.

c: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Mansur,
m: meaning Ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, who said: Furwah ibn Nawfal al-Ashja’i told me: Ibn Mas’ud said: Mu’adh was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth. I said to myself: Abu Abd al-Rahman is mistaken. God the Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God. He said: Do you know what a nation is, and what a devout person is? I said: God knows best. He said: A nation is one who knows good, and a devout person is one who obeys God and His Messenger. Mu’adh ibn Jabal also knew good, and he was obedient to God and His Messenger. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated: Shuʿbah narrated: I heard Firas narrating, on the authority of al-Shaʿbi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud, that he said: Muʿadh was a nation obedient to God. A man from Ashjaʿ called Furwah ibn Nawfal said: He forgot, that was Ibrahim. ʿAbdullah said: Who forgot? We used to liken him to Ibrahim. ʿAbdullah was asked about a nation, and he said: A teacher of goodness, and the obedient is the one who obeys God and His Messenger.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Firas, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: I read this verse in the presence of Abdullah: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God. He said: Muadh was a nation obedient to God. He said: Do you know what a nation is? A nation is one who teaches people goodness, and the obedient is one who obeys God and His Messenger.

c: Abu Hisham Al-Rafa’i told us: Ibn Fadil told us: Bayan bin Bishr Al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi: Abdullah said:
m: Muadh was a nation, obedient to God, upright, and he was not one of the polytheists. A man said to him: You forgot. He said: No, but he is similar to Abraham. The nation is the teacher of goodness, and the obedient is the obedient.

c: Ali bin Saeed Al-Kindi told me: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, inclining toward truth. He said: Obedient.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr told us: Abdullah said:
m: Muadh was a devout, obedient nation, and a teacher of goodness. He mentioned things that are disputed about the nation. He said, And remember after a time a nation, meaning after a while, and a middle nation.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Sabeq, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, who said:
m: There was no earth left without fourteen people on it, through whom God would protect the people of the earth and bring forth its blessings, except during the time of Abraham, for he was alone.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Sayyar told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, he said: Zakariya and Mujalid told us, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud,
m: similar to what Ya’qub told, on the authority of Ibn Ulayyah, and he added to it: The nation is the one who knows good, follows it, and is emulated, and the obedient is the one who obeys God and the Messenger. Abu Furwa Al-Kindi said to him: You are mistaken.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said:
m: Surat al-Nahl 16:121 Thankful for His blessings, He chose him and guided him to a straight path.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, Abraham was a nation on its own, devoutly obedient to God he said: obedient.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same, except that he said: Obedient to God in this world. Ibn Jurayj said: Uwaimir told me, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he said: Qanitan: obedient.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God, he said: He was an imam of guidance, obedient, following his Sunnah and his religion.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that Ibn Mas’ud said:
m: Muadh ibn Jabal was a devout nation. Other than Qatada said: Ibn Mas’ud said: Do you know what a nation is? The one who knows good.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Firas, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said:
m: I read to Abdullah bin Mas’ud, Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient. He said: Indeed, Mu’adh was a nation obedient. He said: So they repeated it, and he repeated it to them, then he said: Do you know what a nation is? The one who teaches people good, and the obedient is the one who obeys God. We have explained the meaning of the nation and its aspects, and the meaning of the obedient with the differences of those who differed about it in other than this place in our book with its evidence, so that it is sufficient to repeat it in this place.

evidence.text: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Firas, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I read this verse in the presence of Abdullah: Indeed, Abraham was a nation obedient to God.

x: God Almighty says: And We gave Abraham, for his obedience to God, his gratitude to Him for His blessings, and his sincere worship of Him in this world, a good remembrance and beautiful praise that will last for days. And indeed, in the Hereafter, he will be among the righteous. He says: And indeed, in the Hereafter on the Day of Resurrection, he is among those whose affairs and status with God are good, and whose status and honor therein are good. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And We gave him good in this world. He said: A truthful tongue.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And We gave him good in this world. So there is no person of religion who does not support him and be pleased with him.

x: God Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’

God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Then We revealed to you, O Muhammad, and said to you: Follow the religion of Abraham, the upright, the Muslim. Upright: He says: Muslim, following the religion that Abraham followed, innocent of the idols and rivals that your people worship, just as Abraham had been innocent of them. And His statement:
h
The Sabbath was only made obligatory for those who differed about it
. God Almighty says: God did not impose, O people, the reverence of the Sabbath except on those who differed about it.
Some of them said: It is the greatest of days, because God Almighty finished creating things on Friday, then He made the Sabbath the Sabbath.

Others said: Rather, the greatest day is Sunday, because it is the day on which the creation of things began. So they chose it and abandoned the veneration of Friday, which God imposed upon them to venerate, and they considered it permissible. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
The Sabbath was only made obligatory for those who differed about it
. They followed it and abandoned Friday.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: The Sabbath was only made. He said: They meant Friday, but they made a mistake, so they took the Sabbath in its place.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
The Sabbath was only made obligatory for those who differed about it
, some of them considered it permissible, and some of them considered it forbidden.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
The Sabbath was only made for those who differed about it
. He said: Because they considered the Sabbath permissible.
b.via: Abu Malik and Saeed bin Jubair

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told me, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement:
h
The Sabbath was only made for those who differed about it

, he said: They were seeking Friday but they missed it, and they took Saturday, so He made it for them. And His statement: And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ. God Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, will judge between these people who differed among themselves regarding the permissibility and prohibition of the Sabbath when they return to Him on the Day of Resurrection. He will judge between them regarding that and other matters over which they used to differ in this world with truth, and He will decide with justice by rewarding the one who was right in it with his reward, and the one who was wrong in it with what he deserves.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Call O Muhammad, to whom your Lord has sent you with the call to His obedience to the way of your Lord meaning: to the law of your Lord that He has legislated for His creation, which is Islam with wisdom meaning: with the revelation of God that He reveals to you, and His Book that He has sent down to you and good instruction meaning: and with the beautiful lessons that God has made an argument against them in His Book, and reminded them of in His revelation, like those that He enumerated against them in this Surah of His arguments, and reminded them of what He mentioned of His favors and argue with them in a way that is best meaning: and argue with them in a way that is better than anything else, that is, forgive the harm they have caused you in terms of honor, and do not disobey Him in carrying out what is required of you in conveying to them the message of your Lord.
And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And argue with them in a way that is best, turn away from their harm to you.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And His saying: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of who among His creation has deviated from the right path, from those who stayed behind on the Sabbath and other days, and has deviated from God. And He is most knowing of who among them was following the right path and the path of truth, and He will reward all of them with their reward when they come to Him.

x: God Almighty says to the believers: And if you, O believers, punish someone who has wronged you and transgressed against you, then punish him with the equivalent of the punishment that your oppressor inflicted upon you. But if you are patient and do not punish him, and you seek reward from God for the injustice he inflicted upon you, and you entrust his affair to Him, so that He is the One who takes charge of his punishment, it is better for the patient. He says: To be patient and not punish him with that is better for the people of patience, seeking reward from God, because God compensates him for what He wanted to inflict upon him by taking revenge on his oppressor for his injustice to him with the pleasure of victory, and it is from His saying it is as a metaphor for patience, and that is good, even if patience was not mentioned before that, because His saying and if you are patient indicates it.
The people of interpretation differed about the reason for which this verse was revealed. It was said: It was abrogated or decisive.

Some of them said: It was revealed because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions swore when the polytheists did what they did to the Muslims’ dead on the day of Uhud, mutilating them, that they would go beyond their action in mutilating them if they were granted victory over them one day. So God forbade them from that with this verse, and commanded them to limit themselves to mutilating them if they were granted victory over the like of what they had done. Then He commanded them after that to leave mutilating them and to prefer patience instead, by saying:
h
And be patient
, and your patience is not but through God. Thus, in their view, what they had been permitted to do of mutilation was abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us:
m: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Amer, that the Muslims said, when the polytheists did to their dead on the day of UHud 11:If we are victorious over them, we will do it. Then God Almighty revealed: “
h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.” They said: Rather, we will be patient.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abd al-Wahhab told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Aamer, who said:
m: When the Muslims saw what the polytheists did to their dead on the day of Uhud, slitting open their bellies, cutting off their genitals, and mutilating them badly, they said: If God gives us victory over them, we will do this and that. So God revealed about them: “But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.
h
And be patient
, and your patience is not but through God.”

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, who said:
m: The entire Surah An-Nahl was revealed in Mecca, and it is Meccan, except for three verses at the end of it, which were revealed in Medina after Uhud, when Hamza was killed and mutilated. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If we are victorious over them, we will mutilate thirty men from them. When the Muslims heard that, they said: By God, if we are victorious over them, we will mutilate them in a way that no Arab has ever mutilated anyone before. Then God revealed: “
h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.”... to the end of the surah.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. The Muslims said on the day of Uhud, and he said:
h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. Up to His saying:
h
That is better for the patient
. Then he said after that:
h
And be patient
, and your patience is not but through God.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said:
m: Surat al-Nahl 16:126
h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient - it is better for the patient.

c: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: When the people of Uhud were struck with a simile, the Muslims said: If we strike them, we will surely mutilate them. So God said: “
h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.”

c: Then he resolved and informed them
m: not to mutilate, so he forbade the simile. He said: The simile of the infidels is like the slain of Uhud, except for Hanzala bin Al-Rahib. The monk Abu Amir was with Abu Sufyan, so they left Hanzala for that reason.

x: Others said: This was abrogated by His statement in Bara’ah Then kill the polytheists wherever you find them. They said: Rather, He said,
h
And if you punish

, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted as information from God to the believers that they should not initiate fighting with them until they initiate it with them, so He said (And fight in the way of God those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed. God does not like transgressors).
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And if you punish

, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted, he said: This is report from God to His Prophet that he should fight whoever fights him. He said: Then Surat al-Bara’ah was revealed, and the sacred months were over. He said: This is one of the abrogated verses.

x: Others said: Rather, God Almighty meant by His saying:
h
And be patient
, and your patience is not but through God the Prophet of God specifically, not the rest of his companions, so the command to be patient was a determination from God, not them.
Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
And if you punish

, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted, he said: God commanded them to pardon the polytheists, so some men who had power converted to Islam, and they said: O Messenger of God, if God had given us permission, we would have taken revenge on these dogs, so the Qur’an was revealed: “
h
And if you punish

, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were afflicted. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient,” and you, O Muhammad, be patient, and do not be in distress from those who take revenge, and your patience is only through God. Then He abrogated this and commanded him to fight them, so all of this was abrogated.

x: Others said: These two verses did not mean anything of what these people mentioned, but rather what they meant was that whoever is wronged by being wronged, it is not permissible for him to take from the one who wronged him more than what the wrongdoer took from him. They said: The verse is decisive and has not been abrogated.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Sirin:
m: h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished. He said: If a man takes something from you, then take the equivalent from him.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: If he takes something from you, then take the same from him. Al-Hasan said: Abd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan said: And they say: If he takes a dinar from you, then do not take from him except a dinar, and if he takes something from you, then do not take from him except the same as that thing.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And if you punish
, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished. Do not transgress.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. The correct statement in this regard is that God, the Most High, commanded whoever among the believers was punished with a punishment to punish whoever punished him with the same punishment he was punished with, if he chose his punishment, and informed him that patience in leaving his punishment, despite what he did to him, is better, and He resolved for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be patient. This is the apparent meaning of the revelation, and the interpretations that we mentioned from those who mentioned them from him, the entire verse is possible for them. If that is the case, and there is no indication in the verse of which of these is meant by it, from report or reason, then it is obligatory for us to judge by it according to a speaker who has no indication, and to say: It is a decisive verse in which God, the Most High, commanded His servants not to transgress what is due to them from others of a right of wealth or life, the right that God made for them to something else, and that it is not abrogated, since there is no indication of its abrogation, and that the statement that it is decisive has a correct and understandable face.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: And be patient, O Muhammad, over whatever harm befalls you for the sake of God. And your patience is not but through God. He says: And your patience, if you are patient, is not except through God’s help and guidance for you. And do not grieve over them. He says: And do not grieve over these polytheists who belie you and deny what you have brought them, while at the same time they have turned away from you and turned away from the advice you have brought them. And do not be distressed by what they are plotting. He says: And do not let your chest become constricted by what they say out of ignorance, and their attributing what you have brought to them to magic, poetry, or divination. Of what they are plotting: Of what they use to trick people into turning people away from the path of God and those who want to believe in you and to believe in what God has revealed to you.

The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Iraq recited it Wa la takun fi dirhyq with a fatha on the dhad in distress according to the meaning that I described in its interpretation.

Some of the reciters of the people of Medina recited it Wa la takun fi dirhyq with a kasra on the dhad. The first of the two readings that is more correct in our view is the reading of the one who reads it in distress, with the opening of the letter ḍād, because God Almighty only forbade His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from having his chest constricted by the harm he encounters from the polytheists, for conveying to them God’s revelation and sending down, so He said to him, So let not there be in your chest constriction therefrom that you may warn thereby, and He said, “Perhaps you would abandon some of what is revealed to you, and your chest would be constricted by it lest they say, ‘Why was not a treasure sent down to him or an angel brought with him? You are only a warner.’” Since that is what God Almighty forbade him, then opening the letter ḍād is the well-known expression of the Arabs in that meaning.

The Arabs say, In my chest is constricted from this, and the letter ḍād is only broken in the case of a livelihood, a narrow dwelling, and the like. If the opening of the letter ḍād occurs in the place of the opening of the letter ḍād with the breaking, it is for that which is sometimes spacious, and narrow from scarcity in one of two ways, either in the plural of constriction, as A’sha Bani Tha’labah said: If your Lord, out of His mercy, removes our distress and makes things easy for us, The other is to lighten something narrow, just as the easy is lightened by the soft, so it is said: He is easy and soft.

The first of the two readings that is more correct in our view is the reading of the one who reads it in distress, with the opening of the letter ḍād, because God Almighty only forbade His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from having his chest constricted by the harm he encounters from the polytheists, for conveying to them God’s revelation and sending down, so He said to him, So let not there be in your chest constriction therefrom that you may warn thereby, and He said, “Perhaps you would abandon some of what is revealed to you, and your chest would be constricted by it lest they say, ‘Why was not a treasure sent down to him or an angel brought with him?

x: God Almighty says, Indeed, God, O Muhammad, is with those who fear Him in His prohibitions and avoid them, and fear His punishment for them, so they refrain from advancing upon them, and those who are doers of good, meaning: He is with those who do good by observing His obligations, fulfilling His rights, and adhering to His obedience in what He has commanded them to do and what He has forbidden them to do. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: Indeed, God is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good. He said: Fear God in what He has forbidden them, and do good in what He has made obligatory upon them.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: It was mentioned to us that when death approached Haram bin Hayyan al-Abdi, it was said to him: Make a will. He said: I do not know what to make a will, but sell my armor and pay off my debt. If it does not pay off, then sell my horse. If it does not pay off, then sell my slave. I advise you to recite the last verses of Surat al-Nahl 16:“Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is [rightly] guided. And if you punish, then punish with the equivalent of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.” It was mentioned to us that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Rather, we will be patient.

notes.en: Ṣ reads “asnafṭ”; T2: “astayfaʿt”; al-Ḥilyah: “intazaʿat”; Shuʿab al-īmān: “istanfaqat”; al-Durr al-manthūr: “istafāqat.” “The believer’s soul istanqaʿat” means it gathered in his mouth, ready to depart, as water gathers in its basin. “Soul” here means spirit. Lisān al-ʿArab (root n-q-ʿ).
notes.ar: في ص: "اسنبفت"، وفى ت 2: "استيفعت"، وفى الحلية: "انتزعت"، وفى الشعب: "استنفقت"، وفى الدر المنثور: "استفاقت". واستنقعت نفس المؤمن: إذا اجتمعت في فيه تريد الخروج، كما يَسْتَنْقِع الماءُ في قراره، وأراد بالنَّفْس الرُّوح. لسان العرب (ن ق ع).

notes.en: Nazaʿa means “he cited” or “he inferred.” Al-Tāj (root n-z-ʿ) says one may “cite a verse or poem.” Of a person who infers the meaning of a verse, it is said: “He has inferred a fine meaning”; this is figurative.

Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/118, to the author, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim. Aḥmad, 13/531–532 (8220), and al-Bukhārī (4975) transmitted it through ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Maʿmar, from Hammām ibn Munabbih, from Abū Hurayrah, as a report traced to the Prophet. Al-Bukhārī (3193, 4974) transmitted it through Abū al-Zinād, from al-Aʿraj, from Abū Hurayrah, likewise traced to the Prophet.
notes.ar: أخرجه ابن أبي حاتم في تفسيره، كما في تفسير ابن كثير 4/ 491، من طريق حجاج عن ابن جريج عن عطاء وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 118 إلى المصنف وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم. كما أخرجه أحمد 13/ 531، 532 (8220)، والبخارى (4975)، من طريق عبد الرزاق عن معمر عن همام بن منبه عن أبي هريرة مرفوعًا، والبخاري في (3193، 4974) من طريق أبي الزناد عن الأعرج عن أبي هريرة مرفوعًا.

notes.en: Its source documentation was previously given at length through Maʿmar, from Qatādah.

notes.en: Ṣ is undotted; T1, T2, and F read “dakhar”; the sources documenting the report read “iddakhar,” “iddakhara,” or “dhakhar.” These mean the same thing. See al-Nihāyah, 2/155–156, and Tāj al-ʿarūs (root dh-kh-r).
notes.ar: في ص غير منقوطة، وفى ت 1، ت 2، ف: "دخر"، وفى مصادر التخريج: "ادخر" وادَّخر وذخر بمعنى، ينظر النهاية 2/ 155، 156، وتاج العروس (ذ خ ر).

notes.en: Al-Baghawī mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 5/20, and Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr, 4/491. Al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-manthūr, 4/118, to Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: ذكره البغوي في تفسيره 5/ 20، وابن كثير في تفسيره 4/ 491، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 118 إلى ابن المنذر.

notes.ar: في م: "ذكرناه".

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, T2, and F: “yuḥā,” with yāʾ. This is the reading of Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Ḥamzah. ʿĀṣim, in Ḥafṣ’s transmission, read “nūḥā,” with nūn. See al-Sabʿah, p. 373, and al-Taysīr fī al-qirāʾāt al-sabʿ, p. 106.
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "يوحى" بالياء. وهى قراءة نافع وابن كثير وأبي عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة. وقرأ عاصم في رواية حفص "نوحى "ينظر السبعة ص 373، والتيسير في القراءات السبع ص 106.

notes.en: In Ṣ, T1, T2, and F: “yuḥā.”
notes.ar: في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "يوحى".

notes.en: In M: “that is.” This reading does not yield a coherent meaning.
notes.ar: في م: "أي". ولا يتجه بها المعنى.

notes.en: Raʾaytuhu qibalan, qubulan, qabilan, qibalan, qabiliyyan, or qabilan means “face-to-face, directly, and visibly.” Lisān al-ʿArab and Tāj al-ʿarūs (root q-b-l).
notes.ar: رأيتُه قَبَلًا وقُبُلًا وقُبَلًا وقِبَلًا وقَبَليًّا وقَبِيلًا. أي مُقابَلَةً وعِيانًا. لسان العرب، وتاج العروس (ق ب ل).

notes.en: Abū Ḥayyān mentioned it in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 5/493, with the wording “the Jews. The Reminder is the Torah.”
notes.ar: ذكره أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 5/ 493، بلفظ: "اليهود. والذكر: التوراة".

notes.en: Abū Ḥayyān mentioned it in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 5/493.
notes.ar: ذكره أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 5/ 493.

notes.en: Here and below, where the verse is cited and the author comments on it, Ṣ, T1, T2, and F read “yuḥā.”
notes.ar: هنا، وفيما يأتى عند ذكر الآية ومن كلام المصنف على تفسير الآية، في ص، ت 1، ت 2، ف: "يوحى".

notes.en: Al-Ṭūsī in al-Tibyān, 6/384, and Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 5/493, gave the wording “the people of the Qurʾān”; Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 4/492.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسى في التبيان 6/ 384، وأبو حيان في البحر المحيط 5/ 493، بلفظ: "أهل القرآن"، وابن كثير في تفسيره 4/ 492.

notes.en: Abū Ḥayyān mentioned it in al-Baḥr al-muḥīṭ, 5/493, with the wording “the people of the Qurʾān”; Ibn Kathīr mentioned it in his Tafsīr, 4/492. Neither includes the following addition from the rest of the report.
notes.ar: ذكره أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 5/ 493 بلفظ: "أهل القرآن"، وابن كثير في تفسيره 4/ 492، والزيادة الآتية من بقية الأثر ليست عندهما.

notes.en: Ṣ is undotted; T1 is unclear; T2 and F read “yuḥā.”
notes.ar: في ص: "يوحى" غير منقوطة، وفى ت 1 غير واضحة، وفى ت 2، ف: "يوحى".

notes.en: See what the author will discuss here and on the following page, and Maʿānī al-Qurʾān, 2/100–101.
notes.ar: ينظر ما سيذكره المصنف هنا وفى الصفحة القادمة، ومعاني القرآن 2/ 100، 101.
